While we know of a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for the classical rank aggregation problem, the corresponding fair variant only possesses a quite straightforward 3-approximation algorithm due to Wei et al., SIGMOD'22, and Chakraborty et al., NeurIPS'22, which finds closest fair ranking for each input ranking and then simply outputs the best one.
  In this paper, we first provide a novel algorithm that achieves $(2+ε)$-approximation (for any $ε> 0$), significantly improving over the 3-approximation bound. Next, we provide a $2.881$-approximation fair rank aggregation algorithm that works irrespective of the fairness notion, given one can find a closest fair ranking, beating the 3-approximation bound. We complement our theoretical guarantee by performing extensive experiments on various real-world datasets to establish the effectiveness of our algorithm further by comparing it with the performance of state-of-the-art algorithms.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Fixed several typos in Appendix A

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Sorting by block-reversals: closing the gap
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In block-reversal sorting an elementary operation is to reverse the order of a contiguous block in a sequence, at cost proportional to the length of the block. In SODA 2004, Bender, Ge, He, Hu, Pinter, Skiena, and Swidan showed that every sequence of length $n$ can be sorted at cost $O(n\log^2{n})$ and some sequences can only be sorted at cost $Ω(n\log{n})$.
  In block-partition sorting, an elementary operation is to partition the sequence into contiguous blocks, and simultaneously reverse all blocks. The model was introduced in SODA 2024 by Jelínek, Opler, and Pekárek, who showed that every sequence can be sorted in $O(\log^2{n})$ steps and some sequences require $Ω(\log{n})$ steps.
  We close both gaps, showing that the upper bounds are tight, and the $\log^2{n}$ factors are unavoidable.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Bin Packing with Per-Bin Maximum Delay
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In online bin packing with delay, items of sizes in $(0,1]$ arrive over time and may wait before being packed into unit-capacity bins. A service selects a nonempty feasible batch of pending items and seals it in a new bin, at a service cost of one. We study the objective that adds one maximum waiting time for each sealed bin to the total service cost. Thus a bin's delay is determined by its oldest item, and younger items that fit can join it without increasing that delay. We give a randomized online algorithm with strict competitive ratio $2$ against an oblivious adversary, running in polynomial time in the ideal random-real model. It maintains one Next-Fit buffer and uses a single random silence threshold. Its analysis combines an offline-bin fragmentation bound with a two-unit saving per silence cluster. The ratio is tight for this policy; $b$ fair bits suffice for ratio $2+2^{-b}$. A fixed threshold gives deterministic ratio $1+\sqrt3$. The lower bounds $2$ and $e/(e-1)$ are attained when capacity is nonbinding. Offline, the problem minimizes the number of bins plus their total arrival span. We prove strong NP-hardness, an absolute approximation barrier of $3/2$, a deterministic polynomial $2$-approximation, and exact algorithms for several special cases. We also give stronger online ratios with exact endpoint-packing oracles and an AFPTAS for the fixed-length weighted endpoint subproblem. Finally, for Poisson arrivals of half-size items, we determine the offline and optimal causal long-run cost rates. Two natural asymptotic ratio measures coincide and have maximum $4/3$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A simple Path-based LP Relaxation for Directed Steiner Tree
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study the Directed Steiner Tree (DST) problem in layered graphs through a simple path-based linear programming relaxation. This relaxation achieves an integrality gap of O(l log k), where k is the number of terminals and l is the number of layers, which matches the best known bounds for DST previously obtained via lift-and-project hierarchies. Our formulation bypasses hierarchy machinery, offering a more transparent route to the state-of-the-art bound, and it can be exploited to provide an alternative simpler proof that O(l) rounds of the Sherali-Adams hierarchy suffice for reducing the integrality gap on layered instances of DST.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: A calculation was incorrect

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Beyond 1/3-Approximation: Random Greedy for Constrained \(\boldsymbol{k}\)-Submodular Maximization
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
\(k\)-submodularity generalizes submodularity by allowing each selected element to be assigned one of \(k\) labels. We study the maximization of a non-monotone \(k\)-submodular function, where \(k\ge2\), under matroid and knapsack constraints. We develop a proportional Top-2 randomized framework that achieves an approximation ratio of \(\sqrt2-1\approx0.4142\) under either constraint, breaking the previous \(1/3\) barrier. Once an element is selected, its label is chosen from the two labels with the largest marginal gains, with probabilities proportional to their positive parts.
  We further improve the approximation guarantees to $1/2$ under cardinality and knapsack constraints, through a Bellman-style backward induction analysis using the same proportional Top-2 rule. Our $1/2$ guarantees for cardinality and knapsack constraints are asymptotically tight as $k\to\infty$. They are also tight for $k=2$. The value-oracle complexities are \(O(Bnk)\) for cardinality, where \(B\) is the cardinality bound, \(O(n^2k)\) for matroid, and \(O(n^3k^2)\) for knapsack.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 40 pages

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: For each fixed $k$, iterative-width search finds optimal plans in polynomial time on tasks of bounded tuple-chain width, but the approximability of planning width has remained open even when an optimal plan is supplied. When all optimal plans visit the same state sequence, we characterize set and chain width as hitting numbers of competing states. We construct positive-precondition STRIPS tasks with a supplied unique optimal plan, a single reachable goal state, binary branching, and constant-size actions. Every reachable state lies on a goal-reaching execution at most one action longer than optimal, yet distinguishing width $1$ from $Θ(N)$, where $N$ is the number of atoms, is NP-hard for set, chain, and goal-admissible width. Unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm achieves a one-sided approximation factor $o(N)$ or a symmetric factor $o(\sqrt{N})$, and simple estimates attain both orders. For positive-precondition tasks with a supplied unique optimal plan of length at least two, testing set or chain width against a threshold $k\geq 1$ is coNP-complete for each fixed $k$ and $Σ_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete when $k$ is part of the input. Both results also hold for goal-admissible width if only one goal state is reachable. On an explicit state graph, a greedy algorithm approximates set width within a logarithmic factor even when optimal plans branch. Thus, knowing an optimal plan does not eliminate the difficulty of certifying substantially smaller width.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 38 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: ObliGraph: Graph Pattern Query Processing with Full and Differential Obliviousness
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Graph pattern query is a fundamental primitive in graph databases for retrieving data graphs that match a query graph under various structural constraints. As graph data is increasingly outsourced to third-party cloud servers for scalable query processing, however, both the query graph and the data graphs may leak sensitive structural information through server-side access patterns. In this paper, we study privacy-preserving graph pattern query processing in the outsourced setting, aiming to protect the structures of both the query and data graphs from access-pattern leakage. To this end, we propose $\mathsf{ObliGraph}$, the first oblivious graph search framework that supports multiple classes of graph pattern queries under two privacy modes: $\mathsf{FOS}$ achieves full obliviousness by uniformly evaluating candidate mappings, making the server-side access pattern independent of the structures of the query and data graphs; $\mathsf{DOS}$ further improves query efficiency through pruning while retaining a provable privacy guarantee of differential obliviousness. This design enables a smooth trade-off between stronger privacy and higher efficiency within a single framework. Experiments on real and synthetic datasets demonstrate that $\mathsf{ObliGraph}$ efficiently supports a range of graph pattern queries, achieving substantial improvements while preserving strong privacy guarantees.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving High-Dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In the AI era, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on vector databases is critical as it supports similarity retrieval over high-dimensional vectors, which is essential for many large language model (LLM) applications. To reduce costs and improve scalability, vector databases are often outsourced to cloud servers, raising privacy concerns for users whose query vectors contain sensitive information. In this work, we study the problem of asymmetric privacy-preserving ANN search, where the vector database is public but user queries must remain private from an untrusted cloud server. To solve this problem, we propose ObliSC, an efficient privacy-preserving search framework that protects query privacy against access-pattern leakage. ObliSC consists of (i) a search base that retrieves ANNs with a strong privacy guarantee of full obliviousness; and (ii) parallel optimization strategies that accelerate candidate retrieval and refinement while preserving full obliviousness and retrieval quality. Experiments on six standard ANN benchmarks show that ObliSC not only achieves efficiency and result quality competitive with baseline methods but also maintains a lightweight index compared with the evaluated privacy-preserving approaches.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $δ\|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $δ$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Subexponential Algorithms for Continuous Euclidean $k$-Means in Subpolylogarithmic Dimension
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{Q}^d$ and an integer $k$, the continuous Euclidean $k$-means problem asks for $k$ centers in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that minimize the sum of squared distances from the input points to their nearest centers. In one dimension, the problem can be solved in polynomial time by dynamic programming. In higher dimensions, the algorithm of Inaba, Katoh, and Imai [SoCG 1994] runs in polynomial time when both $k$ and $d$ are fixed. Mahajan, Nimbhorkar, and Varadarajan [TCS 2012] showed that the problem is NP-hard even in the plane when $k$ is part of the input, answering a question of Dasgupta [2008].
  In this paper, we give a deterministic exact algorithm for continuous Euclidean $k$-means. For arbitrary $k$ and $d=(\log n)^{o(1)}$, the algorithm runs in $O^*(2^{o(n)})$ time and uses polynomial space.
  Aman, Karthik C. S., and Punna [ESA 2024] asked whether the $2^n$ time bound for Euclidean $k$-means can be improved in high dimensions. Our result gives an affirmative answer to the corresponding question in subpolylogarithmic dimension.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 22 pages

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Busy Time Minimization with Preemption, Migration, and One Resource Requirement
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the Busy Machine Time with Preemption and Migration and One Resource Requirement problem, motivated by energy minimization in cloud data centers. Given unlimited identical-capacity machines and jobs with release times, deadlines, processing times, and resource requirements, we allow free preemption and migration at integer times and seek to minimize total machine busy time. The problem is NP-hard, and previous results consist of a 2-approximation, 2-competitive algorithm for the case of uniform heights.
  We obtain a 5671/2340 < 2.424-approximation algorithm and a 2.5-competitive online algorithm, both running in O(n^2 log n) time. Our methods are based on new non-asymptotic performance bounds for the First Fit Decreasing algorithm for Bin Packing, and a new generalization of Span Minimization, the Huge-Tiny Busy Time problem, for which we present an exact offline algorithm and an optimal (3/2)-competitive deterministic online algorithm.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Testability of Homomorphism Inadmissibility: Property Testing Meets Database Theory
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In this paper, we utilize the perspective of property testing to consider the testability of relational database queries. A primary motivation is the desire to avoid reading an entire database to decide a property thereof. We focus on conjunctive queries, which are the most basic and heavily studied database queries. Each conjunctive query can be represented as a relational structure $\mathbf{A}$ such that deciding if the conjunctive query is satisfied by a relational structure $\mathbf{B}$ is equivalent to deciding if there exists a homomorphism from $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$. We phrase our results in terms of homomorphisms.
  Precisely, we study, for each relational structure $\mathbf{A}$, the testability of homomorphism inadmissibility from $\mathbf{A}$. We consider algorithms that have oracle access to an input relational structure $\mathbf{B}$ and that distinguish, with high probability, the case where there is no homomorphism from $\mathbf{A}$ to $\mathbf{B}$, from the case where one needs to remove a constant fraction of tuples from $\mathbf{B}$ in order to suppress all such homomorphisms. We provide a complete characterization of the structures $\mathbf{A}$ from which one can test homomorphism inadmissibility with one-sided error by making a constant number of queries to $\mathbf{B}$. Our characterization shows that homomorphism inadmissibility from $\mathbf{A}$ is constant-query testable with one-sided error if and only if the core of $\mathbf{A}$ is $α$-acyclic. We also show that the injective version of the problem is constant-query testable with one-sided error if $\mathbf{A}$ is $α$-acyclic; this result generalizes existing results for testing subgraph-freeness in the general graph model.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Version of an article that appeared in PODS '19

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Revisiting Generalized Median Estimators: Exact Bitwise Computation and Gray Code Acceleration
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Generalized median estimators evaluate the median of a symmetric kernel over all $M = \binom{n}{k}$ subsets of size $k$. Exhaustive evaluation was considered impractical even for $n = 29, k = 5$ ($M = 118,755$), prompting stochastic subsampling (Wilde and Grimshaw, 2013). We show that this barrier is computational, not combinatorial: storing all subsets requires $Θ(kM)$ space, whereas stateful enumeration uses $\mathcal{O}(k)$ auxiliary state and retains only $M$ kernel values. We combine two exhaustive traversals with three-way Quickselect and a deterministic median-of-medians fallback, giving worst-case $\mathcal{O}(M)$ selection. Gosper's successor takes $\mathcal{O}(k)$ kernel work per subset for $n < w$; a Revolving Door Gray code changes one element out and one in, enabling $\mathcal{O}(1)$ kernel updates between recalibrations and $\mathcal{O}(M + kM/P)$ total time. We derive floating-point error bounds for the location ($h_1$) and mean-centered sample variance ($h_2$) kernels and their resulting median. For $n = 29, k = 5$, our ANSI C implementation evaluates all $118,755$ subsets in $0.74$ ms and $0.71$ ms, respectively. A direct C sweep places the crossover with partial lexicographic unranking at approximately $18,000$-$23,000$ subsets ($15\%$-$19\%$ of $M$), below the $32,160$-$45,420$ subsets required by Wilde and Grimshaw's sequential approximation at $ε= 0.01$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 12 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are widely used for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. Their guarantees are typically in expectation. Such guarantees alone do not ensure that covering constraints hold, limiting the applicability to problems with covering requirements.
  We prove lower-tail concentration bounds for the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and Włodarczyk (AW) under the intersection of $k$ matroid constraints. For every linear function with coefficients in $[0,1]$,the output attains nearly the fractional value divided by $k+1$ with failure probability exponentially small in this benchmark,independently of the ground-set size. We extend this bound to normalized monotone submodular functions: the fractional value is given by the multilinear extension, and the concentration bound accounts for the largest singleton value. These guarantees apply to both objectives and covering requirements. Our analysis bounds the fractional value lost in each update and applies a general gain--loss concentration theorem whose bounds are independent of the number of updates.
  We apply these bounds to obtain new approximation guarantees for matroid intersection coloring and for monotone submodular maximization under matroid, packing, and covering constraints.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Bayesian Optimal Stopping: Invincible Prophets and Achievable Philosophers
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study Bayesian optimal stopping: a hidden world $H$ is drawn from $K$ worlds according to a known prior and determines the joint distribution of $n$ observations. A decision-maker selects one observation irrevocably to maximize its value, learning about the world as observations arrive. We compare algorithms against the Bayes-optimal online policy (the philosopher) and the offline optimum (the prophet).
  Our results show that the philosopher is achievable in that we find a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation of the Bayes-optimal policy that runs in time $\mathrm{poly}(|\mathcal{I}|^{\log^* |\mathcal{I}| + 1/\varepsilon} \cdot (1/\varepsilon)^{1/\varepsilon^2})$, where $|\mathcal{I}|$ is the size of the input. By contrast, the prophet is invincible and no algorithm can obtain a competitive ratio that substantially exceeds the worst-case guarantees. When the observations are conditionally independent and identically distributed given $H$, the secretary's rule is $1/e$-competitive. We show that no algorithm can guarantee a competitive ratio better than $1/e + 1/\mathrm{poly}(K)$ and this bound is attainable.
  Our approximation scheme builds on a primal improvement subroutine connecting the two benchmarks. Given an $α$-competitive algorithm against the prophet, we construct an algorithm with a strictly better approximation factor against the philosopher. We randomize between the baseline algorithm and a threshold algorithm based on dual martingales that exploit the Bayesian structure. Each improvement yields a tighter dual martingale, enabling repeated primal-dual updates. We approximate these martingales in polynomial time using importance-weighted Monte Carlo sampling. Dual martingales also establish our upper bound on the competitive ratio and may be useful for more general Bayesian online optimization problems.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Hypercube LSH for approximate near neighbors
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A celebrated technique for finding near neighbors for the angular distance involves using a set of random hyperplanes to partition the space into hash regions [Charikar, STOC 2002]. Experiments later showed that using a set of orthogonal hyperplanes, thereby partitioning the space into the Voronoi regions induced by a hypercube, leads to even better results [Terasawa and Tanaka, WADS 2007]. However, no theoretical explanation for this improvement was ever given, and it remained unclear how the resulting hypercube hash method scales in high dimensions.
  In this work, we provide explicit asymptotics for the collision probabilities when using hypercubes to partition the space. Vectors at angle $π/3$ collide with probability $(\sqrt{3}/π)^{d + o(d)}$ in dimension $d$, compared to $(2/3)^d$ for random hyperplanes, and near-parallel vectors collide with similar asymptotic probabilities in both cases. The limiting exponential base tends continuously to zero as the angle approaches $\fracπ{2}$ from below.
  For fixed near and far angular thresholds below $π/2$, these asymptotics determine the limiting LSH collision-probability ratio $ρ$. We further describe how to use hypercube LSH in practice. A direct partial-hypercube analysis gives a heuristic lattice-sieving time bound $2^{0.3347d+o(d)}$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: v2 (Nov 2026) fixes an error in one of the branches of the main result

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Precedence Constraint Scheduling on a Fixed Number of Machines
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give a deterministic exact algorithm for $P_m\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$ for every fixed $m\ge3$. The algorithm constructs an optimum schedule in $$
  O(L)+m^{O(m^2)}\, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, {\log n} $$ elementary RAM operations, where $n \ge 2$ is the number of jobs and $L$ is the binary input length. Its word size is $O(m^2 \log n)$ bits. A direct implementation on a deterministic Turing machine with a fixed number of tapes uses $O(L)+m^{O(m^2)} \, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, \log^2 n$ steps. Thus both models have polynomial degree $94$ for three machines, apart from the displayed logarithmic factors.

Signal Processing.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
Signal Processing.summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period. Applied to an unmodified InGaAs PIN photodiode at room temperature, a 10 us waveform decoded by a neural network reconstructs spectra of one to three laser lines across the 80 nm of the telecom C+L band, locating the lines to 0.3-0.4 nm, counting them in about 99% of measurements and identifying their power levels, with line shifts tracked to tens of picometres. Because OED relies on universal semiconductor transport physics, the approach is material-agnostic and applies in principle to any off-the-shelf photodiode, turning detectors already deployed as power monitors into low-cost spectral sensors.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables

Signal Processing.title: Decision Age: Information Freshness under Fusion Rules in Multi-Sensor Command and Control
Signal Processing.summary: Command and control systems decide automatically on evidence that a fusion rule requires from several sensors. The Age of Information measures how current a datum is when it reaches the fusion node, but existing multi-source results treat additional sources as redundancy: the age at the monitor falls as sources are added. This paper addresses the opposite regime. When a rule demands corroboration the decision waits for the slowest required source, so the binding quantity is a maximum, not a minimum, of source ages. We define the decision age of an arbitrary monotone fusion rule, obtain its distribution in closed form for periodic and event-driven sources, and show that the mean decision age grows linearly with the corroboration level, from the floor of the age sawtooth to its peak. We add a dominance criterion that identifies which sensor governs decision freshness, and a measurement methodology for fielded systems. Freshness becomes a verifiable requirement, and adding sensors is shown to make automatic decisions older rather than fresher.

Signal Processing.title: Decision Fusion in Wireless Networks: A Tutorial and Survey of Classical and Learning-Based Methods
Signal Processing.summary: Decision fusion combines local decisions from distributed sensors to support reliable detection of phenomena in wireless networks. The effectiveness of decision fusion depends on sensing accuracy, reporting-channel reliability, and available communications and computation resources. This article surveys decision-fusion techniques for wireless sensor networks and emerging communication systems, bringing together their theoretical foundations and practical implementation requirements. We review network architectures and hard, soft, and quantized reporting strategies, and examine statistical, learning-based, game-theoretic, and heuristic fusion approaches. Advanced fusion techniques, including relay-aware combining, link-adaptive regeneration, branch selection, and likelihood approximations, are discussed with emphasis on their assumptions, information requirements, and limitations. The survey examines tradeoffs among detection performance, computational complexity, communications overhead, energy consumption, and latency. The tradeoffs are considered across representative sensing applications and emerging technologies, including massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication, uncrewed aerial vehicle-assisted networks, and the massive Internet of Things. The reviewed literature highlights the importance of jointly considering sensing quality, reporting reliability, and fusion processing when selecting a suitable strategy. Finally, we identify research directions in resource-aware optimization, uncertainty calibration, and robust learning-based fusion under heterogeneous data, missing reports, and changing wireless conditions. Particular attention is given to convergence, generalization, and the costs of training and inference.
Signal Processing.comment: 36 pages, 6 figures, journal

Signal Processing.title: Sensor-Free Shockable Rhythm Classification During CPR Using the Existing ECG Channel of Public-Access Automated External Defibrillators
Signal Processing.summary: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs) are public-access devices intended for use by lay rescuers, yet they must pause chest compressions to analyze the rhythm because compressions corrupt the electrocardiogram (ECG). Removing this pause requires a method that uses the hardware already present in the device, fits within its processor budget, and meets the rhythm-recognition performance required for defibrillator approval. Existing approaches rely either on an auxiliary sensor, which entails a hardware redesign, or on an additional network that reconstructs the ECG before classification. This work classifies the compression-contaminated ECG directly, using only the existing ECG channel of the AED. A cascade of three compact convolutional networks trained with different class ratios verifies each decision with a second network biased toward the proposed outcome; disagreement yields an indeterminate outcome. Evaluated on an independent manufacturer-provided cohort of 464 subjects over 15 train-validation partitions, the cascade satisfies both adjudicable American Heart Association criteria under all six noise conditions at an eight-second window and a signal-to-artifact ratio of 0 dB, with sinus-rhythm specificity of 99.20-99.43% and other non-shockable specificity of 95.48-96.20%, leaving only 1.07-1.48% of segments indeterminate. The criteria are not met at -3 dB. Single networks matched in parameter count and inference cost do not reproduce this performance. Each decision evaluates two of the three networks and requires 6.68 ms on a single thread of a general-purpose processor, and eight-bit quantization reduces the model to 1.45 MiB without changing any compliance verdict. Thus, rhythm analysis during ongoing CPR can be implemented with the ECG hardware already present in public-access AEDs, without auxiliary sensing hardware, subject to validation on the target device.

Signal Processing.title: Finite-Support Structure of Optimal i.i.d. Inputs for Finite-Memory Poisson Channels
Signal Processing.summary: Discrete-time Poisson channels with finite intersymbol interference provide a natural model for direct-detection optical links in which multipath memory and signal-dependent shot noise appear simultaneously. Under peak and average optical-intensity constraints, we study the stationary mutual-information-rate optimization under an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) input restriction. We prove that every input distribution maximizing the stationary mutual information rate within the i.i.d. input class has finite support. The proof is carried out directly on the entropy rate of the continuous-state hidden Markov output process induced by the finite-memory channel. We first establish a filtering-forgetting estimate whose constants are uniform over all admissible i.i.d. input laws. We then derive the entropy-rate first variation, construct a holomorphic extension of the corresponding influence function, and combine the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker condition with a supralinear growth argument.
Signal Processing.comment: 34 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: Chance-Constrained Joint Beam Hopping Scheduling and Bandwidth Allocation for LEO Satellites
Signal Processing.summary: Service level agreement (SLA) reliability is a key requirement in multibeam satellite systems, where operators must satisfy heterogeneous and time-varying traffic demands using limited resources. Beam hopping (BH) enables flexible resource allocation by activating only a subset of beams at each time slot. However, most existing BH optimization methods rely on predicted channel conditions and do not explicitly control the probability of SLA violation under spectral efficiency uncertainty. This work introduces an SLA-aware chance-constrained BH optimization model for joint beam scheduling and bandwidth allocation. The proposed formulation maximizes the expected delivered traffic while ensuring that each cell demand is satisfied with a target reliability level. By modelling the spectral efficiency prediction error as Gaussian, the probabilistic SLA constraints are reformulated as deterministic second-order cone constraints. Evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains the target SLA reliability under increasing traffic load and spectral efficiency uncertainty, while maintaining fairness and efficient resource allocation.

Signal Processing.title: Temporal Contrastive Alignment of EEG and Naturalistic Video Only Beats Linear Decoding On In-Sample Stimuli
Signal Processing.summary: Neural tracking, the temporal alignment between a continuous stimulus and the elicited brain response, enables decoding of attention from electroencephalography (EEG), yet its application to naturalistic video remains largely unexplored and mainly relies on linear canonical correlation analysis (CCA). We investigate whether a temporal contrastive model, pairing pretrained VideoMAE features with a lightweight EEG encoder trained on a correlation-based InfoNCE objective, can strengthen EEG-video alignment. Benchmarked against CCA under three generalization regimes, the model outperforms CCA across subjects (leave-one-subject-out), matches it within the stimulus manifold (leave-video-segment-out), and falls behind CCA when extrapolating to entirely novel videos (leave-one-video-out). Because this advantage appears only for seen stimuli, we probe its basis: a sham control shows that a high accuracy does not certify genuine alignment, as a synthesized correspondence fit to the seen stimuli can reproduce it without genuine temporal alignment in the training pairs. This does not preclude practical use: on a downstream attention-decoding task with seen stimuli, the model remains better than CCA since the decoding only requires a strong statistical coupling, regardless of whether that coupling is physiologically meaningful. Using a group-averaged EEG reference, we further show that genuine, generalizable coupling is nonetheless learned, only buried in the noise of single-subject EEG. These results indicate that progress hinges on data scale, diversity, and single-subject denoising.

Signal Processing.title: Transition Dynamics Matter: Hidden Markov Scoring of Epileptogenic Channels in SEEG
Signal Processing.summary: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) represents the most effective technique for the detection of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ) in drug-resistant epilepsy. This procedure produces a multi-dimensional signal with hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain location. In this work, we propose a joint Hidden Markov Model (HMM), in which each SEEG channel is described by a latent Markov chain, with states shared across the network and channel-specific transition probabilities. Accordingly, we develop a detection algorithm that identifies the channels belonging to the EZ by quantifying, through the Kullback-Leibler divergence, the difference between their transition probabilities in the inter-ictal period and at seizure onset. We evaluate our framework in SEEG recordings from 30 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy and compare it with a benchmark that operates in the same observation space but does not consider a latent-state structure. Compared against medically validated EZ definitions, our study shows that modeling channel-specific temporal transitions can improve EZ localization and offer a data-driven framework to investigate the latent dynamics underlying seizures.

Signal Processing.title: Reading Across Space, Time and Frequencies: Tensor Decomposition of SEEG Signals to Support Epileptogenic Zone Definition
Signal Processing.summary: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) is an invasive technique used in the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy to support the localization of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ). SEEG data are particularly complex to analyze, as they include hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain site, with interactions varying in both time and frequency. In this study, we propose a new framework for SEEG analysis, based on the Canonical Polyadic (CP) decomposition, to extract the latent modes underlying seizure generation. We model SEEG signals as a third-order tensor (channel x time x frequency), and factorize the tensor into rank-1 factors. We then exploit the channel-specific factor as an unsupervised feature set for identifying the EZ. The framework is validated on SEEG-recorded seizures from 35 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. The results show that the joint combination of multiple frequency bands significantly enhances classification performance.

Signal Processing.title: Absolute User Fairness for a Downlink Multiuser MIMO-NOMA System
Signal Processing.summary: User fairness has been widely researched in various non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems. In this paper, max-min or min-max fairness is adopted for a downlink multiuser multiple-input multiple-output NOMA system, where one multi-antenna base station (BS) transmits to multiple NOMA clusters and each cluster is composed of two single-antenna users sharing a single beam on the same time-frequency resource block. Specifically, under perfect channel state information in the transmitter (CSIT), max-min fairness is adopted to maximize the minimum achievable rate among all users. Under partial CSIT, i.e., the BS only knows the distance and channel direction information of each user, min-max fairness is adopted to minimize the maximum outage probability among all users. Under either CSIT case, to avoid solving the coupled problem, zero-forcing beamforming is designed to obtain a power control problem and then a binary search or formula based algorithm is proposed. Theoretical analyses reveal that under either CSIT case, the problem can be guaranteed to have a unique solution and the proposed algorithm is computationally efficient due to only simple closed-form expressions involved.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: SEP Analysis of Fluid Antenna GSC Reception under Correlated Nakagami-m Fading and Imperfect Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Channel estimation (CE) errors and correlation among the fading channels are two of the most fundamental factors degrading the performance of any multi-antenna system. This paper aims to analytically capture their joint effect on fluid antenna systems (FASs) performing generalized selection combining (GSC), i.e., combining the received signals at the best $\tilde{L}$ of the $L$ available ports using maximum ratio combining (MRC). More specifically, the FAS receiver is subject to arbitrarily correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading channels following the fully correlated Jakes' model, and employs a pilot-aided maximum-likelihood rule for CE prior to data detection. A novel tight moment-matching-based Gamma approximation is proposed for the marginal distribution of the estimated channel gains, which is then used to derive the joint statistics of the estimated correlated channels for the case of non-identical integer or half-integer fading severity parameters. Considering that the transmitter employs $M$-ary phase-shift keying or quadrature amplitude modulation, the joint statistics are further exploited to obtain exact finite-integral symbol error probability (SEP) expressions for a GSC-based FAS receiver, along with closed-form counterparts for the case of identical fading parameters. In addition, asymptotic SEP expressions at high signal-to-noise ratio are derived, analytically establishing that non-ideal CE and fading correlation degrade only the FAS's coding gain, while the diversity order is preserved and governed solely by the number of combined ports and the estimated fading severity. The presented numerical SEP investigations offer concrete design insights into the trade-offs between CE quality, fading correlation, and port selection for the GSC-based FAS receiver.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures

Signal Processing.title: Tensor-Based Dynamic Channel Estimation for mmWave Movable Antenna MIMO Systems
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates the dynamic channel estimation algorithm in mmWave movable antenna (MA) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To achieve highly accurate channel estimation, we propose a tensor decomposition-based channel estimation algorithm. First, by leveraging the path response model and utilizing the intrinsic sparsity of mmWave channels, the channel corresponding to MA pairs at the base station and mobile station is transformed into a superposition of channels from sparse paths. Next, the received signal is constructed as a fourth-order tensor to fully capture the high-dimensional structural information of the MA MIMO channel. Then, two tensor decomposition schemes are adopted to extract the factor matrices, and our analysis reveals that the uniqueness of the decomposition can be guaranteed in our model. Subsequently, the propagation loss, frequency offset, angle of arrival/departure, and time delay are obtained based on these factor matrices and the channel matrix can be rebuilt. Additionally, Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is also derived as a performance evaluation standard, proving that the proposed algorithm achieves a higher estimation accuracy and nearly approaches this minimum bound. Moreover, normalized mean square error (NMSE) is selected as the evaluation metric for estimation accuracy. Finally, simulation results reveal a notable reduction in the estimation error of the proposed algorithm when compared to the baseline algorithms, confirming its estimation advantage.

Signal Processing.title: Channel-Aware Codebook Design for Task-Oriented Token Communication Over Wireless Networks
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates the adaptive codebook design for task-oriented token communication over wireless networks with dynamic channels. This paper proposes the channel-aware codebook (CAC), a joint channel- and reconstruction-driven framework that reorders the labels of a frozen 14-bit VQGAN codebook. In the considered framework, a balanced geometric partition forms prefix groups, a prefix bijection places the groups on the label hypercube, and bijective suffix assignments place the codewords within each group. The problem is formulated to minimize the expected full-image perceptual distortion of the frozen decoder under a binary symmetric channel, averaged over a design set of bit error rates (BERs) and retaining simultaneous token errors. An offline algorithm alternates prefix and suffix exchanges and screens and confirms candidates on paired batches under a fixed decoder-evaluation budget. The assignment preserves the error-free reconstruction and the payload and deploys as static lookup tables without retraining. Under the binary symmetric channel at BER $0.01$, it reduces LPIPS by $12.3\%$ and improves COCO AP by $14.1\%$ ($1.72$ points) relative to the native labels, and it lowers LPIPS by a further $4.5\%$ relative to a related assignment adaptation at the same payload.

Signal Processing.title: Detecting Formation-Preserving GNSS Spoofing of UAV Swarms through Transmitter Parallax in Pseudorange and Doppler
Signal Processing.summary: Swarms of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) detect Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing by checking the drones' reported positions against their known formation. Formation-preserving spoofing evades this check: in GNSS-WASP, one transmitter per satellite, a few kilometres away, shifts the whole swarm while keeping its formation. We show that such an attack still leaves a trace below the position level. Because the transmitters are close, each drone sees them under a slightly different angle, and this parallax bends the signal arrival times across a 90 m swarm by 20-40 cm for a transmitter at 5 km, whatever delays the attacker applies. We propose a likelihood ratio test that reads this trace from the pseudoranges and Doppler every drone already measures, with all clocks and attacker delays unknown and no extra antennas. In simulations with real GPS and Galileo orbits and white receiver noise, 16 drones detect GNSS-WASP at 5 km in 13-60% of 10 s windows in straight flight and in every window during a formation turn with a precise Doppler receiver, where the countermeasure proposed with GNSS-WASP detects at most 5%. The same test also catches single-transmitter and ground-array spoofing.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 7 main figures, 7 main tables. Includes supplementary appendices

Signal Processing.title: Blind tests of a simple-body model of submarine target strength on open benchmarks
Signal Processing.summary: Finite-element and boundary-element models of a submarine's sonar echo need a mesh and a solver, and their cost grows quickly with frequency. SSR-Sim takes an analytical route. The hull is cut into a few simple bodies, the echo of each is a closed-form result of geometrical acoustics or of the Kirchhoff approximation, the surface enters through a plane-wave reflection coefficient, and the echoes add in energy. This paper describes the method, including the reduction of a hull and its sail to simple bodies, and tests it on three open cases. (1) The reflection coefficient of a 50 mm rubber tile on steel plating, computed with finite elements by Yang et al., is reproduced to 0.02 rms or better at incidence angles from 0° to 75° once the layer is allowed to refract. (2) For the rigid full-scale BeTSSi submarine at 1 kHz, a prediction fixed before the reference was opened agrees with the boundary-element results of Venås and Kvamsdal to within 0.7 dB in every aspect sector from the bow to 150°; in the stern sector it is 5 dB high. (3) For a 1:15 BeTSSi model with 10 mm tiles measured in a lake, a second blind prediction is within -3.1, +1.4 and -0.5 dB of the measured level over aspects 0-120° at 5, 15 and 20 kHz, against -3.1, +3.1 and +3.5 dB for the Kirchhoff-finite-element computation published with the measurement. At 10 kHz, on a resonance of the tile, the prediction is 6.9 dB low, and in the bow sector it is 7 dB or more low at every frequency. The tests cover the specular component and the coating model only. The failures show what such a model lacks: edge diffraction and the returns that set the off-beam floor of a real model.
Signal Processing.comment: 17 pages, 6 figures, 9 tables, Data: https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/11704

Signal Processing.title: Feedback-Free FDD Cell-Free Massive MIMO With Sparse AP Activation and Dual-Mode Precoding
Signal Processing.summary: This correspondence enables practical frequency-division duplex (FDD) operation in cell-free massive MIMO via two mechanisms. Sparse access-point (AP) activation reduces downlink pilot overhead to enable coherent detection, while angle-reciprocity precoding steers beams using only uplink-estimated angles, eliminating channel feedback entirely. A load-adaptive dual-mode optimizer further enhances performance: closed-form signal-to-leakage-and-noise-ratio precoding for high-load rate boosting, or semidefinite relaxation for low-load power minimization. Simulations verify its superiority over existing feedback-free FDD solutions in spectral and energy efficiency, and its robustness to angle errors, reciprocity mismatch, and multipath.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology

Signal Processing.title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
Signal Processing.summary: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training. To encourage cooperation without inter-device communication, a shared global reward aligned with system cost is employed. Extensive simulations demonstrate rapid convergence and significant improvement in overall system cost compared with baselines, e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN).
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026

Signal Processing.title: Massive MIMO-OFDM ISAC for Sparse ISAR Imaging: Joint Power and Subcarrier Allocation
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates a massive multiple-input multiple-output (mMIMO) orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) framework for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging. A dual-function architecture combines communication precoding and dedicated sensing beamforming to support simultaneous downlink communication and ISAR imaging. To address incomplete measurements arising from intermittent pilot transmission and sparse sensing-subcarrier activation, an adaptive reweighted two-dimensional alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is developed for sparse ISAR reconstruction. A joint resource-allocation framework is formulated to optimize communication-subcarrier assignment, sensing-subcarrier selection, and transmit power allocation under communication quality-of-service (QoS) and sensing constraints. Exploiting channel hardening, analytical full-band benchmarks based on statistical channel state information (CSI) are derived for maximum-ratio (MR) and zero-forcing (ZF) precoding, while a soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm is developed for sparse-sensing resource allocation. Numerical results demonstrate that the adaptive ADMM algorithm improves ISAR reconstruction accuracy over conventional methods, while the SAC-based design achieves higher sum spectral efficiency than both the analytical full-band ISAC benchmarks and the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) baseline under both MR and ZF precoding, while satisfying the communication QoS and sensing constraints.

Signal Processing.title: Robust SAC-Enabled UAV-RIS Assisted Secure MISO Systems With Untrusted EH Receivers
Signal Processing.summary: Secure downlink transmission in UAV-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multi-user multiple-input single-output (MISO) networks is challenged by imperfect channel state information (CSI), internal eavesdropping by untrusted energy-harvesting receivers (UEHRs), discrete RIS phase shifts, and nonlinear energy harvesting (EH). This paper jointly optimizes the UAV hovering position, base station (BS) transmit power allocation, and discrete RIS phase shifts to maximize the worst-case secrecy energy efficiency (WCSEE) under bounded CSI uncertainty and nonlinear EH constraints. The resulting problem is a highly non-convex mixed-integer fractional optimization problem with tightly coupled spatial, power, and RIS variables. To address these challenges, we develop two complementary solution frameworks. First, for perfect CSI and continuous RIS phase shifts, we derive an analytical benchmark based on block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Second, for the general robust setting with discrete phase quantization and CSI uncertainty, we propose a customized soft actor-critic (SAC) framework that incorporates continuous-to-discrete action projection, twin critics to mitigate value overestimation, and a feasibility-aware reward mechanism. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed SAC policy achieves up to $28\%$, $16\%$, and $6\%$ higher WCSEE than the SCA benchmark, DDPG, and TD3, respectively, while exhibiting faster convergence and maintaining stable performance across varying user densities, UEHR counts, and CSI uncertainty levels.

Signal Processing.title: DISC: A Deterministic Instantaneous-SINR Combiner for Uplink Massive MIMO Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Future Massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) systems will fit more antennas into compact arrays, making minimum mean-square-error (MMSE) combining computationally demanding. Maximum-ratio (MR) combining serves as a cheaper alternative but performs poorly in multi-user scenarios. Existing solutions to this either mimic the MMSE combiner using second-order statistics or, as in the optimal bilinear equalizer (OBE), rely on the loose use-and-then-forget (UaTF) bound. In this paper, we propose DISC, a novel receive combiner that instead maximizes a deterministic approximation of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), obtained by replacing the random terms in the SINR with deterministic equivalents. This approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the number of antennas grows, and it exploits useful information discarded by the UaTF bound. The computational complexity of DISC matches that of OBE, with the low-complexity variant DISC-D being even cheaper than conventional MR combining. We further prove that the SINR achieved by DISC grows unbounded with the number of antennas, even under pilot contamination, similarly to MMSE combining. Finally, we numerically demonstrate that DISC achieves a sum spectral efficiency close to that of MMSE combining under full pilot sharing, while outperforming other combiners across signal-to-noise ratio, pilot length, and spatial correlation models.

Signal Processing.title: A Generative AI-Enhanced Digital Twin Framework for Proactive Interference Management in Hybrid Near/Far-Field Wireless Systems
Signal Processing.summary: The applications of Digital Twins (DTs) and Generative AI (GenAI) have demonstrated significant potential for modeling and learning-based wireless communications. However, their joint potential for proactive wireless system design remains largely underexplored, particularly in extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) networks characterized by hybrid near-field (NF) and far-field (FF) propagation. In this work, we propose an integrated GenAI-enhanced DT framework for proactive interference management in dynamic indoor environments. The DT constructs a site-specific virtual replica of the deployment, enabling geometry-aware modeling of blockage and hybrid NF/FF propagation. Conditioned on the DT environment and historical network states, GenAI generates multiple plausible future channel and blockage realizations, which are incorporated into regime-aware proactive beamforming. Extensive Sionna ray-tracing simulations across open and cluttered indoor environments, including different user equipment (UE) speeds, demonstrate improved interference suppression, signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), and prediction accuracy compared with reactive and deterministic DT-based benchmarks.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 6 Tables

Signal Processing.title: Modeling and Link Budget Feasibility Analysis of Secure LoRa-Based Peer-to-Peer Communication for Short-Range Tactical Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Short-range reliable and secure communication is a major priority in the tactical, military and disaster response settings where the traditional communication infrastructure is either off-line or prone to interception. Current VHF/UHF radios and software-defined radios are popular but large-sized devices and require lots of power, making them not suitable to be used as lightweight wearable devices with seamless hand-free use. In this paper, the design and theoretical framework of a miniature, LoRa based encrypted intercommunication device that can be used in secure field communication over a range of 1-1.5km and under line-of-sight conditions is provided. The suggested system consists of a voice-activated acquisition block, digital audio compression, an embedded microcontroller processor, and AES-128 encryption followed by a low-power transmission via the LoRa protocol. Through the ability of chirp spread spectrum modulation to utilize the long-range and low-energy properties, the system is guaranteed reliable communications coupled with low power consumption and low electromagnetic footprint. The theoretical analysis of the proposed communication range is justified using a link-budget that justifies the practicability of the communication range in the real propagation conditions. This architecture focuses on infrastructural agnosticism, peer-to-peer security as well as wearable ergonomics. The given scheme shows the possibilities of LoRa technology in the scope of other traditional IoT telemetry, and it can be further extended to include secure tactical voice communication platforms.

Signal Processing.title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition
Signal Processing.summary: Cross-environment deployment is the central obstacle to practical WiFi sensing: a pipeline reaching 0.89+ top-1 in its training environments collapses to 0.408 under Leave-One-Domain-Out (LODO) evaluation with only K-shot labels. A ceiling analysis shows the collapse is not an alignment problem: the action signal is strong across seen environments (about 0.89 K10), environment identity is decodable from the encoder (0.965), and the failure concentrates in the encoder's extrapolation to the novel environment. A pre-registered falsification chain confirms that "align the domains" methods--training-time alignment, readout-level prototype alignment, adversarial confusion, and covariance/subspace alignment (CORAL -3.8pp, subspace -8.3pp)--degrade performance, and that source-domain statistics anti-correlate with cross-environment contribution. The effective levers lie elsewhere; we combine them into Dec-H: (i) closed-form source within-class whitening, provably re-geometrizing the readout's L2 regularization (+8.6pp, zero cost); (ii) profile-mixing augmentation (+1.0pp); (iii) few-shot adaptation with alternating whitening refit (+1.5pp; fixed preconditioners are 20/20 negative); (iv) heterogeneous decision ensembles (+1.7pp); homogeneous scaling and source-weighted stacking are saturated or harmful. Dec-H reaches 0.560 K10 (0.812 K40), +15.2pp over the baseline, consistent across all four environments and seeds; all thirteen configurations were pre-registered with frozen criteria.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Preprint of a manuscript submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

Signal Processing.title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
Signal Processing.summary: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for presentation at IEEE CloudNet 2026

Signal Processing.title: Signed Powers-of-Two Greedy Vector Approximation of Zadoff-Chu Sequences
Signal Processing.summary: This paper explores the use of sums of signed powers-of-two (SOPOT) for a representation suitable for multiplierless applications of ZC sequences, where multiplications are reduced to a prescribed number of shift-and-add operations. The SOPOT representation is achieved using a greedy algorithm that outperforms other approaches for multiplierless approximations, such as CORDIC and CSD. The proposed algorithm is based on the matching pursuits using generalized bit planes (MPGBP), and the proposed modification enables robustness to hyperparameter tuning. The resulting sequences retain, to some extent, the good autocorrelation properties of ZC, as shown in a matched-filter detection simulation. This corroborates to their use in various practical applications across mainstream cellular systems and devices requiring moderate computational cost.

Signal Processing.title: A Continuous Payload-Bearing Discrete Multitone Modulation Framework for Fiber-Optic Integrated Sensing and Communication
Signal Processing.summary: A key challenge in fiber-optic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is to make the payload-bearing waveform itself serve both functions without a separate sensing waveform or sensing-only silent interval. We propose a continuous discrete multitone (DMT) framework with two waveform modes, in which the same payload-bearing waveform supports forward intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) communication and backward distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). A unified phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (φ-OTDR) model represents distributed Rayleigh backscattering as a finite-memory sensing multipath channel. It shows that conventional pulse-and-wait φ-OTDR requires a round-trip-time-scale silent interval to isolate successive returns, while nonzero off-peak samples in practical matched-filter (MF) pulse compression cause spatial intersymbol interference (ISI). Continuous DMT instead retains superposed returns and separates range-cell contributions through known-waveform channel reconstruction. Cyclic-prefix DMT (CP-DMT) uses a full-memory CP and one-tap frequency-domain equalization (FDE); under sufficient-CP and ideal full-bin inversion conditions, it eliminates MF-correlation-induced spatial ISI. Cyclic-prefix-free DMT (NoCP-DMT) applies regularized least squares (LS) to the long-memory linear convolution, avoiding the CP at higher receiver complexity. Experiments over a 10-km fiber link localize a 600-Hz disturbance applied by a piezoelectric transducer (PZT) near 5.071 km and recover gauge-differential phase with correlations of 0.989 and 0.987 for CP-DMT and NoCP-DMT, respectively. At 2- and 1-V PZT drive levels, the ten-record localization standard deviations are 0.16/0.11 m and 0.18/0.38 m, respectively. The corresponding IM/DD error vector magnitude values range from 4.80% to 5.00%, with no bit errors observed.
Signal Processing.comment: This manuscript has been submitted for consideration for publication

Signal Processing.title: Self-Supervised Operator Learning for Channel Estimation in Fluid Antenna Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communications through adaptive antenna repositioning. Recently, Fourier neural operators (FNOs) have shown strong potential for FAS channel estimation owing to their ability to learn resolution-invariant mappings and generalize across different port densities. However, existing operator learning approaches require densely sampled channel realizations as training labels, whereas a practical receiver only collects noisy pilot observations from a small subset of ports. This mismatch between training requirements and practical channel acquisition poses a major obstacle to deployment. To address this challenge, we develop a self-supervised framework that trains the FNO-based estimator directly from noisy sub-sampled pilots without any labeled channel fields. The proposed objective combines a pilot splitting strategy, which creates supervision at ports hidden from the model input, with a correction based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE) that eliminates the measurement noise bias. We prove that this objective admits the same minimum mean square error (MMSE) solution as the ideal supervised criterion. Since the loss relies solely on received pilots, the estimator can be continually adapted online on the live pilot stream. Simulation results show that the self-supervised FNO achieves accuracy comparable to supervised training, generalizes zero-shot to unseen port resolutions, and rapidly recovers from distribution shift via online adaptation.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to an IEEE conference

Signal Processing.title: A closed-loop agentic research environment for MRI development within Siemens IDEA platform
Signal Processing.summary: Motivation: Testing new ideas in MRI can require substantial effort to learn sequence programming and reconstruction tools and to debug implementations before the scientific question can be addressed. Goals: Reduce the implementation and debugging burden of testing MRI ideas while retaining researcher control of scientific decisions. Approach: We developed an environment where LLM agents develop sequences in the native Siemens IDEA platform, evaluate them through Bloch simulation and reconstruction, and further iteratively refine them using scanner feedback. Results: As test cases, the agentic environment was used to implement and validate a GIRF-based gradient-calibration sequence and reconstruction in approximately 4 hours, and to develop and optimize a rapid 3-second multichannel calibration scan in approximately 12 hours of researcher-guided iteration.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to ISMRM 2027

Signal Processing.title: Lightweight Low-Frequency Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring via Karhunen-Loève Feature Distillation and Temporal Convolutional Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical enabler for demand-side management which allows for smart grid optimization. A deployment-ready NILM solution necessitates three key features: accurate disaggregation, low-frequency sampling, and low computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight, edge-oriented NILM framework that combines activity-boundary-aware synthetic data augmentation with Karhunen-Loève Transform (KLT) feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The augmentation stage extracts and recombines complete or near-complete appliance activation segments so that the model can be trained without new fully labeled household aggregates. The KLT filter bank extracts decorrelated, appliance-informed temporal features which are then fed into a compact TCN along with the original aggregate for energy disaggregation. Evaluations on two standard NILM datasets, UK-DALE and REDD, at 10-s sampling and with leave-one-house-out testing, demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior disaggregation accuracy relative to NILMFormer, BERT4NILM, BiLSTM, and BiGRU. The computational footprint of the framework is 31,009 parameters, the fewest of the five models compared, and on a single CPU thread it needs 2.78 ms per 1000 samples, 84-95% less than the baselines. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for low-frequency smart-meter NILM.
Signal Processing.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid. S. Peeris, P. Thennakoon and P. Sumanasekara contributed equally

Signal Processing.title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
Signal Processing.summary: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.
Signal Processing.comment: 20 pages, 3 figures

Signal Processing.title: An LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for CKM-Assisted Network Deployment Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) offer reusable, site-specific radio priors to facilitate environment-aware network planning. However, deploying heterogeneous network nodes to meet diverse performance requirements in complex environments is challenging and requires executable workflows that coordinate scene preparation, candidate-site specification, CKM construction, optimization, and validation. This paper presents a large language model (LLM)-orchestrated agent framework for CKM-assisted network deployment optimization, where an LLM translates high-level requirements into modular, typed, and reproducible planning workflows. In this framework, an LLM layer interprets intent, selects modules, and populates normalized configurations; physics-grounded modules generate scene, CKM, optimization, and validation artifacts; and a deterministic guarded controller performs validation-guided refinement. A common target-candidate-CKM-optimizer interface supports the registration and composition of compatible planning modules, with CKM backends, samplers, and solvers remaining replaceable. We instantiate the proposed framework for base station (BS) deployment, intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) deployment, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory planning. An urban-block case study demonstrates automatic scene consistency checks, bounded BS/IRS deployment refinement, and collision- and radio-feasible UAV planning.
Signal Processing.comment: In Proc. IEEE ICCC 2026

Signal Processing.title: 20 ghz longitudinal surface acoustic wave resonators in 100-nm x-cut lithium niobate on silicon carbide
Signal Processing.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($λ$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $λ$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $λ= 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $λ= 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $λ\geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/λ\leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/λ$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

Signal Processing.title: Learning MMSE Filters for OFDM Channel Estimation: Attention Transformer Gains at Linear Inference
Signal Processing.summary: In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), accurate channel estimation is crucial. Classical signal processing-based approaches, such as linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) estimation, often require second-order statistics that are difficult to obtain in practice. Recent deep neural network (DNN)-based methods have been introduced to address this, but they often suffer from high inference complexity. This paper proposes an Attention-aided MMSE (A-MMSE), a model-based DNN framework that learns the linear MMSE filter via the Attention Transformer. Once trained, the A-MMSE performs channel estimation through a single linear operation, eliminating nonlinear activations during inference and thus reducing computational complexity. To improve the learning efficiency of the A-MMSE, we develop a two-stage Attention encoder that captures the frequency and temporal correlation structure of OFDM channels. We also introduce a rank-adaptive extension that adjusts the filter rank at deployment time, enabling efficient operation under resource-constrained receivers. Numerical simulations show that A-MMSE consistently outperforms baseline methods across a wide range of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. In particular, the A-MMSE and its rank-adaptive extension provide an improved performance-complexity trade-off.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: WiFo-D: Wireless Foundation Model Based on Discrete Representations
Signal Processing.summary: Wireless foundation models have shown strong generalization capabilities across heterogeneous wireless tasks and configurations. However, most existing models rely on continuous representations, limiting ultra-low-overhead channel state information (CSI) feedback, few-shot generalization, and robustness to noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a wireless foundation model based on discrete representations (WiFo-D), which learns multi-granularity discrete CSI representations. It comprises a CSI encoder, multi-codebook vector quantization, and a modulation-based decoder, with the learned token maps and quantized features supporting multi-rate CSI feedback, CSI reconstruction, and diverse CSI-related downstream tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong CSI feedback performance at an ultra-low latent compression ratio of 1/32 with 3 bits per token, reducing normalized mean square error (NMSE) by more than 4.7 dB compared with the strongest baseline. Furthermore, for frequency-domain prediction with limited training samples, WiFo-D improves generalization and noise robustness over continuous-representation-based methods. The results also demonstrate its superiority across downstream tasks, including beam prediction, wireless localization, and line-of-sight/non-line-of-sight identification.

Signal Processing.title: Distributed Fiber Monitoring on a Coherent DSP ASIC: Implementation of Longitudinal Power Monitoring
Signal Processing.summary: Coherent DSP ASICs and transceivers to date report a rich set of optical link metrics, yet these remain cumulative over the link and provide no spatial localization. This paper presents the implementation design of fiber-longitudinal power monitoring (LPM), which recovers spatially resolved power profiles from received traffic, on a coherent DSP ASIC chip. We first identify the challenges specific to DSP implementation, and describe the enabling algorithm and architecture. We then present the key design considerations for retaining the estimation fidelity of the on-chip LPM during in-service operation. On this basis, we implement LPM on a coherent DSP, a 3-nm 800G low-power DSP ASIC housed in an OSFP pluggable module, which constitutes, to our knowledge, the first coherent DSP ASIC and transceiver to perform distributed fiber monitoring and data communication simultaneously. The on-chip LPM is experimentally validated over links of up to 1005 km using 400ZR+ and 800ZR+ traffic, with no measurable impact on Q factor or module power consumption. Multi-vendor interoperability is also demonstrated, where the on-chip LPM operates on signals transmitted by third-party transceivers. These results extend coherent DSPs from cumulative to spatially resolved monitoring, allowing pluggable transceivers, deployable from DCI to long-haul, to act not only as cost-efficient transmission elements but also as distributed monitoring points across diverse optical network infrastructure.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 19 figures

Signal Processing.title: A Deep Zero-Inflated Model of North Atlantic Right Whale Presence To Support Blue Economy Management
Signal Processing.summary: Effective modeling of endangered marine mammal species, such as the North Atlantic Right Whale, is critical for balancing marine conservation with the growing blue economy. Passive acoustic monitoring data collected by autonomous underwater vehicles provide new opportunities for localized marine species detection and oceanographic sensing, but introduce complex statistical challenges such as zero inflation, imperfect detection, and intricate dependence structures. In response, we propose the Deep Zero-Inflated Bernoulli (DeepZIB) model, a deep statistical method which jointly models latent species presence and conditional detection probabilities while learning complex habitat relationships from heterogeneous covariate information. We establish theoretical results on the model's structural properties and conduct simulation experiments to demonstrate its ability to recover underlying parameters and latent presence fields. Application to real-world passive acoustic monitoring data on the North Atlantic Right Whale along the U.S. East Coast demonstrates improved model adequacy and predictive performance in capturing the species' dynamic and spatially varying habitat.
