To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy, while textual image descriptions do not consistently help and may degrade performance. These findings suggest that reasoning is important for stable visual mathematical judgement, whereas description-based intermediates require more careful design.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: A Vision-Based Framework for Manual Assembly Verification and Adaptive Operator Assistance
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Manual assembly remains difficult to monitor because operator actions, components, and task progress must be interpreted together. This paper presents a modular framework based on a single overhead red-green-blue (RGB) camera, combining object detection, hand-motion tracking, region-aware interaction detection, finite-state verification, task-specific pose classification, and configurable visual guidance. The system was evaluated during pneumatic-piston assembly and disassembly with eight participants under three assistance conditions: full, mid, and no guidance. Mixed-effects analysis identified an association between assistance condition and a composite measure of motion quality, with lower estimated scores under mid and no guidance relative to full guidance. However, the condition-by-trial interaction was not statistically significant, and the estimated differences in learning trajectories remain descriptive. No condition differences were detected in completion time or failed-stage counts. The study demonstrates the integration of visual perception, procedural verification, and configurable operator feedback in a single-camera workflow. Selecting assistance according to operator expertise remains a design objective for future investigation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two RGB frames. Alongside LARYBench classification and regression, we measure how much wrist motion a frozen code retains and how strongly it responds to a synthetic view or lighting change. EgoLAM has the highest hand-motion decoding score among eight evaluated models. Across three LIBERO suites, policies pretrained on its codes and fine-tuned on expert demonstrations achieve 79.38% mean success, 28.73 points above expert behavior cloning and 9.76 points above the strongest other latent action model in each suite on average.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Any3R: Feedforward 3D Reconstruction from Any Camera Type
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Geometry foundation models recover camera poses and dense scene geometry from multiple images using feed-forward networks, but are typically designed for pinhole cameras. This assumption is embedded in the backbone itself: positional encoding locates each patch by its pixel index and the training loss weights every pixel equally, so both treat image coordinates as if they fixed the viewing direction in 3D space, which holds only for pinhole cameras. We condition both on the dense ray field, which maps each pixel to its 3D viewing direction and represents any central camera regardless of its projection model. $\textit{Angular coordinates}$ use the viewing direction of each patch for positional encoding, and $\textit{solid-angle weighting}$ scales the point loss by the angular area covered by each pixel. Together, they allow the same encoding and supervision to be used across different camera models. $\textbf{Any3R}$ is therefore a feed-forward model that reconstructs from any mix of central cameras without lens-specific retraining. On a benchmark of eight central cameras across three datasets, where every method reconstructs with its own predicted camera poses, it is the most consistently accurate method. $\textbf{Any3R}$ enables 3D reconstruction from crowdsourced and archival image collections containing diverse camera types. Project page: https://jingong-chen.github.io/Any3R/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. We introduce InterBand-EMG, which combines band-specific quantization with cross-band reconstruction and structured masked code prediction to learn transferable EMG representations for hand-pose tracking. We also introduce SynapMyo, an eight-channel EMG-to-pose dataset comprising 1,227.74 hand-hours from 499 users across 68 movement categories. Experiments on emg2pose and SynapMyo show that InterBand-EMG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in joint-angle accuracy across all three generalization settings on both datasets. The source code and the SynapMyo dataset will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Preserving Pretrained CFG Structure in RL for Diffusion Models with Conditional Contrast Regularization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become an important component in the post-training of diffusion models. In practice, however, standard RL often improves the target reward without reliably preserving holistic generation quality, leading to unstable reward-quality trade-offs that we view as a form of reward hacking. Since Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is known to improve visual clarity, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality in generation, we investigate whether its underlying structure can serve as a useful prior during RL. We present a unified geometric view that interprets both CFG and RL as correction vectors in a common prediction space, and identify the projection of the RL-induced correction onto the pretrained CFG correction as a useful diagnostic of quality-related structural preservation. Geometric analysis and rotation intervention further show that the pretrained CFG direction carries information useful for generation quality that reward-driven RL updates do not necessarily preserve. Based on this insight, we propose Conditional Contrast Regularization (CCR), which uses the frozen reference model's conditional contrast as a local structural prior during RL. Experiments across multiple reward settings and backbones show that CCR more consistently preserves generation quality while maintaining competitive reward, yielding a better reward-quality trade-off than standard RL and generic regularization methods.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SIR-Agent: Skill-Augmented Image Restoration Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Agents for Image Restoration (IR) aim to leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to autonomously perceive image degradation and invoke IR tools. However, existing IR agents typically rely on fine-tuning MLLM parameters to adapt to new IR tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting of IR knowledge. To address this limitation, we propose a skill-augmented IR agent, dubbed SIR-Agent, that maintains IR knowledge in a scalable skill library and uses Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) to facilitate efficient skill-library evolution. Specifically, we design a Chain Feedback-driven Skill Revision (CFSR) to evolve the skill library. The CFSR analyzes restoration chains to identify and revise weak operations in existing skills. The compatibility of a revised skill with known tasks decides if it replaces the original skill or is appended independently. Furthermore, to advance CFSR's skill-library evolution, we present an RSI-driven skill meta-learning mechanism, which identifies CFSR's inefficient operations and autonomously refines its revision strategy. Extensive experiments across 14 IR benchmarks, covering 6 single-degradation and 8 mixed-degradation scenarios, demonstrate SIR-Agent's superior IR performance. Further evaluation on 7 unseen tasks validates SIR-Agent's generalization to new IR tasks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: GAAFormer: Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer for Joint Point Cloud Denoising and Upsampling
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Point cloud denoising and upsampling require samples that accurately recover the underlying surface from noisy or sparse observations. A central challenge in both tasks is preserving surface coverage while refining point locations. We introduce GAAFormer (Geometry-Anchored Attention Transformer), a unified generative octree transformer that performs both tasks with a shared network. Its decoder anchors attention neighborhoods to geometry, providing spatial context for occupancy prediction and point generation. Fixed voxel windows and alternating shifts preserve the grouping of surviving nodes as the output tree changes. The design retains the encoder, positional encoding, prediction heads, and parameter count of a serialized-attention backbone. We establish a deletion-consistency property of the neighborhood rule and evaluate both tasks using the same model. On PUNet, GAAFormer achieves a mean Chamfer distance (CD) of $6.0643\times10^{-5}$, reducing CD and Hausdorff distance by 3.35% and 19.34%, respectively, relative to the serialized backbone. For upsampling, it achieves CD values of $0.8475$, $1.7057$, and $1.0147$ ($\times10^{-5}$) on PU-GAN, PU1K, and Sketchfab, respectively, with improvements in CD, Hausdorff distance, and point-to-surface distance over the same backbone on PU-GAN and Sketchfab. These results establish a single architecture for point cloud denoising and upsampling. Within the shared encoder-decoder, the same geometry-anchored attention module improves both noise removal and dense point generation without task-specific redesign or additional parameters.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MODULE: A Mutual-Promoting Deep Unfolding Framework Towards Degradation-Robust Multi-modal Image Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multi-modal image fusion is crucial for comprehensive scene representation, yet real-world degradations compromise its efficacy, necessitating degradation-robust fusion paradigms. Existing degradation-robust multi-modal image fusion methods are often hindered by cascaded sub-optimal solution or black-box opacity. To address these challenges, we propose a theory-inspired mutual-promoting deep unfolding framework. It reformulates degradation-robust image fusion as a joint optimization problem, utilizing the degradation model and modality generation mechanism to explicitly model both single-task priors and cross-task dependencies. By decomposing the complex multi-task optimization problem into task-related iterative subproblems, the framework establishes a bidirectional reciprocal information flow between restoration and fusion. This process is further unfolded into a multi-stage deep neural network, where each component explicitly corresponds to a specific mathematical operation. In our framework, the fused cross-modal prior actively regularizes the ill-posed restoration, while the purified modality features continuously refine the fusion output. It ensures a transparent architecture that combines the merits of both model-based and data-driven methodologies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our paradigm achieves state-of-the-art performance while providing superior interpretability. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Meskend/MODULE.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Budgeted Safety Verification for Streaming Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A streamed video generator releases each chunk the moment that it is produced, so a safety decision that waits for the finished clip arrives after the harm has been seen. We measure a guardrail by exposure, the harmful frames a viewer is shown, and ask where a fixed moderation budget should be spent. The accurate detector reads decoded frames with a video language model and is too expensive for every chunk, so our guard reads hidden states the generator has computed already and spends a cheap score on deciding when to call it. On 599 streams from a distilled causal generator the undefended model shows 46.25 harmful frames of 81. The video model on every chunk leaves 0.91 frames at 80.1 scored per benign stream, and the same model triggered by our guard leaves 2.35 at 5.3. Spending that budget at random leaves 37.20 frames, so the gain is in the ordering, and a frame detector in the same role gives up almost six, so the judging stage must read the chunk as a clip. The ordering is worth more as the stream lengthens, and the guard carries to a second system. An independent guardrail model agrees with our oracle at $κ=0.74$, and a blinded audit by 50 participants puts its precision at 96.1% and recall at 82.8%. Warning. This paper contains examples of generated content that some readers may find disturbing or offensive in nature.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PP-CFG: Polarity-Preserving Guidance for Controllable Few-Step Image and Video Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Few-step diffusion distillation reduces sampling cost but often weakens adjustable classifier-free guidance (CFG) and runtime negative prompting. We introduce PP-CFG, an architecture that keeps positive and negative text conditions separate and combines their attention responses with opposite signs within a shared visual backbone. Its Scale-Time Polarity Mixer refines each condition using the guidance scale and denoising timestep, allowing prompt influence to vary throughout generation. The student retains a continuous scale input and selectable negative prompts with one visual backbone pass per step. We evaluate PP-CFG on Wan2.1 for video generation with distribution matching distillation (DMD), and on Qwen-Image with both latent consistency model (LCM) distillation and DMD. PP-CFG achieves 81.46 VBench in four steps and lower video teacher-student distances across guidance scales than step-distilled DMD. On NegElement-1K, our benchmark of 1,000 matched image and video prompt cases, it achieves higher target-removal rates than the corresponding teachers. These experiments support the method's generality across attention architectures, generation modalities, and distillation objectives while retaining competitive generation quality.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) still struggle with fine-grained understanding of high-resolution images: attention heads vary in their reliability for grounding target entities and their attributes, while localized details are often disconnected from the broader scene context. We propose EAGLE (Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding), a plug-in framework that jointly selects grounding signals and organizes hierarchical visual evidence. EAGLE employs a fine-grained dataset to screen visually-grounded attention heads, followed by entity-aware grounding to extract target-specific regions. It then integrates hierarchical evidence construction and question-guided routing to select optimal view combinations, feeding them into the frozen MLLM to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. Experiments with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B demonstrate that EAGLE consistently improves performance across both backbones and achieves SOTA results on V*, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K compared with existing methods using the same backbone.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Beyond Prompt Imitation: Capability-Aware Video Generation with Smaller Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Inference-time methods that lift a small open video generator toward a proprietary one are compared through preference scores, which never say how much of the gap to a target video they close. We introduce the oracle control ladder, which hands a fixed student progressively richer information from a target clip and reads the closure of each fidelity metric at each rung as an empirical headroom reference for the methods that must synthesize that information. On 954 clips of the principal student, a dense caption reproduces little of the appearance and almost none of the motion of a target, a first frame closes half of the appearance gap and a tenth of the motion gap, a depth video closes three quarters of the motion gap and leaves color untouched, and the two together close 64 to 94% of every fidelity gap across four teachers, while a second student agrees on the rungs that it accepts. An item response model forecasts which rung closes which clip with held-out AUC of 0.76 to 0.95 on the fidelity criteria and serves as the prior of a budgeted selection policy. When controls are free, a fixed dense-control rung is hard to improve upon, and once controls are priced the policy lies above the fixed-rung frontier at matched cost and survives critics that ruin critic-driven search.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 2D or 3D? Rethinking Token Pruning in 3D VLAs with Cross-Modal Correlation Awareness
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D vision-language-action (VLA) models process both image and point cloud tokens at each control step, increasing the cost of action prediction. Token pruning can reduce this cost, but a token's contribution depends on which other tokens remain. We present 2Dor3D, a framework that jointly selects which 2D and 3D tokens to retain under a fixed token budget. Our analysis shows that either modality can compensate for the other within a patch, that neighboring correlations help explain differences in pruning risk, and that shared tokens couple pruning decisions across patches. In one box-closing observation, two patches with nearly identical interaction scores differed eightfold in the action deviation caused by removing their image token. Guided by these findings, 2Dor3D transfers cross-modal prediction residuals to retained tokens, uses neighborhood correlation entropy to explore more retention choices at local outliers, and updates pruning costs after each proposed exchange between coupled regions. A fused GPU kernel packs the selected tokens into a shorter sequence for subsequent Transformer layers. Across RLBench and LIBERO, 2Dor3D speeds up end-to-end inference by $2.06$--$2.10\times$ on MLA and $1.86$--$1.91\times$ on FiS-VLA, with task success rates 0.5--0.6 percentage points below the corresponding unpruned models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: WINSO: A Large-Size Very-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Dataset for Wind Turbine Detection and Solar Panel Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Wind and solar energy are central to the global transition toward net-zero emissions and sustainable development. Accurate spatial inventories of wind and solar facilities are essential for future energy planning. Satellite remote sensing provides a practical and efficient means to acquire such geospatial data at scale. However, reliable facility mapping from large-size satellite images remains constrained by the scarcity of carefully annotated datasets and the lack of systematic evaluation protocols. To address these limitations, we introduce \textbf{WINSO}, a large-scale wind and solar benchmark based on very-high-resolution (VHR) satellite imagery with ground sampling distances (GSDs) of 0.5--0.7\,m. WINSO comprises 10,962 large-size images sampled from diverse geographic locations across the Asia-Pacific region, covering at least 71,600\,$\text{km}^2$ and totaling 286.36 gigapixels, with individual image dimensions reaching 44,032$\times$62,208 pixels. Through manual annotation and expert verification, a total of 166,473 instances are labeled using horizontal bounding boxes (HBBs) for wind turbines and polygon masks for solar panels. To build baselines for clean-energy facility mapping, we evaluate state-of-the-art detection and segmentation models, specialized ultra-high-resolution (UHR) architectures, and vision-language models across different inference strategies. Furthermore, cross-dataset evaluations on two external public datasets illustrate the strong generalization capability of the WINSO. WINSO establishes a standardized benchmark to advance automated clean-energy mapping, paving the way for wide-area monitoring of the clean-energy transition.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Zero-shot Video Moment Retrieval via Off-the-shelf Multimodal Large Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The target of video moment retrieval (VMR) is predicting temporal spans within a video that semantically match a given linguistic query. Existing VMR methods based on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) overly rely on expensive high-quality datasets and time-consuming fine-tuning. Although some recent studies introduce a zero-shot setting to avoid fine-tuning, they overlook inherent language bias in the query, leading to erroneous localization. To tackle the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes Moment-GPT, a tuning-free pipeline for zero-shot VMR utilizing frozen MLLMs. Specifically, we first employ LLaMA-3 to correct and rephrase the query to mitigate language bias. Subsequently, we design a span generator combined with MiniGPT-v2 to produce candidate spans adaptively. Finally, to leverage the video comprehension capabilities of MLLMs, we apply VideoChatGPT and span scorer to select the most appropriate spans. Our proposed method substantially outperforms the state-ofthe-art MLLM-based and zero-shot models on several public datasets, including QVHighlights, ActivityNet-Captions, and Charades-STA.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learning and Comparing Local Traces for Weakly Supervised Image Manipulation Localization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image manipulation localization identifies edited regions and provides spatial evidence for assessing image reliability, but fully supervised methods require costly pixel-level annotations. Weakly supervised methods reduce this cost using image-level labels, but classification can rely on a few salient cues without ensuring accurate or complete localization. This difficulty is pronounced when manipulation traces are weak and unevenly distributed and authentic and manipulated regions share similar appearance. We propose a CLIP-based framework that integrates Trace-Oriented Vision--Language Adaptation (TOVA) and Relation-Aware Trace Discrimination (RATD). TOVA adapts the visual encoder and uses global visual context to aggregate edge-weighted patch features into image-conditioned class prompts. The resulting class representations support image-level alignment and guide patch selection for Hierarchical Trace Contrastive Learning, providing local contrastive supervision across visual layers. RATD combines local context, spatial structure, and original-image details, then compares learned descriptors between appearance-matched regions. Bidirectional comparison messages are integrated with local features for dense localization. The two components share a visual encoder and are jointly trained using only image-level authenticity labels. Experiments on multiple public benchmarks demonstrate that our framework outperforms the evaluated weakly supervised baselines in image manipulation localization.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Prune to Expand: Training Prompt Enhancers with Less to Imitate
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Prompt enhancement (PE) refines concise user prompts into detailed descriptions to improve the compositional aesthetics of generated images while preserving user intent. A common practice constructs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pairs by deriving short, user-like prompts from dense captions, implicitly assuming that captions that improve image generation also provide effective supervision. In this paper, however, we uncover a counterintuitive finding: PE models trained on caption pairs with substantial generation gains perform comparably to those trained on pairs with only marginal gains. We argue that dense captions can impose redundant supervision by requiring PE models to reproduce image-specific details weakly related to user intent. Motivated by this discrepancy, we introduce Prune to Expand (P2E), a simple text-only method that refines dense-caption supervision by selectively removing redundant sentences under a per-example deletion bound while preserving explicit user requirements and informative visual structure. Extensive experiments under identical training configurations demonstrate that P2E improves alignment with human preferences and visual quality over conventional dense-caption SFT across diverse image categories and visual generators.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: EAST: Event-Anchored Surface Transport for Event-Based Gaussian Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Event-supervised Gaussian reconstruction combines the high temporal resolution and wide dynamic range of event cameras with efficient explicit rendering. However, recovering a continuous surface remains difficult: changes in rendered appearance can compensate for depth errors while preserving the predicted brightness changes. We introduce Event-Anchored Surface Transport (EAST), which couples an event-constrained signed distance field to Gaussian rendering. Triangulation-supported candidates anchor the zero set, while normal flow measured from event timing constrains ray-surface intersection depths. Gaussian centers receive bounded corrections from the descriptor difference between the live field and a frozen initial reference. The correction is zero at initialization, yet transmits image gradients to the live field. Experiments on PAEv3D and NeRF Synthetic show improved surface accuracy and reference-view rendering over Gaussian baselines, together with efficient mesh extraction from the learned field.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A causal video generator writes every segment it produces into a key--value (KV) cache, and later segments know the past only through it. Self-rollout training stops the gradient at this cache, and Self Gradient Forcing (SGF) restores it, but applies it to the same weights that generate the current segment. We find that writing and generating are different roles: in a pretrained generator the written KV already differs from the KV used for denoising, and on shared weights the gradient from future reads is negatively aligned with the gradient of generation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV), which gives the write its own parameters, a low-rank residual used only when a segment enters the cache, and trains them with the gradient of the later segments that read what they wrote. Opening this gradient through the cache in common use exhausts GPU memory. We trace this to checkpoint replay re-writing the cache, not to the gradient path, which removes the need for the second reconstruction pass of SGF. dKV Forcing keeps the cache as persistent differentiable pages and computes the exact gradient in one temporal traversal, with an $11\%$ lower memory peak and $28\%$ less resident memory. With pages that store hidden states, it trains 15\,s clips on which the two-pass reconstruction runs out of memory. Trained on 5\,s clips, dKV Forcing reaches the highest VBench-Long quality score at 60\,s and 240\,s and outperforms SGF by $3.6$ and $6.1$ points of aesthetic quality, with a higher dynamic degree.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AlphaWiSE: Adaptive Weight Interpolation for Continual Multimodal Representation Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal retrieval models align audio, images, and text in a shared embedding space, but sequential adaptation can degrade cross-modal relationships learned in earlier phases. Existing continual-learning procedures produce a single final checkpoint, so every retrieval direction shares the same stability-plasticity trade-off. We introduce AlphaWiSE, a post-hoc weight-space interpolation method that combines a sequential fine-tuning endpoint with a companion endpoint obtained with a stability-oriented continual-learning method. AlphaWiSE fits one scalar interpolation coefficient for each corresponding parameter tensor on an exemplar memory while both endpoints remain frozen. The interpolated tensors are then materialized into a single checkpoint, so the deployed model retains the architecture and inference cost of a single backbone. On continual audio-image-text retrieval, the fused model improves on the better of its two endpoints in 13 of 18 average retrieval measures and on the fixed blend of the same checkpoints in 25 of 36 measures. Its pairings achieve the strongest average audio-to-text and image-to-audio retrieval among all compared methods. Project page: https://alphawise.cvmlgroup.web.illinois.edu/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HiFi-Portrait: Zero-shot Identity-preserved Portrait Generation with High-fidelity Multi-face Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent advancements in diffusion-based technologies have made significant strides, particularly in identity-preserved portrait generation (IPG). However, when using multiple reference images from the same ID, existing methods typically produce lower-fidelity portraits and struggle to customize face attributes precisely. To address these issues, this paper presents HiFi-Portrait, a high-fidelity method for zero-shot portrait generation. Specifically, we first introduce the face refiner and landmark generator to obtain fine-grained multi-face features and 3D-aware face landmarks. The landmarks include the reference ID and the target attributes. Then, we design HiFi-Net to fuse multi-face features and align them with landmarks, which improves ID fidelity and face control. In addition, we devise an automated pipeline to construct an ID-based dataset for training HiFi-Portrait. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses the SOTA approaches in face similarity and controllability. Furthermore, our method is also compatible with previous SDXL-based works.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Morphology-Aware Sample Assignment: Overcoming IoU Insensitivity for Surface Defect Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Intersection-over-Union (IoU), as a pivotal metric for evaluating the spatial alignment between candidate proposals and ground-truth annotations, directly determines the quality of positive sample sets and the training efficacy of visual detection models. Through theoretical modeling and analysis, we uncover a non-sensitive region on the IoU response curve, within which samples yield nearly identical IoU scores despite distinct geometric overlaps. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a set of morphological similarity metrics covering area, shape, and aspect ratio, to refine the positive sample assignment process, thereby ensuring more discriminative and reliable matching. A supplementary matching score is derived via mean-based aggregation of these multidimensional similarities, compensating for the intrinsic limitation of IoU in representing structural correspondence. Theoretically, incorporating morphological similarity reshapes the response distribution of the matching function, yielding both effective directional gradients and polygon-like iso-response contours, which tightly confine high-response regions around each ground-truth instance and substantially enhance the precision of positive sample selection. Experiments based on the YOLOv9 framework demonstrate consistent performance gains on both NEUDET and GC10- DET datasets. Notably, the proposed approach is fully plug-and-play and incurs zero additional inference overhead, thereby ensuring deployment efficiency for industrial visual inspection.

Information Retrieval.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

Information Retrieval.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
Information Retrieval.summary:
Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model's calibrated answer to a natural-language question, with outcomes yes, no, or not stated. A record's embedding is its answers across an ordered set of questions. Similarity decomposes exactly into per-question contributions, and new questions add coordinates without altering existing ones.
  On public product benchmarks, question-space retrieval matches dense candidate generation statistically in a retrieve-then-verify entity matcher, while providing exact explanations for accepted matches. Questions derived from retrieval failures triple mean reciprocal rank without re-encoding prior answers. For search, inferring the attributes of a suitable result outperforms encoding only the literal request, and combining question-space and dense scores improves retrieval, though not at our prespecified confidence threshold. A single small neural network predicts the full interpretable vector from an existing dense embedding, enabling corpus backfilling from a few thousand labeled rows at roughly 1/200 the cost. We position interpretable embeddings as a complementary, readable retrieval channel for explaining matches, filtering on attributes, and extending indexes as failures expose missing facts.
Information Retrieval.comment: 25 pages, 7 figures, including appendices. Evaluations on WDC Products and STaRK-Amazon

Information Retrieval.title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
Information Retrieval.summary: Text encoders turn earnings calls into vectors for search, for language models that answer from retrieved passages, and for forecasting models. A live retriever can use an encoder trained once on all available text, as finance retrievers are, but a backtest needs an encoder that read no text written after the date of each vector. To address this look-ahead bias, from 412,248 calls we train vintages under four pretraining recipes, with yearly cutoffs from 2010 to 2024, and each vintage reads only text dated on or before its cutoff. We then fine-tune each vintage on the question-answer pairs of the calls themselves. The vintages we train on calls alone, with 33.8M parameters, retrieve answers on held-out calls better than the general retrievers we tested in every test quarter. Their vectors also raise by about half the rank correlation between next-day returns and forecasts built from past returns and firm size. When each vintage continues the previous one, a later vintage retrieves better on earlier quarters than the vintage available at the time, and a point-in-time language model that answers from the passages the later vintage retrieves inherits the gain. The 2024 vintage of our families also forecasts earnings surprises better, although the interval of this gain includes zero on calls that no vintage read. It forecasts returns no better, so point-in-time vintages matter most for retrieval and little for forecasts of returns.
Information Retrieval.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the 3rd IEEE International Workshop on Large Language Models for Finance, IEEE BigData 2026. Code: https://github.com/Alessiobrini/point-in-time-encoders-for-earnings-calls

Information Retrieval.title: Pre-Crawl Prioritization and Seed Classification for Large-Scale Web Archiving
Information Retrieval.summary: Pre-crawl prioritization systems decide which pages to fetch first before indexing, aiming to improve crawl efficiency and coverage. Existing approaches based on page popularity and relevance are unsuited to web-archival crawlers that prioritize comprehensive coverage over selective retrieval. We explore prioritization techniques tailored to web archival operations using URL lexical analysis, dynamic domain reputation systems, and HTTP response analysis to inform crawl scheduling decisions. By incorporating predictive models that estimate content change and disappearance probabilities, we improve crawl completeness while reducing redundant visits to stable resources. Through large-scale experiments, we demonstrate that our methods improve archival effectiveness and resource utilization compared to undirected crawling.
Information Retrieval.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Published in the 2025 ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries (JCDL)

Information Retrieval.title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: AI agents that talk with users across many sessions need long-term memory to stay coherent and personalized. Existing approaches use either flat retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that ignores how memories connect, or entity-centric knowledge graphs. Entity-centric graphs split each message into separate triples, which loses its context, and in conversations the speakers become hubs linked to almost every message, so propagation through them tells retrieval little. We present GAAMA, a graph-augmented associative memory that organizes conversations around topics. It keeps verbatim episodes, uses an LLM to distill them into atomic facts and topic concepts, and then synthesizes higher-order reflections. These four node types are linked by five kinds of structural edges, and topic concepts supply the cross-cutting paths, so mega-hubs do not form. Retrieval blends nearest-neighbor similarity search with Personalized PageRank whose transitions depend on edge type. We also introduce GRAFT (Graph Repair by Augmenting Facts & Topology), an offline repair step: for questions whose retrieved evidence fell short, a bounded ReAct agent searches memory again and records the grounded answer as a fresh fact, so later questions find it directly without extra query-time cost. On LoCoMo10, GAAMA achieves the highest average score of all compared methods (79.1%) and is competitive in every question category; GRAFT adds a small further gain. In a controlled comparison, replacing GAAMA's concept-linked facts with entity relation triples lowers reward by 3.0 pp. On MemoryArena, scored on what memory alone determines, GAAMA has the best score on average.

Information Retrieval.title: CogRec: Structure-Cognitive Fast-and-Slow Reasoning for Generative Recommendation
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative recommendation reformulates next-item prediction as identifier sequence generation, yet existing methods mainly treat the generated identifiers as target sequences to be memorized, leaving their hierarchical and relational structure underused for explicit reasoning. We propose CogRec, a structure-cognitive fast-and-slow reasoning framework that grounds intermediate reasoning in the same SID topology used for target generation. CogRec augments the vertical SID hierarchy with intra-layer semantic graphs and introduces SID Routing to represent recommendation reasoning through layer-wise Match, LateralJump, and Explore operations. These operations provide a structural interpretation of fast localization and slow navigation. A supervised multi-stage pipeline aligns newly introduced SID tokens, establishes direct generation, and trains natural-language and SID Routing branches from a shared checkpoint. Experiments on three Amazon Reviews 2014 categories show dataset-dependent effects of SID Routing. Routing improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 over its direct-generation counterpart on Beauty and Sports, while reducing both metrics on Toys. These results characterize the benefits and dataset-dependent behavior of SID-grounded intermediate reasoning for generative recommendation. Code is available at https://github.com/caskcsg/CogRec.

Information Retrieval.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
Information Retrieval.summary: Learning effective feature interactions is essential for industrial recommender systems. DCN and DCNv2 efficiently automate polynomial feature crossing. However, their cross layers construct interactions using only non-negative integer powers of the input features, with the maximum degree controlled by network depth. Consequently, they cannot directly represent the reciprocal terms required for ratios, rates, and normalized counts unless such features are explicitly provided as inputs. We introduce DCDN, a Deep Cross-Division Network that augments a DCNv2-style cross layer with a division branch. DCDN jointly learns product, ratio, and mixed product-ratio interactions. We characterize the representable interactions as multivariate Laurent polynomials and show that a $K$-layer DCDN generates Laurent monomials of $\ell_1$-order up to $K+1$, with signed degree between $-K$ and $K+1$. We evaluate DCDN against a production-optimized neural-ranking baseline built around DCNv2 and supplied with manually engineered ratio features. Replacing the DCNv2 block with DCDN allowed us to eliminate the entire class of manually engineered ratio features from the model input, reducing the number of input features by $40.1\%$. DCDN is deployed in the production ranking stack of a major short-video service. In a live A/B test on this service, DCDN increased likes by $3.25\%$, shares by $16.26\%$, total view time (TVT) by $0.33\%$, and clicks to open fullscreen by $0.38\%$; all changes were statistically significant. The number of shown videos decreased slightly ($-0.24\%$). These results demonstrate that DCDN can improve user engagement while eliminating reliance on manually engineered ratio features. Our code is publicly released at https://github.com/rw404/DCDN.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted at WSDM 2027. 14 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables

Information Retrieval.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wrocław, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the best of thirteen backbones from seven pretraining paradigms reaches 94.7%. Accuracy falls slowly as candidates are added: for DINOv2, by about 0.8 points each time their number doubles. A natural design for a phone guide compares a photograph only with statues near the user. In simulation this helps, but less than an equal number of randomly chosen statues does, so random subsampling overstates its value; a permutation test ties the penalty to the real layout (p = 0.005). Used as a weight instead of a filter, location raises DINOv2 from 93.4% to 98.7% for a simulated user 25 m from the statue. With the query's photographer withheld, learned local-feature matching raises DINOv2 accuracy from 81.8% to 85.5% and also improves DINOv3. Comparing the two best candidates cuts DINOv2's false acceptance of unknown statues from 38.3% to 19.6% at 90% known acceptance.
Information Retrieval.comment: 23 pages, 6 figures in the main text; includes appendix. Project page: https://turhancan97.github.io/doppeldwarf-306/

Information Retrieval.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
Information Retrieval.summary: Long-term memory is essential for personalized agentic systems that interact with users over long time periods, yet current architectures only capture what happened while leaving the reasoning of why it happened to be derived later by underlying LLMs. These events can, however, convey not only what a user experienced but also how that experience shaped their behavioral patterns. We introduce STARK, a dual-graph memory architecture which treats these events not just as nodes but also as edges between behavioral insights. STARK maintains an Episodic Graph which records interactions as temporally, causally, and semantically linked episodes; and an Insight Graph which represents LLM-extracted behavioral signals scored by how many events support them, connected by the very events that led to them. At inference, behavioral knowledge is retrieved directly from insight nodes grounded by event-as-edges, eliminating repeated episodic traversal. The event-as-edge structure also naturally enables projecting the knowledge graph into a relational embedding space where cross-user transfer becomes possible under shared contextual circumstances, allowing the system to infer missing insights for cold-start users. Evaluations show that STARK improves by 1.48 judge score on LongMemEval information extraction and 0.93 on LoCoMo open domain questions over state of the art. On the public LongLaMP abstract-generation benchmark, cross-user transfer improves open-ended judge scores by 0.7 points and ROUGE-L by 3 at 5% graph sparsity.

Information Retrieval.title: From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search
Information Retrieval.summary: Agentic search demands that a search engine move beyond per document relevance ranking to assemble document sets optimized for downstream LLM reasoning. Prior work addresses this either by improving individual pipeline stages in isolation or by applying RL based selection on top of relevance trained upstream modules, leaving the full stack unaligned to utility for reasoning. We propose rubric aligned search, a framework that unifies the traditional search pipeline under a single supervision surface. For each query, we derive a rubric from coarse to fine, specifying weighted positive criteria that the document set must satisfy and negative criteria that it must avoid. From this rubric we derive two training signals. First, a lightweight labeler distills rubric grounded judgments into per document utility labels, which supervise a contrastive dual encoder for retrieval and a multi task ranker trained with four rubric aligned scoring heads. Second, a rubric conditioned evaluator produces a set level reward that drives a dual branch RL selector, combining GRPO with best rollout distillation to resolve credit assignment in subset optimization. Deployed in Yuanbao Search, the pipeline improves end to end answer quality by 8.52% over the online production baseline.
Information Retrieval.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables, accepted at KDD 2027

Information Retrieval.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
Information Retrieval.summary: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. On the three long-form tasks of LongLaMP with three LLMs, SP-Refine outperforms LongLaMP's retrieval-augmented baseline in 25 of 27 ROUGE and METEOR comparisons, by 10.2% on average and by up to 35.8%. Annotating users' own texts with the extracted profiles shows that StylePrism captures concrete, checkable habits, from the order of rhetorical moves to a reviewer's sign-off. Ablations show that the profile helps as revision guidance, not as a replacement for the samples: writing from the profile alone is worse in all 27 comparisons, while a single implicit-inference call is a cheaper alternative that comes close. Oracle variants that let the reviser see the reference, together with reference-free controls, show that larger refinement gains require information unavailable at inference time.

Information Retrieval.title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems
Information Retrieval.summary: Large-scale recommendation systems face "Memory Wall" bottlenecks due to massive, dense embedding tables. While generative retrieval uses discrete tokens for IDs, high-dimensional context still relies on inefficient dense formats. Inspired by computer vision data compression, we propose Dual-purpose Semantic IDs to achieve LLM-level I/O efficiency. Our methodology uses hierarchical quantization to condense continuous embeddings into discrete Semantic IDs performing two concurrent roles: (1) Collaborative Identity: modeling user-item interactions via learnable embedding table; and (2) Content Reconstruction: using a lightweight Semantic Decoder for on-the-fly embedding approximation. This approach replaces massive vector storage with on-demand reconstruction, reducing system overhead and data footprints. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework through offline evaluations and successful online deployment in production-scale ranking and retrieval systems at a major video sharing platform, showing that discrete tokens are indeed all you need for highly efficient, content-rich recommendation.

Information Retrieval.title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing
Information Retrieval.summary:
Online A/B testing is the standard approach for evaluating changes to user-facing systems, such as a new recommendation or ranking policy, before deployment. While the difference-in-means estimator of a standard A/B test is unbiased, it often suffers from high variance. When the treatment and production policies choose the same actions with similar probabilities, the resulting observations can add noise while providing little information about the difference between the policies. Consequently, A/B tests can require large amounts of traffic and long durations to detect small treatment effects. Existing variance-reduction methods mainly improve the estimator after the data-collection scheme has been fixed, and recent overlap-aware designs only optimize a single traffic split between the two policies; thereby, they cannot direct traffic to the actions on which the policies disagree.
  In this paper, we jointly optimize how actions are sampled and how the resulting observations are used to estimate the treatment effect. Our contributions are two-fold. First, building on pairwise off-policy evaluation, we derive the variance-optimal action-level logging policy for estimating the average treatment effect between two policies, which has a closed-form solution for any fixed control variate. Second, we use historical logs to jointly optimize the logging policy and a control variate to further reduce variance. Our experimental results in simulated policy A/B tests show that our designs estimate the average treatment effect more accurately than existing variance reduction methods on every evaluated setting, while generally improving statistical power and reducing how often the worse policy is selected. As a result, our designs enable practitioners to reach reliable deployment decisions with considerably less online traffic.

Information Retrieval.title: Towards Comprehensible Recommendation with Large Language Model Fine-tuning
Information Retrieval.summary: Recommender systems have become increasingly ubiquitous in daily life. While traditional recommendation approaches primarily rely on ID-based representations or item-side content features, they often fall short in capturing the underlying semantics aligned with user preferences (e.g., recommendation reasons for items), leading to a semantic-collaborative gap. Recently emerged LLM-based feature extraction approaches also face a key challenge: how to ensure that LLMs possess recommendation-aligned reasoning capabilities and can generate accurate, personalized reasons to mitigate the semantic-collaborative gap. To address these issues, we propose a novel Content Understanding from a Collaborative Perspective framework (CURec), which generates collaborative-aligned content features for more comprehensive recommendations. CURec first adapts the LLM with recommendation objectives through post-training, equipping it with instruction-following and chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Next, we use the LLM-generated features to train the recommender model. Then, we treat the user-item prediction scores produced by the trained recommender model as reward signals to guide RL-based refinement of the LLM, thereby improving the quality of generated reasons and pattern. The corrected reasons are directly integrated into the recommender model to enhance comprehensibility and recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of CURec over existing methods.

Information Retrieval.title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewrites advantages using a deduplicated group reward and marginal advantage within GRPO, avoiding auxiliary diversity objectives. Deployed online with a lightweight 0.1B backbone, TS-GEAR serves over 150 million queries per day in the search advertising pipeline of Taobao Shangou, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods on both HitRate and geographic validity, and achieving 3.8% gains in ad impressions and 4.2% in ad revenue.

Information Retrieval.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
Information Retrieval.summary: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. We study the leader finding problem, where the query is a project and a team and the output is a ranked list of candidate leaders. We model the problem in a probabilistic framework that combines technical fit, managerial knowledge, and communication with the team, and we propose one evaluation metric for each of these qualities. On two large collections built from Stack Overflow, the best configuration of our model more than doubles the NDCG@10 of the strongest baseline. These results show that a ranking of leaders must balance several qualities that topical expertise alone does not capture.
Information Retrieval.comment: Extended version of the ICTIR '21 short paper (doi:10.1145/3471158.3472230). 30 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables

Information Retrieval.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. Moving queries to a different encoder normally requires re-embedding the whole corpus, and at cold start there are no query logs while every document embedded by the new encoder incurs an API or compute cost. We present ERA (Embed, Route, Adapt), a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval. ERA spends a small anchor budget on maximally informative documents, selected from the existing target index via Cosine Farthest Point Sampling, trains a lightweight adapter with a Manifold Alignment Loss that couples directional alignment with orthogonal regularization to prevent representation collapse, and pairs the adapter with a deterministic router that escalates the rare, hard queries that define perceived retrieval quality. Across five BEIR datasets, ERA matches or outperforms point-wise L2 and embedding-conversion baselines, with relative gains of up to 35% nDCG@10 on Arguana, and on clustered corpora its anchor selection also improves prior methods under a fixed anchor budget. With 1.2 ms of adapter and router overhead on top of a ~20 ms local encoder, ERA at a 20% nominal escalation budget reduces end-to-end query latency from roughly 160 ms to 38-86 ms while concentrating escalations on the queries where the projection fails most.

Information Retrieval.title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
Information Retrieval.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. In visually oriented domains such as video streaming, item images provide complementary signals that may also inform recommendation diversity. This raises two questions: when does visual information improve recommendation quality, and can multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) enhance relevance and diversity simultaneously? We investigate these questions through a training-free, diversity-aware multimodal reranking framework that jointly incorporates item images, textual metadata, and user interaction histories. We conduct an empirical study across three public Amazon Review datasets and an industrial Amazon Prime Video dataset, using both open-source and proprietary MLLMs. Our results reveal substantial domain-dependent effects: adding visual information yields up to 121.9% relative improvement in NDCG@5 on Prime Video, while producing limited or inconsistent gains on product recommendation datasets. Furthermore, MLLM-based reranking improves both relevance and category-diversity-sensitive ranking quality over a sequential recommendation baseline, achieving up to 71.0% improvement in NDCG@5 and 14.1% in $α$-NDCG@5 on Prime Video. These findings highlight the conditional value of visual information and the potential of training-free MLLMs for relevance- and diversity-aware recommendation reranking.

Information Retrieval.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
Information Retrieval.summary: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. However, critical experimental details are often distributed across text, tables, figures, captions, and surrounding discussion, making them difficult to recover using conventional text-only extraction. Existing LLM-based and multimodal RAG pipelines typically rely on full-document context or coarse page-level retrieval, introducing substantial irrelevant evidence and high textual and visual token costs. We propose GERF, a Graph-based Evidence Retrieval Framework for token-efficient, schema-guided multimodal scientific IE. GERF represents each article as a heterogeneous evidence graph that connects schema fields, text chunks, figures, and figure-derived content through semantic and structural relations. Using schema fields as retrieval anchors, GERF combines direct semantic retrieval, Random Walk with Restart, and null-aware evidence expansion to construct compact, field-specific multimodal evidence packages. Visual interpretation is applied only to graph-selected figures, avoiding indiscriminate processing of the entire document. We evaluate GERF from two complementary perspectives: evidence retrieval quality and pipeline-level input-token consumption. On the expert-annotated SOFC-Exp corpus, GERF retrieves gold-supported evidence for 94.55% of the evaluated field instances, providing broad field-level evidence coverage for downstream extraction. In the token comparison, GERF reduces average input-token usage by 73.40% relative to full-context processing and uses fewer tokens than the evaluated page-level pipelines.

Information Retrieval.title: DM-Lab at TREC 2026 RAG: Multi-Query Retrieval, Ensemble Judging, and Claim-Pack Generation
Information Retrieval.summary: We present DM-Lab-RAG-2026, a framework developed for the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track. The framework integrates large-scale evidence retrieval and citation-grounded answer generation over the 553-million-document ClimbMix-400B corpus. The retrieval architecture combines multi-query BM25, reciprocal rank fusion, ensemble relevance assessment, listwise reranking, and adaptive retrieval depth. The generation pipeline employs a claim-first strategy to extract evidence-linked atomic claims, construct cited responses, and verify source support. Across 22 development topics, the retrieval system achieved a mean nDCG@30 of 0.604. In the official evaluation, it attained a set precision of 0.455 and a manual nugget gain of 0.910. Additional experiments examine the influence of reranking, evidence selection, and citation verification on system performance. The evaluation demonstrates the potential of diversified lexical retrieval and language-model-based relevance assessment for large-scale evidence discovery. It further identifies evidence preservation and structured answer construction as key considerations for reliable RAG. This work provides a reproducible framework for investigating retrieval effectiveness and evidence-grounded generation.
Information Retrieval.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 8 tables. TREC 2026 RAG Track. Code: https://github.com/Elyasirankhah/TREC-RAG-2026

Information Retrieval.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team's channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. We evaluate Memanto, a memory agent that ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench, which tests memory through 600 simulated workplace tasks, each validated as requiring memory. Running in the Hermes agent harness with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations per conversation, Memanto completes 503 tasks (83.83%). The strongest configuration reported by the benchmark's authors, Mem0 with GPT-5.6-Luna and up to 60 iterations, completes 424 (70.67%). Memanto's run also has the lowest total cost ($10.86, against $61.48 for the cheapest reported run) and the shortest median task latency (15.32s). Grading uses the benchmark's own judge, but the agent model differs, so these results compare complete systems. The memory system affects both whether an agent completes such tasks and what completion costs.
Information Retrieval.comment: Future version will submit to ACL

Mathematical Software.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
Mathematical Software.summary: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1, \dots, n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the records published before this work; one of them, the optimal formula for $π$ with 1-9 (error $2.81 \cdot 10^{-14}$), was found independently by M. Verheyen, and we prove it optimal. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
Mathematical Software.comment: 51 pages, 1 figure. v2: acknowledged M. Verheyen's independent discovery of the optimal 1-9 formula for pi, renumbered tables sequentially, updated references, and made minor editorial corrections. Code, data and certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24356239

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Cluster Editing in Subexponential Fixed-Parameter Time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Cluster Editing asks whether at most $k$ edge additions and deletions turn a given $n$-vertex graph into a disjoint union of cliques. For more than a decade, the fastest algorithm for it was the golden-ratio algorithm of Böcker with running time $O(1.62^k+n^{O(1)})$. Cao and Chen had conjectured that the subexponential running time $2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$ is possible, but this contradicts the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH). Recently, the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT of OpenAI and Anthropic refuted ETH itself.
  Our main result transfers running times from 3-SAT to Cluster Editing. If 3-SAT on formulas with $m$ clauses can be decided in time $T(m)$, then there is an algorithm that, given a graph with $n$ vertices and integers $k$ and $r$ with $2\le r\le k^{1/3}$, decides Cluster Editing in time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot T(2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k)\cdot n^{O(1)}$. Combined with the breakthrough algorithms for 3-SAT, this proves Cao and Chen's conjecture, as it solves Cluster Editing in time $2^{O(k\cdot(\log\log\log k)^{3/2}/\sqrt{\log\log k})}\cdot n^{O(1)}=2^{o(k)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$. The key ingredient is a sparsification theorem for Cluster Editing, the counterpart of the Sparsification Lemma for satisfiability: In time $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}\cdot n^{O(1)}$, it reduces a given instance to $2^{O((k\log r)/r)}$ weighted instances with $O(rk)$ vertices and degree $O(r)$, each of which is equivalent to a 3-SAT formula with $2^{O(r^2\log r)}\cdot k$ clauses. Conversely, by a known reduction with linear blow-up, every saving in the exponent for Cluster Editing is, up to constant factors, a saving for 3-SAT.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: One partition function call to rule them all: Efficiently computing the equilibrium landscape of multiple nucleic acid strands
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In the nearest neighbour model of DNA/RNA binding, the partition function (PF) is a sum of Boltzmann-weighted free energies of the exponentially large set of secondary structures. Dirks et al. [SIAM review, 2007] gave a polynomial time PF algorithm for $O(1)$ strands, generalising McCaskill [Biopolymers, 1990] single-stranded case. Despite the intuition that PF may somehow encode the entire state space, thus far different approaches were required to solve various energy-landscape prediction problems. For example: finding the minimum free energy (MFE), structure(s) for $O(1)$ strands was open since 2007, and we recently solved [ICALP, 2025] via new techniques.
  We asked if there is a magnifiable PF algorithm [DNA31, 2025], which we answer here in the affirmative. We give an $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space algorithm, for $c=O(1)$ strands of $N$ bases, the same overhead as Dirks et al. (non-magnifiable) algorithm. However, we show that magnification allows for efficient decoding of the entire landscape, concretely: a single call to the magnifiable PF efficiently solves and improves upon a large number of problems, giving:
  - MFE in $O(N^3(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^2)$ space; a considerable improvement over our $O(N^4(c-1)!)$ time, $O(N^4)$ space result [ICALP 2025].
  - The first polynomial time algorithm for the multi-stranded density of states problem, in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space.
  - The first polynomial time algorithm outputting the entire list of energy levels occupied by at least one structure (in time $O(N^3(c-1)!),O(N^2)$ space), and the first algorithms for various energy landscape and counting problems.
  Our approach unifies the field of energy landscape prediction showing that a single, general, algorithmic framework neatly unifies a large collection of problems that practitioners care about, and required distinct techniques with worse time bounds.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter.
  We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid.
  A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Benefit of Migration in Throughput Maximization on Unrelated Machines and under Restricted Assignment
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In preemptive throughput maximization on parallel machines, jobs have release dates, due dates and weights, and the goal is to maximize the total weight of the jobs completed by their due dates. We study the benefit of migration, i.e., by what factor the optimal weight can increase when a preempted job is allowed to resume on a different machine. By a classic result of Kalyanasundaram and Pruhs, on identical machines the migratory optimum is at most $O(1)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We give, for the first time, bounds for unrelated machines and for restricted assignment. We show that on unrelated machines, when every eligible machine can complete a job by itself, the migratory optimum is at most $O(\sqrt n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum, where $n$ is the number of jobs. Under restricted assignment it is at most $O(\log n)$ times the nonmigratory optimum. We provide instances which show that both bounds are best possible up to constant factors, even when the jobs have unit weights. Since our proofs are constructive, we obtain the first nontrivial approximation algorithms for migratory throughput maximization on unrelated machines and under restricted assignment.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 68 pages, 5 figures

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Linear-Size Spectral Sparsification by Sign Descent
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Given an undirected graph with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and arbitrary positive weights, we construct a $(1\pm\varepsilon)$-spectral sparsifier with $O(n/\varepsilon^2)$ edges. For every $0<\varepsilon<1$, the algorithm succeeds with high probability and runs in time \[
  O\!\left(n+\varepsilon^{-3}\bigl[m\log^2 n+n\log^3 n\,(\log\log n)^4\bigr]\right). \] In each phase we seek a reweighting that brings many edge weights to zero or twice their current value while keeping the relative change in every graph energy small. Reversing the weight changes preserves the error and exchanges deletion with doubling, so one choice deletes at least half the edges that reach an endpoint. We balance a smooth penalty for spectral error against a linear reward for alignment with independent random signs. Each step changes the free weights by a fixed fraction of their values at the start of the phase, with directions chosen from the estimated signs of the negative gradient. A weight stays fixed once it reaches an endpoint. We show that while few weights are fixed, the remaining edges admit a direction whose gain in reward exceeds its first-order spectral cost by a constant. The objective is bounded below, so this decrease forces a constant fraction of the weights to an endpoint. We repeat the partial coloring on the surviving edges, choosing the tolerances to keep the total relative error within $\varepsilon$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Approximation Ratio of $k$-means++ Is $2\ln k+O(1)$
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Given a finite set of points in Euclidean space, $k$-means clustering seeks $k$ centers that minimize the sum of squared distances from each point to its nearest center. The $k$-means++ algorithm chooses its first center uniformly at random from the data points and each subsequent center with probability proportional to its squared distance from the nearest center already chosen. Let $R_k$ be the worst-case ratio between the expected cost of the $k$ seeds chosen by $k$-means++ and the optimal $k$-means cost. In their seminal paper introducing $k$-means++, Arthur and Vassilvitskii (SODA 2007) showed that $2\ln k\le R_k\le8(\ln k+2)$, and Makarychev, Reddy and Shan (NeurIPS 2020) improved the upper bound to $5(\ln k+2)$. We prove that $R_k=2\ln k+O(1)$; more precisely, $2H_{k-1}+2\le R_k\le 2H_{k-2}+5$ for $k\ge2$, where $H_j$ is the $j$th harmonic number, so the two bounds differ by less than $3$. We also determine $R_2=5$ and $R_3=185/32$, with a unified proof of both upper bounds, and give a second family of lower bounds that exceeds $2H_{k-1}+2$ for $2\le k\le18$. Previous analyses bound the expected cost of a cluster just after it is first sampled by a constant times its optimal cost, and then charge that cost for the rest of the run. We track how a cluster's cost evolves after its first hit. At each subsequent draw, the probability of sampling that cluster again is exactly its share of the current cost. We show that the cost reductions from these later hits suffice, in expectation, to bring the leading coefficient down to $2$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 24 pages, 1 figure. Verification code included as ancillary files

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Geometrically Constrained Learning I: Agnostically Learning Adversarially Robust Classifiers
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
