Given strings $X$ and $Y$ and a displacement tolerance $d$, LAMAS reports, for every position $i$ of $Y$, the longest substring starting at $i$ that occurs in $X$ at a position $j$ with $|j-i|\le d$, together with the displacement $(j-i)$. MS is the special case of LAMAS with unbounded $d$. Our main result is an algorithm that solves LAMAS in $\mathcal{O}(n)$ time and space for strings of length at most $n$ and any $d$; this is optimal and matches the complexity of MS. The algorithm reduces LAMAS to predecessor and successor queries over a sliding window of suffix ranks and answers them in linear total time via a window decomposition and interval union-find.
  Experiments on 20 real datasets and synthetic data show that LAMAS substantially improves over MS and $q$-gram distance in similarity-based classification, top-$K$ retrieval, and clustering. It is competitive with edit distance and a constrained dynamic time warping variant in classification and generally outperforms a state-of-the-art method for top-$K$ retrieval under edit distance. Finally, our implementation of the main algorithm for LAMAS scales linearly in $n$ and does not slow down as $d$ grows.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on $n$ fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature $β$ to precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,β,\log(1/δ))$. This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/δ))$. (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,β,\log(1/δ))$. Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error $δ$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $β$ and linear in $1/δ$ up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the $\exp(β)$ overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 57 pages,1 figure

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Optimal Private Gaussian Multi-sampling
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give polynomial-time algorithms for Gaussian multi-sampling under approximate $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differential privacy, with optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors. Our main construction uses $\widetilde{O}(m+d\sqrt{m}/\varepsilon)$ independent input samples from a $d$-dimensional Gaussian $P$ with unknown mean and covariance to generate $m$ exactly independent outputs. Their joint distribution is $α$-close in total variation to $P^{\otimes m}$. Our lower bounds hold even for dependent outputs under the same joint accuracy guarantee, showing that exact independence incurs no additional sample cost beyond logarithmic factors.
  The single-sampler of Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis [COLT 2025] uses $\widetilde{O}(d/\varepsilon)$ input samples. Running it on a separate input dataset for each of $m$ outputs therefore costs $\widetilde{O}(md/\varepsilon)$ in total. Our construction reduces this dimension-dependent sample cost from linear to square-root dependence on the number of outputs.
  Our approach builds on the stable weighted statistics of Brown, Hopkins, and Smith [COLT 2023], also used for Gaussian single-sampling by Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis. To control privacy loss when the entire batch shares these statistics, we compare the joint output densities and obtain a privacy bound that scales with the square root of the batch size. The stability step downweights influential records and can reject the entire batch. Both actions can make the outputs dependent. Our correction restores exact independence while preserving differential privacy and joint accuracy.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 78 pages, 1 figure, includes appendices

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Sublinear Time Quantum Algorithm for Attention Approximation
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Given the query, key and value matrices $Q, K, V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, the attention module is defined as $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)=D^{-1}AV$ where $A=\exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})$ with $\exp(\cdot)$ applied entrywise, $D=\mathrm{diag}(A\mathbf{1}_n)$. The attention module is the backbone of modern transformers and large language models, but explicitly forming the softmax matrix $D^{-1}A$ incurs $Ω(n^2)$ time, motivating numerous approximation schemes that reduce runtime to $\widetilde O(nd)$ via sparsity or low-rank factorization.
  We propose a quantum data structure that approximates any row of $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)$ using only row queries to $Q, K, V$. Our algorithm preprocesses these matrices in $\widetilde{O}(ε^{-1} n^{0.5} (s_λ^{3} + s_λ^{2} d + d) + ε^{-2} s_λd)$ time, where $ε$ is the target accuracy and $s_λ$ is the $λ$-statistical dimension of the exponential kernel defined by $Q$ and $K$. Each row query can be answered in $\widetilde{O}(s_λ^2 + s_λd)$ time. If every row sum of $A$ exceeds $ε\|A\|+λ\sqrt n$, then with probability $1-1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ the answers have Frobenius-norm error $O(β\|D^{-1}\|(ε\|A\|_F+λ\sqrt n)\|V\|_F)$. Here $β=(1-(ε\|A\|+λ\sqrt n)\|D^{-1}\|)^{-1}\geq 1$ is close to $1$ when every row sum is much larger than $ε\|A\|+λ\sqrt n$.
  To our knowledge, this is the first quantum data structure that approximates rows of the attention matrix in sublinear time with respect to $n$. Our approach relies on a quantum Nyström approximation of the exponential kernel, quantum multivariate mean estimation for computing $D$, and quantum sampling of the rows of $V$ by their squared norms, with a median over independent samples, for the multiplication with $V$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: ICLR 2026. This version corrects the main theorem: the preprocessing time, the row-query count, and the error bound, whose $λ\sqrt{n}$ term is additive and which needs large row sums and a full-rank Nystrom factor. The product with V now samples rows by squared norms, as the published leverage-score step and its boosting were invalid, and the error proof is completed

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Graph-based Nearest Neighbors with Dynamic Updates via Random Walks
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) is a common way to retrieve relevant search results, especially now in the context of large language models and retrieval augmented generation. One of the most widely used algorithms for ANN is based on constructing a multi-layer graph over the dataset, called the Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW). While this algorithm supports insertion of new data, it does not support deletion of existing data. Moreover, deletion algorithms described by prior work come at the cost of increased query latency, decreased recall, or prolonged deletion time. In this paper, we propose a new theoretical framework for graph-based ANN based on random walks. We then utilize this framework to analyze a randomized deletion approach that approximately preserves hitting time statistics compared to the graph before deleting the point. However, this guarantee needs at least as many edge samples as there are edges in the clique over the neighbors of the deleted point. We then turn this theoretical framework into a deterministic deletion algorithm, and show that it provides a better tradeoff between query latency, recall, deletion time, and memory usage through an extensive collection of experiments.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: ICLR 2026. This version withdraws the claim that linearly many patch edges suffice: the hitting-time guarantee for randomized deletion needs at least as many edge samples as there are edges in the clique over the neighbors of the deleted point. It also adds a missing hypothesis to the hitting-time theorem and corrects the star-mesh step and the edge sparsification lemma

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Deterministic Polynomial-Query Protocol for Envy-Free Cake Cutting
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a deterministic protocol that divides a heterogeneous cake completely and without envy among $n$ agents using $O(n^6\log n)$ Robertson--Webb queries in the worst case. Valuations may be arbitrary nonnegative, nonatomic measures, and bundles may be disconnected. The protocol makes $O(n)$ calls to certified trimming, which uses $O(n^5\log n)$ queries on $n$ pieces. In a certified trim, each agent receives the end part, or suffix, of a different piece without envy, and every shortened piece has a witness tie leading back to a whole piece. At each step, the witness values the shortened suffix exactly as much as her own. For pieces of positive interval length with strictly increasing suffix values, the retained suffix lengths are unique, although their holders may differ. Candidate assignments share a table of value and cut queries. If the coordinatewise median of their value estimates fails a matching test, the test identifies an agent whose value is underestimated, ruling out at least half the remaining assignments. A weighted median of cut marks lets one repair step remove a small envy while allocating almost all of the residue. For complete envy-free chore allocation, the query bound is $O(n^7\log n)$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Constrained Online Selection with Predictions: Matroid Secretary, Knapsack, and Matching
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study learning-augmented algorithms for constrained online selection problems, including the secretary problem under matroid and knapsack constraints, and the edge-weighted online bipartite matching problem with random vertex arrivals. In each, items arrive in a uniformly random order, and their values are revealed only on arrival. The goal is to select a set of items with nearly maximum total value, subject to the constraints (matroid, knapsack, or matching). In the learning-augmented setting, item value predictions are given in advance. We seek algorithms that are both consistent, in that accurate predictions lead to near-optimal selection, and robust, in that they obtain strong worst-case bounds even when predictions are inaccurate. Building on work of Fujii and Yoshida (2024) on the learning-augmented secretary problem, we study a method that follows the predicted optimum until an item with a large enough prediction error is observed. At that point, it reverts to running a worst-case competitive algorithm. We make a simple but critical modification: the first item with a large prediction error is selected with a carefully chosen probability. With this modification, we prove a general result, showing that if the underlying worst-case algorithm is $α$-competitive for $α\in(0,1]$, this approach achieves competitive ratio $\max\{\fracα{2(1+α)},\frac{1-ε}{1+ε}\}$, where $ε$ is the maximum relative error of any prediction. That is, the algorithm is perfectly consistent, achieving competitive ratio $1$ as $ε\to 0$, and robust up to a constant factor relative to the worst-case baseline. For all three problems we study, $α= 1/e$, and our result is the first to achieve consistency and constant-factor robustness. We hope that our general analysis framework can be applied to other learning-augmented online decision-making problems.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 21 pages

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A characteristic-graph reduction for deterministic L-system inference with classical and quantum-heuristic solvers
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: L-systems are widely used to model and simulate biological growth processes, including plant development. Motivated by the broader goal of automating L-system construction, this paper studies the formal deterministic context-free L-system (D0L-system) inference problem in which the input is a finite, noise-free sequence of strings. We introduce the characteristic graph of a string sequence and prove that the existence of a compatible D0L-system is equivalent to the existence of an independent set of a prescribed size in this graph. This gives polynomial reductions from D0L inference to maximum independent set (MIS) and SAT, and hence an exact classical decision route when combined with an exact MIS or SAT solver. We also describe a Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)-based quantum heuristic for generating candidate independent sets. This heuristic is not a decision procedure for D0L inference, and failure of the heuristic is inconclusive rather than a certificate of nonexistence. We include computational validation on $22$ generated D0L traces and $8$ negative controls, explicitly incorporate known fixed-identity symbols, and report small statevector QAOA simulations. The quantum component is presented as a proof-of-concept candidate generator, not as a claimed quantum speedup; the immediately useful contribution is the characteristic-graph reduction and the exact classical/SAT decision framework it enables.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 26 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables. Published in Research in the Mathematical Sciences (2026)

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Trusted Advice for Scheduling on Unrelated Machines
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Scheduling on unrelated parallel machines under standard objectives, such as makespan minimization or max-min fairness, has posed fundamental theoretical challenges for decades. A prominent example is the longstanding factor 2 approximation barrier for the Min Makespan problem established by Lenstra, Shmoys, and Tardos (1990). We investigate these fundamental challenges within the framework of algorithms with trusted advice. We consider a setting in which a trusted oracle is accessed once and reveals partial but entirely accurate structural information about an optimal solution. This framework allows us to quantify the improvements in approximation guarantees enabled by various trusted advice.
  We formalize a hierarchy of trusted advice oracles, ranging from a strong oracle that reveals the exact assignments of long jobs to a weaker oracle that indicates only which machines process such jobs. By exploiting this information, we obtain approximation guarantees beyond the classical worst-case barriers. In particular, we show that even the weakest oracle improves the approximation ratio for Min Makespan to $\sqrt{3}\approx 1.732$. We also obtain improved ratios of $(\sqrt{33}+1)/4\approx 1.686$ and $(5\sqrt{7})/8 \approx 1.654$ for Restricted Assignment and Graph Balancing, respectively. For the max-min fairness objective, known as the Santa Claus problem, we obtain a 2-approximation using our weak oracle. Finally, we show that these problems remain NP-hard to approximate within certain constant factors even with the trusted advice oracles considered. Interestingly, for the Santa Claus problem, we show a lower bound of 2 which is tight and matches the classical oracle-free bound.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tolerant Testing for Bipartiteness and Unique Games
Tight Query Depth of Recursive Randomized Greedy MIS
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The randomized greedy maximal independent set (RGMIS) algorithm processes vertices in a uniformly random order and greedily constructs an MIS. Its recursive formulation decides whether a vertex belongs to this MIS by querying lower-ranked neighbors in increasing rank order, stopping when a neighbor in the MIS is found. We prove that, on every $n$-vertex graph, this recursive algorithm has $O(\log n)$ query depth with high probability, even without memoization. The bound holds simultaneously for all starting vertices and is asymptotically tight even on bipartite graphs. The proof combines a bound on the total expected number of query paths with an exposure argument: paths with many two-edge shortcuts are unlikely, while the remaining paths admit sufficiently many applications of a two-hop probability bound.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Constant-Factor Single-Sample Prophet Inequality for Subadditive Valuations
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We establish a constant-factor single-sample prophet inequality for online combinatorial allocation with monotone subadditive valuations. Given one independent sample from each buyer's unknown distribution, our reduction converts any offline algorithm achieving an $α$ fraction of optimal welfare into an online algorithm achieving an $α/120$ fraction of the expected offline optimum. The guarantee holds for arbitrary arrival orders and extends to the stronger Game of Googol model. Our approach has two key ingredients: a prior-free random score generator and a new sample-based construction of tentative allocations. The tentative allocations capture substantial welfare while controlling contention for items, and the score generator relates itemwise competition in the tentative allocations to the value of retained bundles. The reduction is efficient whenever its offline allocator and score generator are efficient.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Catalan Hashing: Efficient Linear Probing for Variable-Length Items
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A defining feature of the linear-probing hash table is its spatial locality: at load factor $1 - \varepsilon$, the hash table can be implemented so that each operation scans a single contiguous region of expected size $O(1/\varepsilon)$ (this is known as the \emph{scan cost}). This guarantee, however, relies on all items having unit size. In this paper, we ask whether it is possible to achieve a similar guarantee, but in a hash table that stores items of arbitrary lengths $|x| \ge 1$.
  The main result of the paper is a new hash table called \emph{Catalan hashing}, which supports amortized expected scan cost $O(|x|/\varepsilon)$ for positive queries, $O(1/\varepsilon)$ for negative queries, and $O(|x|\varepsilon^{-1}\log^{1+δ}|x|)$ for insertions/deletions, for any constant $δ> 0$. As a corollary, we obtain the same bounds in the cache-oblivious model, with a scan cost of $S$ translating to $1 + O(S/B)$ I/Os. Along the way, we introduce several high-level techniques that may be of independent interest; this includes a novel way of using erasure codes in order to perform write optimization within a hash table, and a connection to scheduling that allows us to place elements in a way which avoids clustering at high load factors.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: minor updates

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Faster CONGEST Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Weighted Independent Set in Sparse Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We give deterministic distributed CONGEST algorithms for the weighted version of the problem in trees and graphs of bounded arboricity. All weights are nonnegative integers bounded by $n^{O(1)}$.
  For trees and $\log(n)/n<\varepsilon\leq1/8$, we prove that the task of deterministically computing a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate solution to the maximum weight independent set (MWIS) problem has a tight $Θ(\log^*(n)/\varepsilon)$ complexity. The lower bound already holds on unweighted oriented paths. The upper bound holds even for unrooted trees.
  For graphs $G=(V,E)$ of arboricity $β>1$, we give two algorithms. If the sum of all node weights is $w(V)$, we show that for any $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$, an independent set of weight at least $(1-\varepsilon)\cdot\frac{w(V)}{4β}$ can be computed in $O(\log^2(β/\varepsilon)/\varepsilon + \log(β/\varepsilon)\cdot\log^* n)$ rounds. We further show that for any $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$, an independent set of weight at least $(1-\varepsilon)\cdot\frac{w(V)}{2β+1}$ can be computed in $O(\log^3(β)\cdot\log(1/\varepsilon)/\varepsilon^2\cdot\log n)$ rounds. For $\varepsilon=ω(1/\sqrtβ)$, this significantly improves on a recent result of Gil [OPODIS '23], whose algorithm yields a $1/\lfloor(2+\varepsilon)β\rfloor$-approximation in $O(β/\varepsilon\cdot\log n)$ rounds when its accuracy dependence is tracked. As an intermediate step to our result, we design an algorithm to compute an independent set of total weight at least $(1-\varepsilon)\cdot\sum_{v\in V}\frac{w(v)}{°(v)+1}$ in time $O(\log^3(Δ)\cdot\log(1/\varepsilon)/\varepsilon + \log^* n)$, where $Δ$ is the maximum degree of the graph and logarithmic runtime factors are lower-bounded by one.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 30 pages. Revised full version of the OPODIS 2026 paper

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Greedy BPE with Replacement Counts Achieves the Tight Approximation Ratio $(1-e^{-2})/2$
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) builds the tokenisers of many language models by repeatedly merging a most frequent adjacent pair of symbols. Kozma and Voderholzer showed that $k$ greedy merges save, in the worst case, between $1/3$ and $(1-e^{-2})/2 \approx 0.43233$ of what the best $k$ merges save, and asked for the exact constant. We resolve this question for the replacement-count rule they analyse. For every string and weighted word table, every budget $k$, and every tie-breaking rule, greedy saves at least $\frac12(1-(1-2/k)^k)$ of the optimum. This establishes the exact worst-case approximation ratio $(1-e^{-2})/2$, approached as $k\to\infty$ but never attained. The proof is based on a shadow inequality: after $i$ greedy steps, the optimum is at most $2G_i+kg_{i+1}$, where $G_i$ is greedy's saving so far and $g_{i+1}$ its next gain. We also show that the worst-case ratio at budget $k$ exceeds the limiting constant by $Θ(k^{-1/2})$. For the overlapping-count rule used by deployed trainers, we prove a lower bound greater than $0.38954$ and an asymptotic upper bound of approximately $0.40407$; determining its exact constant remains open.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 58 pages. v3 supersedes v2 (0.391 bound), establishing the exact worst-case approximation ratio for replacement-count BPE, a finite-budget convergence result, and bounds for overlapping-count BPE. Code and certificates: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24451469

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: GreedTok Is a 0.3287-Approximation, and Greedy Tokenizers Lose Order $1/\log k$ on Fixed Alphabets
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: A tokenizer's vocabulary is built once and used on every input, so it matters how much compression a greedy construction can lose. We study two greedy constructions: GreedTok (Lim et al., 2025), which adds the string that saves the most tokens, and byte-pair encoding (BPE), which merges a most frequent adjacent pair. We prove that GreedTok saves at least $0.3287$ of the optimal number of tokens saved on every corpus, while no constant above $0.33862$ is possible. The key idea is that, given the order of greedy's choices, the damage inside an optimal token is fixed by two numbers. On a fixed alphabet both algorithms are asymptotically optimal and their worst deficit with budget $k$ has order $1/\log k$: one counting argument gives the upper bound for both, and one binary corpus, whose first greedy commitment erases a boundary between optimal tokens, gives the matching lower bound for both (for GreedTok, on its committed segmentation), even if greedy's continuation may use almost twice the budget. For BPE on one binary string, a forced first merge can cost $Ω(k)$ final tokens, yet $2k+3$ rules always repair it.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 69 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. v2 adds fixed-alphabet results for GreedTok and greedy BPE (deficit of order 1/log k, tight), a binary-string repair theorem for BPE, and an EPTAS for fixed alphabets; the 0.3287 bound is unchanged. Code and checkers: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24451478

Signal Processing.title: Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: The use of one-bit quantized complex-valued data samples enables efficient distributed computation of an array data covariance. This reduced complexity covariance estimate can be used for adaptive beamforming, but requires careful diagonal loading and results in lower performance compared to a full-precision approach. Two main approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built out of complex one-bit data samples, and a ``hybrid'' cross-covariance between the one-bit data and the full precision data. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for the associated population and finite-sample matrices are derived and compared to the full precision results using tools from linear algebra and statistics. Many strong, well-separated interferers with low overlap with the signal of interest are assumed throughout, none of them dominant.

Signal Processing.title: Goal-Oriented Wave Computing for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Programmable metasurfaces are arrays of elements whose electromagnetic response can be tuned electronically. They can process signals as a wave propagates through or reflects off them, an approach known as wave-domain analog computing, or wave computing. The design strategy is typically indirect: the surface is fitted to a prescribed linear operator, such as a discrete Fourier transform (DFT), and the result is read from output power measurements. Using direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation as a canonical benchmark, we study what this indirection costs across three analog computing topologies: reflective reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), beyond-diagonal RIS (BD-RIS), and stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM). We first derive Cramér-Rao bounds for the complete physical estimation chain, including one that accounts for output detectors measuring only intensity. We then formulate a goal-oriented alternative where the surfaces are trained directly through the deployed readout, with no operator target. We observe that goal-oriented training lets sparsely connected or shallower surfaces reach the task performance of their more complex operator-fitted counterparts, despite nearly identical Fisher information. For fully connected BD-RIS and six-layer SIM, the advantage persists under one- and two-bit control. From 16 to 64 elements, the connectivity a beyond-diagonal RIS needs grows with the aperture, and the depth saving of a stacked intelligent metasurface shrinks. Under tuner and per-layer loss, the goal-oriented designs mostly keep their advantage over DFT fits of the same hardware.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. v2: Monte Carlo results re-run with 60,000 trials; corrected quantized-control training and results; loss study with noise at the detectors; clarified scope; small corrections in the text and Table I

Signal Processing.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
Signal Processing.summary: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

Signal Processing.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Heterogeneous federated systems require agents to learn and exchange informative representations despite differences in data distributions, model architectures, and latent dimensionalities. We propose Sheaf-based Federated Representation Learning (SFRL), a framework that jointly learns and aligns heterogeneous latent representations without sharing parameters, labels, or a single latent space. SFRL relates agent-specific latent spaces through learnable orthogonal transformations and isometric embeddings, promoting consistency via a sheaf-Laplacian gluing regularizer evaluated on a shared set of pilot samples. We develop Sheaf-FRL, a decentralized alternating algorithm combining local gradient updates with closed-form Procrustes updates of the alignment maps, and establish convergence guarantees in deterministic and stochastic settings. On collaborative classification with semantic communication across four datasets, under model and data heterogeneity, Sheaf-FRL improves communication accuracy over federated baselines at no cost in private accuracy, and is more robust to latent-space compression.

Signal Processing.title: Enhancing time-frequency resolution with optimal transport and barycentric fusion of multiple spectrogram
Signal Processing.summary: Time-frequency representations, such as the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), are fundamental tools for analyzing non-stationary signals. However, their ability to achieve sharp localization in both time and frequency is inherently limited by the Gabor-Heisenberg uncertainty principle. In this paper, we address this limitation by introducing a method to generate super-resolution spectrograms through the fusion of two or more spectrograms with varying resolutions. Specifically, we compute the super-resolution spectrogram as the barycenter of input spectrograms using optimal transport (OT) divergences. Our method does not require the input spectrograms to share the same time-frequency grid. The input spectrograms can be computed using any STFT parameters, and the resulting super-resolution spectrogram can be defined on an arbitrary user-specified grid. We explore various OT divergences based on different transportation costs. Notably, we introduce a novel transportation cost that preserves time-frequency geometry while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to standard Wasserstein barycenters. We adopt the unbalanced OT framework and derive a new block majorization-minimization algorithm for efficient barycenter computation. We validate the proposed method on controlled synthetic signals and recorded speech using both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The results show that our approach combines the best localization properties of the input spectrograms while maintaining a smooth energy distribution, and preserving computational efficiency.
Signal Processing.comment: main text: 15 pages, 5 figures. supplementary material: 4 pages, 4 figures

Signal Processing.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
Signal Processing.summary: Advancing physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI) requires moving beyond static object recognition to ground how real-world mechanics (e.g., impact, friction, and force transfer) unfold over time. While multimodal aligners seek to capture these interactions by matching multi-sensor streams, prevailing architectures compress each temporal sequence into a single pooled embedding. We show that this paradigm fails on twin events: distinct physical executions recorded under identical task conditions. Collapsing the temporal dimension averages out transient cross-modal dynamics, effectively reducing physical event alignment to static scene recognition. Formally, we prove that as sequence length increases, any temporally pooled representation converges to the stationary recording condition. Consequently, as windows grow, no choice of loss function or embedding geometry can disambiguate twin events from pooled features alone. Instead, we show that physical events are uniquely identified by the event gap, namely the instantaneous, synchronous co-fluctuations across modalities that are erased by pooling and accumulate only along unpooled trajectories. To recover this signal, we introduce CounterPoint, a lightweight plug-in module that strips out each modality's temporal mean to score frame-level cross-modal agreement. Integrated across four state-of-the-art (SOTA) multimodal aligners, CounterPoint shifts representations from coarse condition matching to fine-grained physical event alignment, consistently outperforming existing temporal alignment methods.

Signal Processing.title: A Closed-Loop Thermal Dynamic Model for AI Data Center Cooling Load Simulation
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate modeling and simulation of cooling electricity demand is essential for characterizing AI data center loads, but time-synchronized operational measurements are scarce. Constant coefficient-of-performance models can oversimplify cooling behavior, while detailed thermal state-space models are cumbersome to use. This paper proposes a closed-loop simulation framework that couples a linear thermal dynamic model with deadband-based control to capture nonlinear cooling behaviors. The framework is validated against operational data from the Marconi100 supercomputer. Compared with the baseline, the proposed model reduces the mean absolute error from 95.80 to 23.52 kW and the root-mean-square error from 109.79 to 29.91 kW. The statistical evaluation further shows improved reproduction of daily peak demand and intraday variability. The framework provides a computationally tractable approach to generate physically interpretable cooling load profiles for power system studies.

Signal Processing.title: PPGFlowECG: Latent Rectified Flow with Cross-Modal Encoding for PPG-Guided ECG Generation and Cardiovascular Disease Detection
Signal Processing.summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical gold standard for cardiovascular disease (CVD) assessment, yet continuous monitoring is constrained by the need for dedicated hardware and trained personnel. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearable devices and readily scalable, but it lacks electrophysiological specificity, limiting diagnostic reliability. While generative methods aim to translate PPG into clinically useful ECG signals, existing approaches are limited by the misalignment of physiological semantics in generative models and the complexity of modeling in high-dimensional signals. To address these limitations, we propose PPGFlowECG, a two-stage framework that aligns PPG and ECG in a shared latent space using the CardioAlign Encoder and then synthesizes ECGs with latent rectified flow. We further provide a formal analysis of this coupling, showing that the CardioAlign Encoder is necessary to guarantee stable and semantically consistent ECG synthesis under our formulation. Extensive experiments on four datasets demonstrate improved synthesis fidelity and downstream diagnostic utility. These results indicate that PPGFlowECG supports scalable, wearable-first CVD screening when standard ECG acquisition is unavailable.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at IEEE ICDM 2026 and awarded the Best Paper Award (Applied Track)

Signal Processing.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
Signal Processing.summary: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.

Signal Processing.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
Signal Processing.summary: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.

Signal Processing.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
Signal Processing.summary: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

Signal Processing.title: Timestep Selection in Diffusion-Based OTFS Channel Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Diffusion-based channel estimators are run with a few deterministic sampling steps, and their step count is treated as a knob that trades accuracy against latency. We show that for the mean squared error this trade-off mainly comes from the default leading timestep spacing, whose first timestep indicates an intermediate noise level although the initial state is pure noise. In a multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time frequency space receiver with ray-traced paths and per-path Doppler shifts, moving only the first timestep of the default spacing to the pure-noise end recovers the gain of trailing spacing, completely for our anchored residual estimator and mostly for a published diffusion estimator. With trailing spacing one to three steps give the most accurate single trajectory of our estimator at every signal-to-noise ratio we test, and longer trajectories raise the error, by 0.34~dB over one step at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20~dB after 50 steps. This is the direction predicted by an idealized analysis in which a long deterministic trajectory turns the posterior mean into a posterior sample. With three trailing steps, the published estimator reaches 0.8 to 1.8~dB lower normalized mean squared error than with its original five leading steps, on its own trained network and test set. A start rule that places the first timestep from the error power of the linear anchor of the estimator, with one threshold per network, recovers trailing spacing for our estimator and matches start timesteps tuned separately for every signal-to-noise ratio on a noise-prediction network. A regression network with the same architecture and data reaches 0.23 to 1.36~dB lower normalized mean squared error than the best diffusion configuration we evaluate. The step count of a diffusion channel estimator should therefore be judged only after its first timestep is fixed.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Code available at https://github.com/tellsgo/otfs-timestep-selection

Signal Processing.title: Asynchronous Uplink Multi-UE Networked Sensing via Multipath Correlation
Signal Processing.summary: Multiuser uplink sensing offers a promising paradigm for networked sensing by leveraging signals from multiple user equipment (UEs) to enhance sensing coverage and performance. This paper investigates asynchronous multiuser uplink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access sensing by exploiting correlated multipath structures across UEs. A common frontend first mitigates the dominant timing offsets (TOs), carrier-frequency offsets (CFOs), and phase offsets (POs) through LoS-referencing and constructs a reduced delay-angle-of-arrival (AoA) search space. Two alternative multiuser sensing estimators are then proposed, with different mechanisms of explicitly and implicitly exploiting UE correlation, respectively. The first explicitly adopts a latent-group shared-private sparse Bayesian learning (Group-SBL) model to exploit group-shared propagation structures while accommodating UE-specific components. The second combines calibrated multiuser observations for joint multiple signal classification (MUSIC) processing, recovering a global delay-AoA pool that can be further associated with individual UEs. Residual-TO refinement is conducted with both estimator updates, followed by local-grid delay-AoA refinement and residual common-phase compensation before Doppler estimation. Simulations under a 5G New Radio-compatible uplink configuration show that both multiuser schemes outperform their corresponding per-UE baselines, with larger gains as cross-UE propagation correlation increases.

Signal Processing.title: Implicit Neural Representation for 3D Radio Map Compression in Low-Altitude Environments
Signal Processing.summary: Low-altitude wireless networks require accurate 3D radio maps (RMs) to support environment-aware communication. However, due to the extensive spatial coverage and multi-modal channel representations, 3D RMs usually incur prohibitive storage and transmission overhead, making efficient compression highly desirable. In this paper, we propose NeRM3D, an implicit neural representation (INR)-based framework for compact 3D RM compression. Specifically, NeRM3D represents the entire 3D RM as a lightweight neural network that maps discrete height values to corresponding RM slices, thereby encoding the RM into a compact neural network. To effectively model the volumetric spatial structure of 3D RMs, NeRM3D jointly integrates horizontal embeddings with height-aware modulation, enabling efficient extraction and fusion of spatial correlations across different vertical layers and channel modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that NeRM3D achieves competitive compression performance with low complexity and decoding latency, making it suitable for resource-constrained devices.

Signal Processing.title: Angular characteristics of attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by single deciduous bush in winter conditions at FR2 band
Signal Processing.summary: Vegetation-induced attenuation and temporal dispersion remain important impairments in millimeter-wave radio propagation, particularly in the frequency range 2 (FR2) band, where highly directional links are employed. Existing vegetation attenuation models, including ITU-R P.833, predominantly address scenarios involving trees or vegetation clusters and are typically derived for the main radiation direction of the transmitting antenna. This paper presents an experimental study of angular-dependent attenuation and temporal dispersion introduced by a single deciduous bush under winter conditions. Measurements were conducted on a university campus at 28 GHz and 38 GHz using a wideband channel-sounding testbed operating from 1 MHz to 44 GHz. The bush, approximately 3 m in height, was located at the center of a circular measurement trajectory with a radius of 10 m, along which the receiver was positioned at angular intervals of approximately 8 deg. Directional antennas with 7-9 deg half-power beamwidth were employed, and reception angles from 0 to 200 deg relative to the transmitter-bush axis were investigated. The results demonstrate significant angular variability in both excess attenuation and temporal dispersion, indicating substantial contributions from scattering outside the main propagation direction. Differences between the two carrier frequencies are analyzed, highlighting frequency-dependent attenuation mechanisms even in leaf-off conditions. The presented findings extend existing single-vegetation models by incorporating angular characteristics and temporal effects, providing valuable insights for the design and modeling of FR2 wireless links in sparse-vegetation environments.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables, 4 equations

Signal Processing.title: Combining Physical Layer Security and Symmetric Encryption to Secure Rate-Splitting Multiple Access
Signal Processing.summary: The demand for increased spectral efficiency (SE) in downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems has led to the development of various multiple access techniques. Among these, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) can improve SE over space division multiple access (SDMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by splitting each user's data into common and private parts. The common parts from all users are then encoded into a single common message, which is transmitted alongside the private messages using an RSMA-specific precoder. Recent results showed that the precoder can be modified to enable physical layer security (PLS) by integrating secrecy rate constraints into the design. However, this approach only secures the private messages, while the common part of each user remains unprotected. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid-PLS RSMA scheme that symmetrically encrypts all user data and embeds key information within the PLS-secured private messages. Additionally, the RSMA precoder is adapted to ensure that the private messages are sufficiently sized to carry the key information. The precoder design is formulated as a non-convex SE maximization problem and solved using successive convex approximation (SCA). Analytical and numerical evaluations demonstrate that the proposed hybrid-PLS RSMA can significantly improve SE compared to partially secure RSMA and secure SDMA, when complete user data security is required.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 algorithm

Signal Processing.title: Safety-Tiered ISAC Scheduling with History-Aware Value of Information for V2X Networks
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) assisted vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks prioritize safety-critical radar sensing over communication. However, existing scheduling methods overlook the varying criticality of vehicles, long-term fairness in service quality, and information staleness. Considering this, we propose a low-complexity sensing-prioritized allocation for radar and communication (SPARC-V) to maximize the value of information (VoI) in V2X networks. SPARC-V addresses these challenges with a two-stage hierarchical resource scheduling framework. For sensing, vehicles are first categorized into safety tiers based on a risk metric. Safety-critical vehicles receive orthogonal resources, while others can reuse resources under specific constraints. Sensing resources are allocated based on a sensing priority metric that balances safety significance and long-term fairness. In the next stage, communication resources are allocated to vehicles with the most outdated information. Performance is measured using a unified VoI metric that considers sensing quality, safety relevance, and information freshness. Monte Carlo simulations show that SPARC-V achieves the highest network VoI of 26.5 among all baselines, with its advantage over baselines widening as vehicle density increases.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE 1st Annual Integrated Sensing and Communication Conference (ISAC) in the current form, Lisbon, 16-18 Nov. 2026. 6 pages and 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: Inferring behind-the-meter demand components from net load via inverse optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Understanding and forecasting electricity demand responses to price signals is essential to support the operational decisions of system operators, retailers, and regulators. Traditional time series and machine learning approaches have performed well under stable consumption patterns. However, the rise of active consumers with flexible assets, such as solar-plus-storage systems and electric vehicles, introduces new complexities. These consumers exhibit behind-the-meter behavior that is generally unobservable to system operators and retailers, who can typically only measure net demand at the boundary meters which are located at the connection points to the grid. Net demand reflects the aggregate of baseload consumption, flexible load shifting, and self-generation, all of which may respond nonlinearly to market prices. As these unobservable components grow, existing forecasting models may fail to capture the true dynamics of consumer behavior. This work develops and implements a data-driven inverse optimization framework to reveal behind-the-meter consumption patterns using only net demand data. By analyzing net demand as revealed at the grid connection point, we estimate parameters for a latent optimization model, enabling predictions that infer the unobservable components. This enables more accurate point and probabilistic forecasting of electricity demand under varying price signals. Thus, it provides actionable insights for system operators to improve local congestion management and flexibility extraction, as well as for retailers and aggregators, who could thereby optimize operations and tariffs to leverage consumer flexibility. We validate the methodology using real-world data, demonstrating improved forecasting accuracy over leading machine learning and time-series benchmarks.

Signal Processing.title: Probabilistic Risk Sensitivity and Loss Aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops a binary-gamble framework for characterizing risk sensitivity and loss aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). The proposed probabilistic risk-sensitivity metric is defined as a probability-threshold ratio that determines acceptance and preference thresholds in choice problems involving either a certain outcome and a binary gamble or two binary gambles. We show how standard notions of symmetric and non-symmetric bet aversion can be recovered within this framework, and we compare the resulting threshold-based conditions with utility premia, probability premia, and Arrow-Pratt curvature measures. The analysis clarifies when these criteria coincide and when they diverge, particularly for increasing aversion conditions, binary gambles with unequal probability distributions, and settings involving probability weighting functions. We also identify technical restrictions that arise when CPT-utility functions are used to represent loss aversion at the reference point. The resulting framework provides a decision-theoretic interpretation of risk sensitivity that is directly tied to probability thresholds and complements existing premium-based approaches.
Signal Processing.comment: This paper has been submitted for publication

Signal Processing.title: Dynamic Channel Gain Map Reconstruction via Object-Attached Gaussian Propagation
Signal Processing.summary: Channel gain maps describe location-dependent propagation, but moving vehicles can change reception beyond their physical footprints. Reconstructing these changes requires connecting local object states to regional power. We consider a fixed transmitter and predefined receiver areas, with historical static and dynamic radio supervision and continuing delayed, noisy vehicle-state messages. We propose OA-GS, an object-attached Gaussian propagation model with a shared area correction. Each vehicle carries anisotropic kernels whose effective attributes are supplied by offline-calibrated templates and affine condition generators. Closed-form Gaussian integrals along finite propagation segments evaluate an effective attenuation model, while directional scattering terms account for additional power. These interactions modulate a learned static reference and contribute to regional channel gain. A shared multilayer perceptron then uses object, propagation, and receiver-area features to predict a bounded path-loss residual that compensates for errors in the compact propagation model. All learned parameters remain fixed during deployment, and reconstruction uses arrived vehicle messages without current-traffic radio measurements. In a fixed-scene ray-tracing study over four development traffic sequences and three initializations, OA-GS reduces map and strong-event dynamic-response root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) from 2.503 to 1.272 dB and from 5.965 to 3.563 dB, respectively, relative to a task-adapted GS-CG baseline receiving eight initial radio reports. The shared correction reduces strong-event dynamic-response error from 3.962 to 3.563 dB under the same propagation backbone, demonstrating the benefit of combining explicit propagation structure with learned regional correction.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table

Signal Processing.title: Deep-Learning-Based Classiffcation of Relay-Surface Scattering Regimes for NLOS Millimeter-Wave Sensing
Signal Processing.summary: In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) millimeter-wave sensing, relay-surface scattering alters target echoes and can cause propagation-model mismatch, angle-estimation errors, and ghost targets. DEKL, a deep-learning framework, identifies the dominant scattering regime from radar echoes without measuring surface roughness. Multipath echo models describe specular reflection, structured multipath reflection, and diffuse scattering. These models and a no-target hypothesis define a model-selection problem with unknown parameters. The Kullback-Leibler information criterion yields an adaptive decision rule for selecting among these hypotheses. A lightweight network, KLNet, learns covariance-domain features and combines attention with confidence-gated iterative decoding to avoid repeated likelihood evaluation. Analytical simulations, independent electromagnetic simulations, and radar measurements show that DEKL improves discrimination over the evaluated information-criterion-based rules. Ablations show how attention, confidence supervision, and gated decoding contribute to selective prediction and robustness under controlled covariance perturbations. The predicted regime guides propagation-model selection for radio-environment repre-sentations in wireless-network digital twins and informs NLOS localization and imaging.
Signal Processing.comment: 15 pages, 13 figures, Submitted to IEEE Journal on Multiscale and Multiphysics Computational Techniques (J-MMCT)

Signal Processing.title: Reciprocal Range-Doppler Estimation with Partial Path Association for Asynchronous Bistatic OFDM-ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: In bistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), clock asynchronism shifts the delay and Doppler measured from orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) echoes. The two stations may see different reflectors, so the receiver must identify which echoes belong to the same path before combining the two views. For partial path association, PreVote finds a common displacement in the directional delay and Doppler differences. One-to-one assignment at this displacement accepts compatible pairs and allows other paths to remain unmatched. Each station uses coherent compression to form a subcarrier vector and a slow-time vector per path. For range-Doppler estimation in reciprocal sensing, the center multiplies paired vectors without conjugation. The opposite constant clock terms cancel, and a correct pair yields twice the physical phase slopes of one path. A Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) for fixed identities and phase branches quantifies the shared clock uncertainty. At the higher signal-to-noise ratios tested, reciprocal fusion yields lower range and Doppler errors than both receivers using calibrated echoes. Under partial visibility, displacement-based matching recovers more targets with correct identities and prescribed accuracy than separate centering with the same fusion stage. Balancing directional energy and extending the common aperture improve Doppler accuracy, while carrier frequency variation increases error.

Signal Processing.title: UV3CP: Universal ViT-Based 3D Channel Predictor for MIMO-OFDM Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Channel aging in time-division duplex multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems causes a mismatch between uplink-based channel state information and the downlink channel at the transmission instant. Although vision transformers (ViTs) are effective for channel prediction, their performance is highly sensitive to the patch size, whose optimum depends on the channel coherence region. Moreover, changing the patch size typically requires retraining because it alters the token grid and patch embedding operator. In this paper, we propose a universal ViT-based 3D channel prediction framework, called UV3CP, for MIMO-OFDM systems. The proposed UV3CP employs an efficient 3D ViT backbone to capture frequency, time, and spatial channel dependencies. First, based on second-order channel statistics, we derive a statistics-aware patch-size selection rule that selects axis-wise patch lengths using a mean-squared-error-based criterion, thereby matching the tokenization granularity to the dominant channel coherence while controlling token length and complexity. Second, we develop a statistics-aware patch-embedding resizing method that enables a single shared UV3CP to operate across different patch sizes without patch-size-specific retraining. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves robustness under various scenarios and patch-size mismatch while reducing the need to train and store multiple patch-size-specific ViT models.

Signal Processing.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
Signal Processing.summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.
Signal Processing.comment: Previously this version appeared as arXiv:2611.17654 which was submitted as a new work by accident

Signal Processing.title: MIMO Integrated Sensing and Communications: A Fisher-based Local Mutual Information Approach
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) beamforming requires a sensing utility that is compatible with the communication rate and aligned with per-target angle estimation. Fisher information (FI)/Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) criteria depend on the angular units and generally involve coupled multi-target matrices, whereas sensing mutual information (SMI) is typically defined on aggregate response variables. This paper proposes Fisher-based local mutual information (F-LMI), a prior-aware bit-domain utility for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) ISAC. F-LMI linearizes each target-specific range-compressed statistic around the angular prior mean and yields a closed-form local information gain. In the single-target case, it admits a Bayesian CRB (BCRB) log-ratio interpretation and is a locally consistent surrogate for the nonlinear parameter MI. For multiple targets, the prior-induced variations of the non-intended targets are marginalized into a beamformer-dependent interference-plus-noise covariance in each branch. We derive a fractional-programming algorithm with linear-system updates and scalar bisection. Monte Carlo simulations with nonlinear target-wise posterior-mean receivers show that F-LMI reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 5.0--14.7\% relative to a target-indexed Bayesian-bound baseline at two matched rates in a closely spaced layout. Under a common basis-selection protocol, it also attains lower branch RMSE than aggregate and joint criteria.

Signal Processing.title: PsyDrift: Healthy-Reference Latent Diffusion for Anomaly Scoring in Autism Spectrum Disorder
Signal Processing.summary: Individual heterogeneity and acquisition-site variability complicate neuroimaging-based characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We propose PsyDrift, combining ASD/healthy-control-supervised functional-connectivity representations with healthy-reference latent diffusion. An encoder produces 128-dimensional representations, and a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) learns exclusively from healthy training latents. Distance from a diffusion-denoised reconstruction provides a continuous deviation score. We evaluate 1,102 subjects from all 20 ABIDE-I sites using five-seed leave-one-site-out cross-validation. The classifier and DDPM achieve mean-site AUROCs of $0.798 \pm 0.003$ and $0.718 \pm 0.013$, respectively; uncertainties denote seed standard deviations. Matched healthy-reference scorers on the same representation achieve 0.68-0.71; the statistical significance of diffusion's modest numerical advantage remains unestablished. Within ASD, scores show weak associations with ADOS Total (Spearman $ρ= 0.108$, $p = 0.038$) and full-scale IQ ($ρ= -0.138$, $p = 0.002$), without adjustment for age, sex, site, or head motion. Frozen evaluation without retraining or hyperparameter adaptation yields pooled AUROCs of 0.69 on ABIDE-II and 0.61 on ADHD-200, providing preliminary evidence of cross-cohort and cross-disorder transfer. These results demonstrate healthy-reference deviation scoring within an ASD-supervised representation; incremental predictive and clinical value remains unestablished.
Signal Processing.comment: Extended version of a paper accepted at the CVPath-Vision4Neuro Workshop at WACV 2027. Includes expanded related-work and future-work discussion

Signal Processing.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
Signal Processing.summary: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment. We release an open dataset of raw IR-UWB measurements collected by a ceiling-mounted radar from 44 participants during scripted activity sequences in 12 layouts across two bedrooms. Using a statistically guided, staged search, we independently tune each representation across five processing and deployment settings. We then compare individual and fused performance under layout and room shifts and quantify computational cost. Across over 1{,}000 cross-validated models, independent tuning proves essential, as optimal processing differs per representation and processing choices shift macro-F1 by up to 26 points, four times the gap between representations. Once tuned, the range-Doppler map leads for unseen layouts (85.1\% macro-F1), while time-Doppler map does for unseen rooms (72.7\%). Fusing all three maps raises these scores to 89.1\% and 80.0\%, respectively. Lower sampling rates and narrower Doppler bands reduce latency by 38--51\% with at most a 1.5-point macro-F1 loss. The best representation for UWB HAR is therefore a deployment decision, not a fixed property.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to IEEE Access

Signal Processing.title: SA-GLRT-D: Sidelobe-Aware GLRT-Based Detector for FMCW Radar
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates adaptive detection for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar in multi-target complex scenarios, where reference-cell contamination, spectral leakage from the cell under test (CUT), and the resulting sidelobe interference severely degrade detection performance. A sidelobe-aware detector based on the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT), termed SA-GLRT-D, is proposed. Unlike conventional filtering-then-constant false alarm rate (CFAR) schemes, the proposed method explicitly accounts for the non-ideal frequency-domain energy spreading of the CUT induced by the finite-window effect. Accordingly, conventional single-cell target detection is extended to local-region detection, and decision statistic construction, CUT-related parameter estimation, and sidelobe interference suppression are jointly accomplished within a unified hypothesis-testing framework. Furthermore, to reduce computational complexity, a fast implementation of SA-GLRT-D is developed, together with a dedicated parameter initialization strategy to enhance the stability of numerical optimization. Simulation and real-measurement results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high-accuracy target detection while maintaining a constant false alarm rate, with favorable computational efficiency.

Signal Processing.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
Signal Processing.summary: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.
Signal Processing.comment: Following further technical review, the authors identified modeling assumptions regarding beam occupancy and interference that require additional validation. We therefore request withdrawal of the current version to reassess the airspace channel capacity analysis and associated numerical results

Signal Processing.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
Signal Processing.summary: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder-based network is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.
Signal Processing.comment: 25 pages, 9 figures, 14 tables. v3: second revised version after peer review; spectra of the denoised signals added, low-pass reference revised, code and data availability added. Submitted to the Journal of the Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering (Springer)

Signal Processing.title: Algebraic Diversity: Group-Theoretic Spectral Estimation from Single Observations
Signal Processing.summary: We establish that temporal averaging over multiple observations is the degenerate case of algebraic group action with the trivial group $G=\{e\}$. A General Replacement Theorem proves that, under signal equivariance and noise ergodicity, a group-averaged estimator from one snapshot achieves equivalent subspace decomposition to multi-snapshot covariance estimation. The Trivial Group Embedding Theorem proves that the sample covariance is the accumulation of trivial-group estimates, with variance governed by a $(G,L)$ continuum as $1/(d_{\mathrm{eff}}\cdot L)$, where $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective dimension of the group average. For group-matched signals the processing gain is up to $10\log_{10}(M)$ dB, the classical beamforming gain, showing that this gain is set by the matched group and not by sensor count. The DFT, DCT, and KLT are unified as group-matched special cases. We conjecture a General Algebraic Averaging Theorem extending these results to arbitrary statistics, with variance governed by $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Monte Carlo experiments on the first four sample moments are consistent with the conjecture in the scalar case. The framework exploits the structure of information (representation-theoretic symmetry of the data object) rather than the content, complementing Shannon's theory. Four applications are demonstrated: single-snapshot MUSIC, massive MIMO, single-pulse waveform classification, and graph signal processing. Earlier quantitative claims on transformer LLMs are retracted. Techniques for blind group matching are described.
Signal Processing.comment: 44 pages, 20 figures. v3: retracted six transformer findings (Sec. 11) due to error in spectral concentration metric; remark on orbit-structure bias in psi. v4: new blind group matching result. v5: updated metrics. v6: new MLE theorem, Nitzberg citation. v7: "group gain" update. v8: corrected Permutation Commutator Formula, Automorphism Theorem condition, effective-dimension bound, DCT group

Signal Processing.title: FL-CsLoc-DH: A Federated Learning-Based Crowdsensing Localization under Dual Heterogeneity
Signal Processing.summary: Mobile Crowdsensing (MCS) provides a scalable way to collect indoor fingerprints and reduce professional calibration effort. To protect the location privacy of participating clients, Federated Learning (FL) is used so that raw fingerprints and measurement trajectories remain local. However, owing to the open and uncontrollable nature of MCS, participating clients collect fingerprints in different propagation environments and possess unequal labeling availability. These conditions jointly cause data and annotation heterogeneity, which degrades FL-based crowdsensing localization. In this work, we propose FL-CsLoc-DH, a federated semi-supervised learning framework for crowdsensing localization under dual heterogeneity. FL-CsLoc-DH coordinates Two-Stage Noisy Gradient Rejection (TS-NGR), Soft Fisher Confidence Alignment (S-FCA), and Trajectory-Smoothed Model Averaging (T-SMA) throughout localization model learning. TS-NGR suppresses unreliable client updates caused jointly by environment dependent data shifts and noisy pseudo labels. S-FCA limits parameter increments dominated by unlabeled data, thereby alleviating annotation heterogeneity during local training. T-SMA smooths the aggregated global localization model trajectory to reduce drift induced by data heterogeneity. Experiment results show that the three mechanisms provide complementary improvements in localization accuracy under the MCS environment while retaining raw client data locally.

Signal Processing.title: Algebraic Diversity: Principles of a Group-Theoretic Approach to Signal Processing
Signal Processing.summary: We present principles of algebraic diversity (AD), a group-theoretic approach to signal processing exploiting signal symmetry to extract more information per observation, complementing classical methods that use temporal and spatial diversity. The transformations under which a signal's statistics are invariant form a matched group; this group determines the natural transform for analysis, and averaging an estimator over the group action reduces variance without requiring additional snapshots. The viewpoint is broadened in five directions beyond the single-observation measurement of a companion paper. Rank promotion admits AD on scalar data streams and identifies the law of large numbers as the trivial-group case of a $(G, L)$ continuum combining sample-count with group-orbit averaging. An eigentensor hierarchy handles signals with nested symmetry. A blind group-matching methodology proposes matched groups from data via a polynomial-time generalized eigenvalue problem on the unitary Lie algebra, placing the DFT, DCT, and Karhunen--Loève transforms as distinguished points on a transform manifold. A cost-symmetry matching principle then extends AD from measurement to blind and adaptive signal processing generally; blind equalization is given as a detailed example, with the Constant Modulus Algorithm's residual phase ambiguity predicted analytically and matched within two degrees on 3GPP TDL multipath channels, and other blind problems in signal processing are mapped into the framework. Four theorems formalize a structural capacity $κ$, the Rényi-2 analog of Shannon and von Neumann's Rényi-1 entropies, quantifying how a signal's information is organized rather than how much information it contains. AD is related to prior work in invariant estimation, minimax robust estimation, algebraic signal processing, and compressed sensing.
Signal Processing.comment: v2: updated blind group matching results for the non-Abelian case; v3: corrected $κ$ inconsistency, added 1973 Hill citation v4: updated blind group matching results; v5: clarified metrics, new metric added; v6: "group gain" clarified; v7: corrected $κ$ definition, DCT group, and commutator formula scope

Signal Processing.title: A concave-convex approach to bit depth allocation for linear MMSE estimation in wireless sensor networks with correlated noise
Signal Processing.summary: Nodes in a wireless sensor network (WSN) are generally powered by batteries, and therefore energy efficiency is crucial. The bit depth used to quantize the sensor signal samples heavily influences energy consumption, as it strongly impacts the amount of information to be transmitted between the sensor nodes. Bit depth allocation problems seek to assign a bit depth to each sensor signal to optimize network resources, such as energy or bandwidth, together with algorithmic performance. We study a general bit depth allocation problem for linear minimum mean squared error (MMSE) estimation in WSNs with spatially correlated noise and a communication energy model depending linearly on the sensor bit depths. This model follows from common configurations in digital communications with orthogonal multiple-access schemes. After relaxation to real variables, we formulate the resulting non-convex problem as a difference of convex (DC) problem, and develop an algorithm based on the concave-convex procedure (CCP) to find a local optimum. We show that the convex problem involved in each CCP iteration can be efficiently solved with a worst-case complexity that is linear in the number of sensors. Additionally, we show that our approach is more computationally efficient than previously proposed bit depth allocation algorithms and generic optimization methods, and it achieves significant energy savings.
Signal Processing.comment: 16 pages double column, 10 figures
