Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Multi-Path TSP and Ordered TSP
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In Multi-Path TSP, given a metric and $k$ pairs of vertices $(s_i,t_i)$, where $k$ is part of the input, we seek $s_i$--$t_i$ paths of minimum total length that together visit all vertices. Ratios below $2$ were known only for graphic metrics and special cases such as multiple depots ($s_i=t_i$); in general metrics, the best ratio was $1+2e^{-1/2}\approx2.213$, by a randomized algorithm of Böhm, Friggstad, Mömke and Spoerhase [SODA 2025]. We give a deterministic algorithm with ratio $\frac{5e-2}{3e-2}<1.8833$ relative to a restriction of their LP relaxation, bounding its integrality gap by the same constant. For Ordered TSP, where a tour must visit $k$ given vertices in a prescribed cyclic order, we compute tours within $1+\frac{e}{2(e-1)}<1.7910$ times the value of the LP relaxation of Armbruster, Mnich and Nägele [APPROX 2024], improving $\frac32+\frac1e\approx1.868$ on both the ratio and the integrality gap. Our algorithms sample a tree for every pair (for Ordered TSP, every two consecutive given vertices) from an LP solution, but keep only the path between the two endpoints. Our main lemma shows that, for arbitrary nonnegative edge weights, a cheapest forest connecting all vertices to these paths has expected weight at most $1/e$ times that of a cheapest forest rooted at the endpoints plus $(1-1/e)$ times the expected weight of the discarded branches. For Multi-Path TSP, we use the weights of a primal--dual growth process that Zhao, Liu and Xiao [arXiv 2026] designed for multiple depots; in these weights, the connecting forest also pays for part of correcting its degree parities.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tight Bounds for Distance-Unbiased Sorting
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study elitist randomized local search for sorting permutations. In this model, each iteration considers a possible exchange of two positions. The entries are exchanged if and only if they are in the wrong order. We introduce \emph{distance-unbiased} selection rules, which may choose an arbitrary distribution over exchange distances but sample uniformly among all pairs at each chosen distance. For static rules, we prove that the optimal worst-case high-probability runtime is $Θ(n(\log n)^2)$. This establishes the asymptotic optimality of the harmonic sorter within this class and partially resolves an open question of Olesker-Taylor. We then allow the distance distribution to change either according to a predetermined schedule or adaptively using the current permutation and the entire history. Matching upper and lower bounds show that both classes have optimal runtime $Θ(n(\log n)^2/\log\log n)$. Thus, scheduled adjustments of the distance distribution improve the optimal static worst-case runtime by a factor of $Θ(\log\log n)$, while full-information adaptation provides no further asymptotic improvement.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Submitted to EvoCOP 2027

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tight Bounds for $(1+ε)$-Approximation for Minimum Spanning Trees in Doubling Metrics
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The minimum spanning tree (MST) problem is one of the most basic optimization problems on metric spaces and graphs. We study the problem of computing a $(1+ε)$-approximation to the MST of an $n$-point metric space of doubling dimension $\mathrm{ddim}$. In doubling metrics, previous deterministic algorithms incur a running time with dependence $ε^{-O(\mathrm{ddim})}$.
  We give a deterministic algorithm that computes a $(1+ε)$-approximate MST in time $$ O_{\mathrm{ddim}}\left(n\log n+ \min\left\{n^2,\frac{n}ε\log(1/ε)\right\}\right) $$ in the standard real RAM model with a unit-cost exact-distance oracle. For bounded doubling dimension, this improves the previous dependence on $ε$ to essentially linear in $ε^{-1}$. We complement this algorithm with a lower bound of $$ Ω\!\left(n\log n+ \min\left\{n^2,\frac{n}ε\log(1/ε)\right\}\right) $$ on running time in the same model, already for metrics of doubling dimension at most seven, showing that our running time is essentially tight.
  For points in $\mathbb R^d$ with $d = O(1)$, exploiting Euclidean geometry allows us to further improve the dependence on $ε$. We obtain a $(1+ε)$-approximate MST in expected time $$ O_d\left( n \log n + \min\left\{n^2, \frac{n}{ε^{1 - β_d}} \log^{1-β_d}(1/ε) \right\} \right) $$ for some $β_d=Θ(1/d)$, improving the accuracy-dependent term $nε^{-2}\log^2(1/ε)$ of Arya and Mount [SODA'16].
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: v2: Updated version with corrected citations v3: Improved running time for MST in doubling metrics, new upper bound for MST in Euclidean spaces, and lower bounds for MST in doubling metrics v4: Added references on WSPC

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Two Rounds Are Already Hard for Loop-Free Updates of Routing Trees
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Updating a routing tree can create loops even when the old and new trees lead to the same destination. A controller chooses which routers update in each round, but their updates may finish in any order. Strong loop freedom therefore requires every partial completion to be acyclic. We show that deciding whether two rounds suffice is NP-complete, even when a safe three-round schedule is supplied. The proof is a linear-size reduction from 3-SAT with one old clause spine and four routers per variable. Three types of mixed cycles enforce consistent literal choices and clause satisfaction. For every nonempty input formula, the constructed instance needs exactly two rounds if the formula is satisfiable and exactly three otherwise.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: An $n^{1/O(\log^* n)}$ Lower Bound for Online Coloring of $k$-Colorable Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In online coloring, the vertices of a graph arrive one at a time with their edges to earlier vertices, and each vertex must be colored irrevocably on arrival. For graphs promised to be $k$-colorable, with $k\ge 3$ fixed, the best deterministic algorithms use $n^{1-Θ(1/k^2)}$ colors, while the best lower bound was Vishwanathan's $Ω(\log^{k-1}n)$ from 1990 until Li recently proved $2^{Ω((\log n)^{1/3}(\log\log n)^{2/3})}$. For every fixed $k\ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we prove a lower bound of $n^{1/(\log^*n+3)}$ colors for deterministic online algorithms on $n$-vertex $k$-colorable graphs, and the same lower bound in expectation for randomized online algorithms. Both bounds hold on a single triangle-free $3$-colorable graph: even an algorithm that is shown this graph in advance, but is not told which of its vertices each arriving vertex is, can be forced to use this many colors by a suitable arrival order. The hard instances are iterated blow-ups of a clique, in which every vertex becomes a block of independent vertices and every edge a private server in the earlier block; each blow-up keeps the forced colors and replaces the chromatic number $χ$ by about $\logχ$, so about $\log^*n$ blow-ups bring it down to $k$. We also show that deterministic lower bounds for different values of $k\ge 3$ are polynomially equivalent, and that no adversary presenting such iterated blow-ups can force more than $n^{1/(\log^*n-O(1))}$ colors. All numbered results are formalized in Lean 4.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 45 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Lean 4 formalization and reproduction material: https://github.com/sfmqrb/lean-verifications-k-colorable

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Bounds for Directed SSSP in Sparse and Intermediate-Density Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a deterministic algorithm for exact single-source shortest paths (SSSP) in directed graphs with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges, and nonnegative real edge weights. When $m=O(n)$, it runs in $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4})$ time. For $m=Θ(n)$, this lowers the exponent of $\log\log n$ in the bound of Duan, Mao, Shu and Yin from $1/2$ to $1/4$. At intermediate densities, writing $d=m/n$, the same algorithm improves on the bound of Duan et al. when $d\geq 3$ and $d\log(2+d)=o(\log\log n)$. For example, when $m=Θ(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$, it runs in $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{5/8})$ time, lowering their exponent from $3/4$ to $5/8$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 61 pages. Clarified Lemma 3.1 and the algorithmic notation, streamlined the presentation, and updated comparisons with prior bounds. Main bounds unchanged

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Faster Directed SSSP on Digraphs with Random Sparse Supports or Few DFS Exceptions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study exact single-source shortest paths (SSSP) in directed graphs with $n$ vertices, $m$ arcs and nonnegative real weights, in the comparison-addition model. This paper continues our earlier work, which gave a deterministic algorithm that takes $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4})$ time when $m=O(n)$ and $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{5/8})$ time when $m=Θ(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$. Our two deterministic algorithms compute the distances on every input and take $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ time on two families of inputs, one per density. The support of an input is its underlying simple undirected graph. When $m=O(n)$, the first algorithm takes $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ time if no two simple cycles of the support with fewer than $P$ vertices share a vertex, where $P=Θ(\sqrt{\log n})$ depends only on the support. For fixed $c>0$, a uniformly random graph with $n$ vertices and $\lfloor cn\rfloor$ edges has this property with probability at least $1-n^{-1+o(1)}$, and the bound then holds for every choice of one or both directions of each edge, all weights and every source. The second family is defined through the depth-first search tree of the support that starts at the source and visits neighbours in identifier order. For fixed $k\ge1$, call a set $Y$ of exceptional vertices $k$-feasible if, for each nonroot vertex, at most $k$ of its proper ancestors are joined to its subtree by arcs whose endpoints avoid $Y$ and whose underlying edges lie outside the DFS tree. Given $k$ but not such a set, the second algorithm takes, for every $k$-feasible set $Y$ of total out-degree $d^+(Y)$, time $O_k(n+m+(1+|Y|)\log n+\sqrt{(n+m)d^+(Y)\log n})$. When $m=Θ(n\sqrt{\log\log n})$, this is $O_k(n\sqrt{\log n})$ if some $k$-feasible set has $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ vertices and total out-degree $O(n/\sqrt{\log\log n})$.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 29 pages. Continuation of arXiv:2611.26453

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Asymptotically Optimal Representation of Tree-Like Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We show how to represent a graph with $n$ nodes, $m=n+k=O(n)$ edges, and $h\le k$ nodes with more than one incoming edge in asymptotically optimal space, in a way that supports basic navigational operations quickly.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Randomized MST Certification beyond Cacti
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study minimum spanning tree certification under explorable edge uncertainty. Edge weights lie in open intervals or singleton sets, and querying an edge reveals its weight at a known positive cost. On general graphs the best known randomized competitive ratio is $1+1/\sqrt2$, while the optimal ratio $3/2$ is known only for cacti. We go beyond cacti in two ways, with conditions that refer to the uncertain edges outside the upper-limit tree rather than to the graph alone. For unit query costs we give a $3/2$-competitive algorithm, which is best possible, whenever every block has at most two such edges; this includes all graphs whose blocks are cycles or theta graphs. The algorithm replaces the constant budget of the water-filling method by budgets chosen with lookahead to the next fundamental cycle. For arbitrary positive query costs and every fixed $k\ge1$, we obtain ratio $1+\sqrt{k/(2(k+1))}$ whenever every block has at most $k$ such edges, in particular when every block has cycle rank at most $k$. This is below $1+1/\sqrt2$ for every $k$, and we show that it is the best ratio attainable with a constant water-filling budget.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Attractors Is All You Need: Parity Games In Polynomial Time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: This paper provides a polynomial-time algorithm for solving parity games that runs in $\mathcal{O}(n^{2}\cdot(n + m))$ time-ending a search that has taken decades. Unlike previous attractor-based algorithms, the presented algorithm only removes regions with a determined winner. The paper introduces a new type of attractor that can guarantee finding the minimal dominion of a parity game. The attractor runs in polynomial time and can peel the graph empty.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: I withdraw this preprint because the algorithm is incorrect. Tom van Dijk provided a four-vertex counterexample, Odd owns all four vertices, labelled by priority. The moves $0\to1\to2\to4$ are forced; from 4, Odd chooses 0 or 2. Even wins every play, yet for d=4 the first pruning step discards the entire Even dominion, contradicting Lemma 3. The claimed polynomial-time result does not follow

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Running-Time Lower Bounds under FPT $\neq$ W[1]
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We revisit running-time lower bounds historically based on the Exponential Time Hypothesis. We survey bounds that can be recovered from earlier work under FPT $\neq$ W[1] and prove seven lower bounds for graph problems and set systems under the same assumption. The new proofs encode clique choices in few bits and control the target parameter in terms of the encoding. This lets us turn a sufficiently fast algorithm for the target problem into a fixed-parameter algorithm for Clique or Multicolored Clique. In several cases, the new bound matches the function of the parameter in the historical exponent, with the additional requirement that the cutoff for any prescribed saving in the exponent be computable.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Efficient Adaptive Data Analysis over Dense Data Distributions
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Modern data workflows are inherently adaptive, repeatedly querying the same dataset to refine and validate sequential decisions, but such adaptivity can lead to overfitting and invalid statistical inference. Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) mechanisms address this challenge; however, there is a fundamental tension between computational efficiency and sample complexity. For $T$ rounds of adaptive analysis, computationally efficient algorithms typically incur suboptimal $O(\sqrt{T})$ sample complexity, whereas for arbitrary distributions, algorithms with $O(\log T)$ sample complexity are computationally intractable under standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work, we shed light on this trade-off by identifying a natural class of data distributions under which both computational efficiency and logarithmic sample complexity in $T$ are achievable. We propose a computationally efficient ADA mechanism that attains $O(\log T)$ sample complexity, optimal in its dependence on $T$, when the data distribution is dense with respect to a known prior. This setting includes, in particular, feature-label data distributions arising in distribution-specific learning. As a consequence, our mechanism also yields a sample-efficient (i.e., $O(\log T)$ samples) statistical query oracle in the distribution-specific setting. Moreover, although our algorithm is not based on differential privacy, it satisfies a relaxed privacy notion known as Predicate Singling Out (PSO) security (Cohen and Nissim 2020) whenever the number of its possible update transcripts is polynomial in the sample size. Our results thus reveal an inherent connection between adaptive data analysis and privacy beyond differential privacy.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 20 pages, NeurIPS 2026 Camera-ready, arXiv title corrected

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: The Complexity of Computing Class Probabilities in BID Probabilistic Databases
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We study the problem of computing class probabilities in block-independent disjoint (BID) probabilistic databases. Given the probability with which each block in the database realizes each feasible tuple type, the goal is to compute the probability of a class of worlds specified by a given tuple multiplicity vector, thus grouping together worlds with the same bag (multiset) of realized tuple types. For this problem, we prove $\#\mathsf{P}$-hardness even for very restricted and structured inputs. On the other hand, we show that it admits an FPRAS, as well as $\mathsf{XP}$-time algorithms parameterized by the number of tuple types and the treewidth of an incidence graph modeling the connections between blocks and tuples. Finally, we show that augmenting the problem with certain compatibility constraints between block realizations renders it $\#\mathsf{XLP}$- and $\#\mathsf{XALP}$-hard parameterized by pathwidth and treewidth respectively, ruling out $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithms under standard assumptions. We leave as an open question whether this also holds in the absence of compatibility constraints.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We prove memory/query-complexity tradeoff lower bounds for the feasibility problem, where the goal is to find a point within an $ε$-ball hidden in the unit $d$-dimensional ball, with access to a separation oracle. This problem admits three regimes: the low-accuracy regime $ε\geq 1/\sqrt d$ where memory does not play a role, the medium-accuracy regime $1/\sqrt d\geq ε\geq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ where prior works identified strong memory/query-complexity separations, and the high-accuracy regime $ε\leq e^{-Ω(d\ln d)}$ for which much less is known. In this regime, low-memory algorithms with significantly faster convergence rates than gradient descent have been developed in [BZJ24]: for accuracy $ε$ and any $δ\in[0,1]$, these require $d^{1+δ}\ln \frac1ε$ memory bits and use $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{O(d^{1-δ})}$ oracle queries. In comparison, gradient descent uses the same memory for $δ=0$ but requires $1/ε^2$ oracle queries. On the lower-bound side, no non-trivial memory/query-complexity tradeoff was known: the best lower bound remained the historical memory-independent bound $Ω(d\ln \frac1ε)$ from [NYD83]. We make progress towards characterizing the memory landscape in this high-accuracy regime by showing that for any $δ\in[0,1]$, any algorithm with $d^{1+δ}\ln\frac1ε$ bits of memory uses at least $\left(d\ln\frac1ε\right)^{\widetildeΩ(d^{(1-δ)/8})}$ oracle calls. This result justifies the seemingly peculiar exponential-in-$d$ dependence of oracle complexity for the aforementioned low-memory algorithms. In particular, our result shows that for high-accuracy feasibility problems, insufficient memory does result in an exponential price in the dimension for the query-complexity.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Version note. This version revises the compression reduction and mutual-information accounting in Section 4.3. The revised argument explicitly includes the shared randomness in the Message between encoder and decoder

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Local-to-Global Approximation Framework for Covering Disjointness-Compliable Set Families
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Many network design problems can be formulated as covering a family of vertex sets by edges. We develop a local-to-global approximation framework for disjointness-compliable families with polynomial-time membership tests. A class of vertices is deficient if it belongs to the family and feasible otherwise. Our local problem seeks a minimum-cost tree that connects one deficient class to feasible classes so that their union is feasible. If this local problem admits a polynomial-time $α$-approximation, then the covering problem admits a polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrtα)^2$-approximation for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Our algorithm first connects deficient vertices that are difficult to separate and then handles regions containing one deficient class at a time. To bound the total local cost, we compare the local trees with a feasible forest. We delete edges of this forest after using them in the bound, so each is counted at most once even when regions overlap. As applications, we obtain polynomial-time $(8+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for generalized point-to-point connection and multiroot quota tree, including multiroot $k$-minimum spanning tree. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first polynomial-time constant-factor approximations for both problems. We also obtain a randomized approximation for multiroot covering Steiner that has the same asymptotic ratio as the known approximation for its single-root version.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: On the Complexity of Orientable Domination
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The orientable domination number of an undirected graph $G$ is the maximum over all orientations $D$ of $G$ of the minimum size of a dominating set of $D$. In this paper, we look at the problem to decide if the orientable domination number of a given undirected graph $G$ is at least a given integer $\ell$. We show that this problem is complete for the class $Σ_2^P$, is fixed-parameter tractable by treewidth, and has a polynomial kernel parameterized by vertex cover number.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (Sofsem 2027)

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Frequency Estimation from the Internal State of the Boyer-Moore Majority Vote Algorithm
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The Boyer-Moore Majority Vote algorithm identifies a majority candidate in a single pass over a data stream using constant memory O(1) and linear processing time O(n). While the classic algorithm identifies a candidate without directly estimating its frequency, its internal register states retain information about item occurrences during execution. This work investigates a frequency estimator derived directly from these internal counters. We establish the conditions under which the counter state enables exact recovery of the frequency of the majority element and characterize the estimation error when these conditions are not satisfied. In particular, we analyze the effect of stream ordering on the estimator and identify delayed-arrival configurations, such as Majority-Delayed sequences, that can lead to systematic estimation errors. We further derive the error behavior associated with late-arriving majority blocks and empirically evaluate the estimator across multiple stream topologies. The results demonstrate that the internal state of the Boyer-Moore algorithm can provide frequency information without increasing its O(1) space complexity. At the same time, its accuracy depends critically on the ordering of elements in the input stream.

Signal Processing.title: Is Classical Error Control Ready for IMT-2030? Information-Loss Interfaces in Channel Estimation, FEC, CRC, and ARQ for Machine-Type Services
Signal Processing.summary: Fault tolerance and structured error control in mobile communication networks--historically implemented as a modular cascade of pilot-aided channel estimation (CE), forward error correction (FEC), cyclic redundancy check (CRC), and hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ)--remain foundational to 5G New Radio (NR). Although finite-blocklength coding, joint estimation-decoding, and grant-free access have been active academic topics for over a decade, commercial 3GPP specifications up to Release 18 still enforce rigid cross-layer boundaries between these blocks. In short-packet machine-type communications (MTC) for IMT-2030 (6G), inserting separate redundancy for channel training, error correction, and error detection shrinks the net payload entropy resolved per channel slot, while standardized UE processing timelines and HARQ round-trip delays collide with sub-millisecond reliability targets. Combining a multi-user MIMO short-packet simulation with real 3GPP TS 38.214 numerology latency budgets, this article diagnoses the structural bottlenecks of the legacy reliability pipeline and outlines an interoperable roadmap for 3GPP Release 20+--spanning soft-output universal decoding, sensing-assisted priors, grant-free joint detection, and task-oriented error control.
Signal Processing.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 1 table

Signal Processing.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.
Signal Processing.comment: accepted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Signal Processing.title: Extreme Value Theory for Peak Power in Discrete-Time Complex Gaussian Processes
Signal Processing.summary: The peak power for a band-limited, radio frequency (RF) signal, often expressed using the dimensionless peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), is an important quantity for signal analysis and the design of RF transmitters and receivers. Modern digital instrumentation, like vector signal analyzers, collect and process discrete-time samples of the complex baseband signal. Also, computer-based simulations of continuous-time processes must be carried out with discrete-time sequences. Therefore, to design such measurements and simulations, accurate models for the distribution of the PAPR for discrete-time complex baseband processes are required. In particular, band-pass thermal noise and modern communication signals, like orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), are often modeled as complex Gaussian processes. To address this problem, we present a new analytical model for the PAPR distribution of a stationary, discrete-time, complex Gaussian process. We demonstrate that the new discrete-time model subsumes prior models based on asymptotic extreme value theory as special cases while providing a larger domain of efficacy. Specifically, using Monte Carlo simulations of filtered complex white Gaussian noise, we show that the new model is more effective for practical sample sizes and dual-band spectra than previous approaches.
Signal Processing.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures

Signal Processing.title: Blind Channel and Noise-Variance Estimation for MIMO Thermal Noise Modulation Systems via Generalized Expectation-Maximization
Signal Processing.summary: Thermal Noise Modulation (TNM) is a communication paradigm in which information is conveyed through different thermal-noise variance levels rather than deterministic signal waveforms. Its stochastic nature makes conventional pilot-based channel estimation challenging, while pilot transmission introduces additional overhead and reduces spectral efficiency. This paper proposes a pilot-free blind receiver for M-ary TNM systems based on the Generalized Expectation-Maximization (GEM) framework. The proposed receiver jointly estimates the channel matrix, latent transmitted symbols, mixture probabilities, and unknown transmit-noise variance levels directly from received observations, without requiring pilot symbols or prior knowledge of the variance constellation. The modulation order M and receiver-noise variance are assumed to be known. Since the maximization step has no closed-form solution, a gradient-ascent procedure is incorporated into the GEM framework to iteratively update the unknown parameters. The proposed approach enables simultaneous channel estimation, symbol detection, and variance learning within a unified blind-receiver framework. Simulation results demonstrate accurate channel Gram matrix estimation and effective symbol detection without pilot overhead. Moreover, the proposed variance learning scheme achieves performance close to that obtained with perfectly known transmit variance levels, with only moderate BER degradation, demonstrating its potential for practical MIMO TNM systems.

Signal Processing.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
Signal Processing.summary: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 7 tables. Reference library and portal at https://lq8.org

Signal Processing.title: Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications: Achievable DoF Analysis
Signal Processing.summary: Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications significantly enhances the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio $γ$, where a server with $L$ transmit antennas communicates with $K$ users. The users are partitioned into $J$ groups, and each user in group $j$ has $G_j$ receive antennas. We propose four content-aware MIMO-CC strategies: \emph{min-$G$} enforces symmetry using the smallest antenna count among users; \emph{Grouping} maximizes intra-subset spatial multiplexing gain at the expense of some global caching gain; \emph{Super-grouping} aggregates users into optimized \emph{min-$G$}-based super-sets with identical effective receive multiplexing gains before applying \emph{Grouping} across them; and \emph{Phantom} redistributes spatial resources assuming "phantom" antennas at the users to bridge the performance gains of \emph{min-$G$} and \emph{Grouping}. We develop these asymmetric strategies under three reference symmetric CC placement-delivery policies with guaranteed linear decodability: a finite-search DoF-optimized policy attaining the best single-shot achievable DoF lower bound, and two closed-form policies, namely combinatorial and linear cyclic low-complexity constructions, with the cyclic policy attaining DoF performance close to the others in many operating regimes. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate significant DoF improvements across various system configurations, and that policy-strategy combinations offer flexible trade-offs between DoF and subpacketization complexity.

Signal Processing.title: MedTimeQ: Query-guided fusion of time-series foundation models and LLMs for multi-lead ECG classification
Signal Processing.summary: Accurate classification of medical time series, such as electrocardiograms (ECGs), requires capturing waveform morphology, long-range temporal structure, inter-lead dependencies, and clinical semantics. Existing large language model (LLM)-based approaches often map signal patches directly into the language embedding space, potentially underusing pretrained time-series knowledge and transferring redundant or irrelevant information. We propose MedTimeQ, a parameter-efficient framework that integrates a lead-aware temporal foundation encoder with an LLM-reprogrammed ECG pathway through gated residual fusion. A Query Former uses learned diagnostic queries to select and compress fused representations into informative soft tokens for a frozen LLM. Semantic prototype learning further guides classification through multiple clinical descriptions per category, statistics-based prompt selection, and knowledge distillation. Both foundation backbones remain frozen, limiting training to lightweight interface and classification components. We evaluate MedTimeQ on PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, and MIT-BIH for recording-level diagnosis, rhythm classification, and heartbeat classification, respectively. MedTimeQ achieves the best performance in 11 of 12 dataset-metric comparisons, with consistent class-balanced gains across all three tasks. On PTB-XL, it achieves 76.93% accuracy and 58.14% macro-F1, exceeding MedTsLLM by 10.08 and 7.07 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the benefits of selectively integrating pretrained temporal representations with clinical language semantics. Code: https://github.com/kkianamm/MedTimeQ

Signal Processing.title: DIBEM: Diffusion-Based Error Mitigation for Uncertainty-Aware UWB Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Ultra-wideband (UWB) localization degrades substantially under Non-Line-of-Sight (NLoS) propagation, where multipath and obstruction induce complex ranging error distributions that are poorly represented by fixed parametric models. We propose Diffusion-based Error Mitigation (DIBEM), an uncertainty-aware framework that learns the conditional ranging error distribution directly from six compact Channel Impulse Response (CIR) statistics. Rather than predicting a deterministic correction or restricting uncertainty to a Gaussian or fixed mixture family, DIBEM uses a conditional diffusion model with denoising diffusion implicit model sampling to generate link-specific error samples. The resulting empirical distributions are incorporated into maximum likelihood position estimation. This allows localization to account for heterogeneous ranging uncertainty across anchor-tag links. Experiments across four indoor environments show that DIBEM achieves the lowest negative log-likelihood for NLoS ranging errors and the lowest or tied-lowest mean localization error across all environments. Compared with least squares approaches, DIBEM reduces mean localization error by up to 64.8 percent, while improving over Gaussian and mixture density probabilistic models by up to 15.8 percent and 14.0 percent, respectively. Results demonstrate the potential of diffusion-based conditional error modeling for uncertainty-aware UWB localization, particularly under challenging NLoS propagation.

Signal Processing.title: Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD) with Divide and Conquer Strategy for DRL-Based BS Localization
Signal Processing.summary: Optimal base station (BS) placement is a fundamental challenge in wireless localization. Conventional optimization approaches may become computationally demanding as the geometric complexity of the environment increases, limiting their scalability to realistic building layouts. This paper proposes an Approximate Convex Decomposition (ACD)-based divide-and-conquer framework integrated with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for optimizing BS placement. The proposed approach exploits the geometric structure of building layouts by partitioning the original environment into smaller sub-regions using cuts associated with reflex vertices. Furthermore, the proposed solution is bench-marked against DRL without ACD and with the optimal solution obtained by exhaustive search. Results show the superiority of the proposed approach and that it approaches the optimal solution.

Signal Processing.title: RF-Florence: Unified RF Detection and Physical Grounding with a Foundation Model
Signal Processing.summary: Reliable signal detection is essential for spectrum sharing and intelligent sensing in sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. Wideband radio-frequency (RF) monitoring must locate emissions and identify those satisfying waveform-family and physical constraints. The latter task, physical grounding, requires query meaning to agree with measurable signal attributes. RF-Florence unifies three tasks---full-scene detection, physical grounding, and supplied-region recognition---through a shared pretrained foundation model. Calibrated spectrograms connect localization coordinates to time and frequency, while common event targets and explicit predicates align task outputs with requests. On synthetic mixtures with family--attribute combinations withheld from training, structured queries improve mean grounding F1 by 7.66 percentage points over natural language. Under the tested two-path channel, direct grounding with structured queries exceeds a You Only Look Once (YOLO) detector followed by rule-based filtering by 3.44 points in mean F1. These results show the value of aligning query expressions with the signal families and physical variables that define the requested event set.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables

Signal Processing.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
Signal Processing.summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(ω)\propto[1+2α(ω-ω_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|ω-ω_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $α\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $α$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $α$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $α$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.
Signal Processing.comment: 27 pages, 9 figures. Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. Code: https://github.com/plustar/A-Closed-Form-Soft-Spectral-Partition-for-Adaptive-Mode-Decomposition

Signal Processing.title: Self-Aligned Resonant Beams for Adaptive Beamforming in 6G IoT
Signal Processing.summary: The integration of communication, sensing, and wireless power transfer (WPT) is becoming an important direction for 6G Internet of Things (IoT). However, conventional beamforming typically depends on channel state information (CSI) acquisition, beam training, and active beam scanning, which can introduce substantial overhead in dynamic or passive-device scenarios. This article reviews the radio-frequency resonant beam system (RF-RBS) as a physical-layer self-alignment mechanism for reducing this dependence. By using retro-directive antenna arrays (RAAs) at the transceivers, RF-RBS can form a cyclic electromagnetic feedback loop in which phase-conjugated waves reinforce a dominant round-trip path. This mechanism enables self-aligned, high-gain beam formation under suitable loop-gain, propagation, and hardware conditions. We discuss the RF-RBS architecture, its operating principles, and its potential roles in WPT, self-aligned communication, and passive positioning. We also examine implementation challenges, including analog hardware integration, multi-user interference, limited coverage, and line-of-sight (LoS) dependence, and outline its potential value for latency-sensitive 6G IoT scenarios such as unmanned systems and industrial automation.

Signal Processing.title: On linear MMSE receivers in the presence of data-like multiuser interference
Signal Processing.summary: Linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receivers have been of great interest for many decades for multi-user interference (MUI) mitigation in radiocommunications networks in particular. Despite the extensive literature on this subject, this topic remains relevant to several current and emerging applications. In this context, the paper presents a continuous-time approach showing that most of LMME receivers of the literature are suboptimal. In particular, they are typically implemented at the symbol rate following matched filtering to the pulse-shaping filter and require a prior knowledge of the MUI channels, which can be difficult and costly to acquire in practice. The main contribution of this paper is to address the key challenge of designing new LMMSE receivers that achieve the performance of the optimal receiver without requiring prior knowledge of the MUI channels. To this end, two novel receiver LMMSE structures are proposed and analyzed for linearly modulated signals impaired by data-like MUI: a two-input receiver and a three-input receiver. The proposed receivers are shown to be quasi-optimal over a broad range of scenarios. These results provide new perspectives for practical implementation of the optimal LMMSE receiver in the presence of data-like MUI, relying only on knowledge of the signal-of-interest (SOI) channel.
Signal Processing.comment: 8 figures

Signal Processing.title: SleepXA: Composing Pretrained Neural and Cardiac Foundation Models for Sleep Representation Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Physiological signals recorded during sleep provide synchronized views of neural, cardiac, respiratory, and other bodily systems, while preserving modality-specific information. Existing EEG and ECG foundation models already capture rich but distinct physiological structure, motivating an alternative to training a multimodal sleep model from scratch: composing existing pretrained models. We introduce SleepXA, a framework that uses synchronized polysomnography (PSG) to compose independently pretrained neural and cardiac foundation models. SleepXA combines pretrained EEG and ECG encoders with lightweight encoders for additional PSG modalities, and learns shared and modality-specific representations through sleep-guided alignment. We pretrain SleepXA on 9,230 overnight PSG recordings from three large cohorts and evaluate it on 27 downstream tasks spanning sleep representation, clinical and disease prediction, and daytime physiological transfer. SleepXA ranks among the top two methods on 22 of 27 tasks. Controlled experiments further show consistent benefits across sensor configurations and EEG-ECG backbone choices, while pretrained initialization outperforms architecture-matched training from scratch and SleepXA surpasses alternative multimodal composition strategies. These results suggest that synchronized multimodal physiology can serve as a natural interface for composing existing physiological foundation models, yielding reusable representations that extend beyond sleep to clinical and daytime physiological settings.
Signal Processing.comment: 36 pages, 16 figures (9 in the main text and 7 in the appendix)

Signal Processing.title: WAFT: A Fourier-Analytic Framework for Steady-State Performance of Walker Constellations
Signal Processing.summary: The Walker configuration is predominantly adopted by nongeostationary orbit constellations exemplified by Starlink and Kuiper. The steady-state distribution of aggregate downlink interference power is critical for spectrum coexistence regulation. Large-scale time-stepped simulation and stochastic geometry (SG)-based models are the mainstream methods for obtaining the distribution, but are either computationally expensive or subject to inherent bias. This paper models the aggregate downlink interference power as an additive observable and proposes the Walker-constellation Analysis via Fourier Transform (WAFT) framework to derive the steady-state performance. Modeling the constellation as a periodic impulse array on the phase torus, the spectral representation of the observable is derived via 2-D Fourier analysis. Analytical expressions for the expectation, variance, and steady-state complementary cumulative distribution function are further derived, and the periodicity of receiver performance along longitude is characterized. For a Starlink sub-constellation example, numerical validation shows that the percentile discrepancies of WAFT relative to a finite-duration time-stepped simulation remain within 0.09~dB. Comparisons with isotropic and intensity-matched SG models reveal that the conditional independence of satellite positions alone makes the models assign a substantial probability mass to physically infeasible values, producing percentile discrepancies.
Signal Processing.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
Signal Processing.summary: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

Signal Processing.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
Signal Processing.summary: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

Signal Processing.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
Signal Processing.summary: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

Signal Processing.title: Denoised but Not Improved: What EEG Denoising Does to a Downstream Task
Signal Processing.summary: Scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is routinely denoised before it reaches a downstream model, and the denoising literature scores a method by how closely its output matches a clean reference waveform. That reference does not exist for real scalp recordings: it is synthesized by adding artifact templates to signals merely presumed clean, and even an exact separation would return cortical activity blurred by volume conduction rather than the activity itself. Fidelity to it is therefore an unvalidatable objective, and whether it predicts any downstream benefit has gone largely unexamined. We report an audit that examines it. Holding a seizure-detection pipeline fixed and varying only the preprocessing stage, we find that five standard denoising methods, spanning analytic, cross-channel and supervised deep families, all fail to improve on the unprocessed signal, and most degrade it. To say what such a stage must instead do, we formalize a label-only, classifier-free probe that reads it by the separability geometry it induces on task-relevant features, decomposing any change into a between-class distance and a within-class scatter term. On a transform that does improve the task, the probe attributes the entire gain to a roughly one-quarter reduction of within-class scatter, with class separation statistically unchanged. What a downstream model benefits from is therefore variance suppression on task-relevant structure, which waveform-fidelity metrics neither measure nor reward.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at the IEEE Symposium on CI in Health and Medicine

Signal Processing.title: From Footprints to Service Regions: Modeling and Analysis of Dense LEO Satellite Networks Using an Orbit-Aware Cox Point Process
Signal Processing.summary: In dense low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks, several accessible satellites cover the same location. A footprint therefore identifies where communication is feasible but does not determine which satellite serves each user. The service region of a satellite, namely the set of locations it serves, governs satellite load, resource sharing, and user throughput. Using an orbit-aware Cox point process on a common orbital shell, we model each service region as the intersection of a satellite's spherical-cap footprint and its spherical Voronoi cell under nearest-satellite association. We then use Palm calculus to derive exact expressions for the mean area and perimeter and a coverage--load identity. After coverage saturates, mean area and load decrease inversely with population. In contrast, adding satellites along existing orbits leaves a positive limiting mean perimeter. We connect this geometry to an approximate noise-limited user rate. Along the tested densification paths, the increase in user rate comes mainly from the decrease in mean satellite load rather than from the improvement of the serving link. We also compare the model with Walker constellations with Starlink-type parameters, using Cox parameters matched to the local orbit and satellite densities at each latitude. The model reproduces the mean area and perimeter of these constellations over broad latitude ranges, with larger differences near component maximum latitudes. These results show that service-region geometry, and hence satellite load and user rate, depend not only on the total satellite population but also on its allocation across orbital planes.
Signal Processing.comment: accepted to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications

Sound.title: SpA2V: Harnessing Spatial Auditory Cues for Audio-driven Spatially-aware Video Generation
Sound.summary: Audio-driven video generation aims to synthesize realistic videos that align with input audio recordings, akin to the human ability to visualize scenes from auditory input. However, existing approaches predominantly focus on exploring semantic information, such as the classes of sounding sources present in the audio, limiting their ability to generate videos with accurate content and spatial composition. In contrast, we humans can not only naturally identify the semantic categories of sounding sources but also determine their deeply encoded spatial attributes, including locations and movement directions. This useful information can be elucidated by considering specific spatial indicators derived from the inherent physical properties of sound, such as loudness or frequency. As prior methods largely ignore this factor, we present SpA2V, the first framework explicitly exploits these spatial auditory cues from audios to generate videos with high semantic and spatial correspondence. SpA2V decomposes the generation process into two stages: 1) Audio-guided Video Planning: We meticulously adapt a state-of-the-art MLLM for a novel task of harnessing spatial and semantic cues from input audio to construct Video Scene Layouts (VSLs). This serves as an intermediate representation to bridge the gap between the audio and video modalities. 2) Layout-grounded Video Generation: We develop an efficient and effective approach to seamlessly integrate VSLs as conditional guidance into pre-trained diffusion models, enabling VSL-grounded video generation in a training-free manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpA2V excels in generating realistic videos with semantic and spatial alignment to the input audios.
Sound.comment: The 33rd ACM Multimedia Conference (MM '25) | Page: https://spa2v.tkpham.me

Sound.title: Music Circuit: Trace and Control Style Dynamics in Large Music Generation Model
Sound.summary: Musical style, a global attribute that functions throughout a whole piece, is a lever widely used by users in modern large music generation models. Yet how style is represented inside these models, and which components drive it, remains largely unexplored. In language models, circuit analysis traces a representation to a sparse sub-network of a few key components, namely attention heads and MLP neurons, and has been used successfully to explain and control global attributes such as emotion. In this work, we use circuit analysis to study the mechanisms behind musical style. Based on YuE2, we build a dataset that pairs the same lyrics with five styles and design a three-step framework. First, stage localization shows that the style forms mainly in the score-planning stage. Second, static observation across the positions of this stage further reveals that style is not a fixed vector but a dynamic representation across tokens. Third, we therefore merge the activation differences across positions into one direction per style, and trace the neurons and attention heads that drive this direction into a sparse circuit. Without any style text, steering this circuit successfully transfers one piece into the target style, matching and even exceeding the style prompt. To our knowledge, this is the first work to analyze and control musical style at the circuit level in a large music generation model. Audio and score examples are available at https://aristo233.github.io/Music_Circuit/.
Sound.comment: 28 pages, 20 figures, 14 tables

Sound.title: PAWP-TTS: Phoneme-Aware Weight Programming for Compact Bilingual English-Nepali Speech Synthesis
Sound.summary: This paper presents PAWP-TTS, a compact non-autoregressive text-to-speech system for English, Nepali, and English-Nepali code-mixed speech at 24 kHz, with no language model at inference. Deterministic pronunciation knowledge lives in a rule- and lexicon-based bilingual frontend that preserves native Nepali contrasts and avoids Hindi phonology, so the network only models acoustics. Counting every learned inference tensor, including the waveform decoder, PAWP-1.5M (1,490,390 parameters, 5.98 MB) reaches 1.50% English and 1.75% Nepali character error rate under a single ASR recognizer, and 5.04% / 4.02% Nepali / English phoneme error rate (PER) on 600 untouched test utterances. Decoder-centric 281K-parameter models (1.1 MB) stay intelligible across three independent seeds, with equal-budget dense models (5.53 +/- 0.08% NE, 5.34 +/- 0.28% EN PER) outperforming K=2 cross-layer shared-basis models (6.35 +/- 0.11% NE, 6.57 +/- 0.47% EN PER). Fixing a frontend/label version mismatch nearly halved Nepali PER, more than any architectural or weight-level change. The paper then studies weight-space programming: inspection-guided, zero-training weight edits. Under strict controls (validation-only selection, one-shot test, paired bootstrap, matched random and same-parameter gradient baselines), edits show real selectivity (27:1 on word-boundary pauses with 96 weights; zero cross-lingual collateral inside language-gated residuals) but no accuracy gain beyond controls. Two apparent targets proved to be label or phonology artifacts. Code, ONNX graphs, and CC BY 4.0 weights are released.
Sound.comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Code: https://github.com/Firojpaudel/PAWP_TTS | Audio Demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Firoj112/pawp-tts-demo | Models: https://huggingface.co/Firoj112/pawp-tts-1.5m and https://huggingface.co/Firoj112/pawp-tts-300k

Sound.title: Who Plays What: Same-Instrument Music Separation from Video
Sound.summary: When two musicians in an ensemble play the same instrument, they sound alike and their instruments look alike. Audio-only separators, and audio-visual separators that rely on appearance, cannot tell them apart. What still differs is how each player moves, and when. We study same-instrument per-player separation: a user clicks one musician in a video and receives that musician's sound alone, even when other players in the video play the same instrument. Our model follows the clicked player and describes them with high level video features and the velocities of body and hand keypoints. A pretrained music separator attends to these tokens through cross-attention. Earlier motion-based separators were scored only on synthetic mixtures of solo videos. We give the first per-player evaluation of same-instrument separation on real ensemble recordings. On 58 players in URMP, each sharing an instrument with at least one other player in the piece, our model reaches a median SDR of 5.3 dB, while four released separators, audio-only and audio-visual, stay at or below 0.3 dB. The gap is wider on same-instrument duets, and our model also beats the audio-visual baselines on their own MUSIC benchmark. Tests show that the gain comes from movement: replacing the video with a still frame removes it, and so does shifting the video by a fraction of a second against the audio.

Sound.title: MusicListenBench: Can Audio LLMs Hear the Difference Yet?
Sound.summary: Audio large language models (LLMs) are typically evaluated on song genre, mood, and instrumentation. A more basic skill is telling whether two short clips play the same melody, chord or instrument. We introduce MusicListenBench, a benchmark of paired listening tests for melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo. Each test item comes with two variants. A FLIP variant changes the music, so the answer must change. A STAY variant changes only the sound, such as room echo or hiss, so the answer must stay the same. The two variants have opposite answers, so a model that ignores the audio scores 50%, whatever letter it prefers. The benchmark has a training split and two test sets, one rendered from symbolic music with exact labels and one built from real recordings. On the rendered test, seven of eight open audio LLMs score within 4 points of this floor. Of four commercial models, both GPT-Audio models are at chance, and the best, Gemini 2.5 Pro, reaches 74.2%, 12.8 points below human listeners (87.0%). Post-training with GRPO on 10k rendered clean pairs raises Qwen2.5-Omni from 61.2% to 99.0% on held-out clean pairs, and the gain transfers to a task left out of training. On FLIP/STAY, however, it only reaches the level of our listeners (86.0%). It now misses almost no change (1.9%, against 24.7% for Gemini 2.5 Pro), yet when only the sound changes, it turns a correct answer into a wrong one 25.7\% of the time. More than half of its false flips come from a quiet background hiss. Models learn to hear a difference much faster than they learn which differences matter. On real recordings, open models again stay near chance, and the trained model calls 27 of 42 pairs of two strums of the same chord different. Adding sound-only pairs to training lowers false flips on both test sets, but no training run teaches relative pitch. We release the data, code, and an open leaderboard.

Sound.title: Self-Distilled Pronunciation and Accent Control for Neural Text-to-Speech
Sound.summary: Text-to-speech that reads raw text has no lexicon: a rare word is read as guessed, and a native Japanese listener accepts a word only if its reading and pitch accent are both right. A known remedy installs a reading-and-accent channel into a released model, but it needs many recordings. This paper removes the recordings: the frozen backbone reads a sentence containing a common word it already says correctly, and that output serves as the teacher for the same sentence with the word replaced by an annotated reading with its pitch accent. Screened raters judged the tag right on 0.80 to 0.93 of unseen difficult words on four backbones spanning autoregressive, diffusion, and encoder-decoder synthesis; plain kana, which cannot express an accent, got 0.38 to 0.60. On words needing no edit, naturalness is non-inferior on one backbone; on the other three, listeners prefer the unedited rendition by 0.19 to 0.26.
Sound.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027. v4 corrects factual errors in the submitted text and adds the release of code, models, and data: https://github.com/shuheikatoinfo/UtterTune-SelfDistill

Sound.title: SWIFT: A Handcrafted, Arithmetic-Minimal FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
Sound.summary: Generative voice cloning threatens voice-based authentication, yet current deepfake detectors rely on power-hungry, high-precision models unsuited to edge hardware. We present SWIFT (Streaming Whiten-Integer Forensic Trust-Engine), a handcrafted detector that works in the high-frequency noise domain where synthesis artifacts concentrate. A first-order integer high-pass residual drives nine families of fixed-point descriptors, among them integer lifting-wavelet cepstral quantiles, Mahalanobis anomaly distances, Poincaré phase-space geometry, and phase jitter, fused by calibrated gradient-boosted trees and a sparse L1-regularised meta-learner. Under leakage-controlled nested cross-validation, with one shared preprocessing chain for real and fake audio, this reference model reaches accuracy of up to 99.86% and an Equal Error Rate (EER) as low as 0.03% across eight benchmarks. Its integer front-end and a fixed-point linear classifier run on the programmable logic of a PYNQ-Z2 (Zynq-7020) board, with a 7.85 microseconds per-frame datapath latency (127.4k frames/s) at 1.734 W and 11.2% LUT utilisation. Integer-only audio deepfake feature extraction is thus feasible at the edge without pretrained neural models or floating-point units.
Sound.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables, 1 algorithm. Accepted at ICISS 2026. Chirantan Banerjee and Soumita Chatterjee are joint first authors

Sound.title: ARRANGE: Agentic Skills for Layering Vocals
Sound.summary: Adding a singing voice to an existing piano recording requires decisions about melody, syllable placement, pronunciation, timing, and vocal register. ARRANGE organizes this work as a sequence of agent skills with readable intermediate artifacts and composer approval checkpoints. An LLM translates instructions in plain English, notes played on a keyboard, and vocal references into local edits; deterministic scripts validate and apply those edits before open audio models render the result. The Score Canvas makes note, syllable, and pronunciation decisions inspectable and editable. In a benchmark of 16 revision requests, three draws per request, and five LLMs, typed edits achieved exact-change correctness of 0.83-0.98, compared with 0.33-0.69 for whole-plan rewriting without ARRANGE instructions. A separate score-editing benchmark and a first-person worked example examine the interaction between representations and corrections. Author listening evaluations further explore voice transfer and register selection, including 185 listening presentations across eight copied voices. These evaluations support the value of constrained editing and expose limits of both model execution and listening measures. The contribution is an interaction architecture for retaining musical decisions through inspectable intermediate representations, rather than a new singing model or evidence of general usability.
Sound.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Under review at the HUMANE-LLM workshop, ACM IUI 2027 (Helsinki). Code: https://github.com/htansetiawan/ARRANGE ; project page: https://htansetiawan.github.io/ARRANGE

Sound.title: Tenlai-TTS 2.0: Continuous-Representation LLM-Based TTS System with End-to-End Training
Sound.summary: Autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) with continuous speech latents avoids quantization-induced information loss, but typically relies on a latent space that is learned separately and then frozen before language-model training. Such a space must satisfy two competing requirements: it must retain enough acoustic detail for high-fidelity reconstruction, yet be sufficiently structured and regularized to support autoregressive prediction by a language model. We present Tenlai-TTS 2.0, which learns continuous speech representations through end-to-end training to balance acoustic detail with autoregressive predictability. The model comprises a speech encoder with a capacity-controlled Gaussian bottleneck, a large language model (LLM) with an autoregressive diffusion transformer (AR-DiT) head, a flow-matching (FM) mel-spectrogram decoder, and a multi-task recognition model (RM). With energy normalization and fixed-variance Gaussian noise, the bottleneck has a closed-form upper bound on its information rate. Through joint optimization with reconstruction, recognition, and next-patch prediction objectives, we learn continuous speech representations that suit all three tasks and train the LLM and AR-DiT for autoregressive generation. The LLM and AR-DiT are further optimized using differentiable reconstruction and recognition feedback on their predicted latents through the FM decoder and RM. On Seed-TTS-eval, this feedback-based optimization reduces character error rate (CER) from 0.82% to 0.74% on test-zh and from 8.32% to 7.08% on test-hard-zh, and word error rate (WER) from 1.32% to 1.27% on test-en, compared with joint training alone. Subsequent reinforcement learning further reduces CER to 6.29% on test-hard-zh and WER to 1.08% on test-en, with speaker similarity scores of 0.811, 0.766, and 0.784 on test-zh, test-en, and test-hard-zh, respectively.

Sound.title: IteraSong: LLM-Guided Iterative Symbolic Music Creation in a Web DAW
Sound.summary: Music creation is inherently iterative, yet many symbolic generation systems still center on producing or regenerating isolated outputs. We present IteraSong, an interactive web-based Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) for LLM-guided iterative symbolic music creation. Unlike one-shot generation systems, IteraSong supports a generate-audition-edit-refine loop over a persistent multi-track project. Users initialize a fully labeled pop draft, then progressively refine it through natural-language instructions. The LLM maps requests to a hierarchical action space of editing primitives exposed via Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, spanning global, track, section, and bar/note scopes. The demo enables attendees to edit multi-track compositions in natural language, apply deterministic and generative edits, and undo/redo changes in real time.
Sound.comment: AAAI 2027 Demonstration Program (accepted). Extended version with appendix

Sound.title: FGAS: Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation
Sound.summary: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has made high-fidelity generated audio widely available across the Internet, driving the advancement of audio steganography. Benefiting from advances in deep learning, current audio steganography schemes are mainly based on encoder-decoder network architectures. While these methods achieve promising perceptual quality, they typically require network pre-training, and maintaining anti-steganalysis performance at high payloads remains challenging. To address these issues, we propose Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation (FGAS). Adversarial perturbations carrying a secret message are embedded into the cover audio to generate stego audio. The sender and receiver independently construct the same fixed decoder from a shared architecture and initialization key, avoiding the transfer of trained decoder parameters. In FGAS, we propose an Audio Adversarial Perturbation Generation (A2PG) strategy with an optional robust extension and design a lightweight fixed decoder. The fixed decoder guarantees reliable extraction of the hidden message, while adversarial perturbations are optimized to keep the stego audio perceptually and statistically close to the cover audio, thereby improving anti-steganalysis performance. The experimental results show that FGAS significantly improves stego audio quality, achieving an average PSNR gain of over 10 dB compared to SOTA methods. Furthermore, FGAS demonstrates strong robustness against common audio processing attacks. Moreover, FGAS exhibits superior anti-steganalysis performance across different relative payloads; under high-capacity embedding, it achieves a classification error rate about 2% higher, indicating stronger anti-steganalysis performance than current SOTA methods.

Sound.title: Dual-Branch Gated Fusion for Open-Set Audio Deepfake Source Tracing
Sound.summary: Attributing a synthetic utterance to its originating system remains an open challenge: closed-set models fail to reject unseen synthesizers and produce overconfident predictions. To address this, we propose a dual-branch gated fusion framework that pairs XLSR-53 with CORES, a 66-dimensional descriptor that, unlike prior Linear Filter Bank (LFB)-only work, spans cepstral, oscillatory, rhythmic, energy, and spectral dimensions to capture complementary synthesis artifacts. Our analysis shows XLSR-53 remains discriminative in-domain (ID) while CORES generalizes stably under distribution shift (OOD), yet their naive concatenation fails due to SSL representational imbalance. To resolve this, an input-conditioned gate adaptively weights each branch under joint training with cross-entropy, an energy margin loss for ID/OOD separation, and a gate diversity term. On the MLAAD benchmark, our system achieves 97.6\% ID accuracy, 4.9\% EERc, and an 83.5\% relative FPR95 reduction over the Interspeech 2025 baseline.
Sound.comment: Published in Interspeech 2026. Revised version includes NSF funding acknowledgment

Sound.title: TRACE: Training-Free Partial Audio Deepfake Detection via Embedding Trajectory Analysis of Speech Foundation Models
Sound.summary: Partial audio deepfakes, where synthesized segments are spliced into genuine recordings, are particularly deceptive because most of the audio remains authentic. Existing detectors are supervised: they require frame-level annotations, overfit to specific synthesis pipelines, and must be retrained as new generative models emerge. We argue that this supervision is unnecessary. We hypothesize that speech foundation models implicitly encode a forensic signal: genuine speech forms smooth, slowly varying embedding trajectories, while splice boundaries introduce abrupt disruptions in frame-level transitions. Building on this, we propose TRACE (Training-free Representation-based Audio Countermeasure via Embedding dynamics), a training-free framework that detects partial audio deepfakes by analyzing the first-order dynamics of frozen speech foundation model representations without any training, labeled data, or architectural modification. We evaluate TRACE on four benchmarks that span two languages using six speech foundation models. In PartialSpoof, TRACE achieves 8.08% EER, competitive with fine-tuned supervised baselines. In LlamaPartialSpoof, the most challenging benchmark featuring LLM-driven commercial synthesis, TRACE surpasses a supervised baseline outright (24.12% vs. 24.49% EER) without any target-domain data. These results show that temporal dynamics in speech foundation models provide an effective, generalize signal for training-free audio forensics.
Sound.comment: Published at CVPR Workshops 2026. Updated version includes NSF funding acknowledgment

Robotics.title: Dynamics Forcing: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Causal Video World Models
Robotics.summary: Causal video world models generate block by block from their own previous outputs. Small errors in early blocks are fed back as history and grow until the scene and the robot fall apart. Teacher forcing trains on clean ground-truth history, so the model never sees the history it will actually condition on, and it also finds a shortcut: copying the previous frame instead of predicting how the scene changes. We present Dynamics Forcing, a training scheme that keeps real video as the only supervision and reshapes how history is presented. History is perturbed in three ways: random noising, self-resampling by the model itself, and joint denoising, in which the most recent blocks are still partly noisy when the next block is predicted. On top of this we move history guidance and first-frame anchor guidance from inference into training, so that the model is pushed to use its history and its reference frame rather than ignore them. Dynamics Forcing needs no teacher model, no distillation, and no additional model at inference. Applied to a 5B video model with LoRA on 77 hours of manipulation video on a single GPU, it better matches unseen real continuations and reduces error accumulation.

Robotics.title: How Should a Home Robot Update Its Memories When Human Routines Change?
Robotics.summary: A home robot that helps with chores needs to know where objects are, but people move objects according to routines that change and later change back. The robot's memory must adapt to the new routine without erasing experience that may become useful again. One approach is to have a language model maintain written summaries of the home from the robot's own observations, but existing evaluations of such memories use static worlds. We explore simulated households where a resident gets sick, recovers, and later gets sick again. We compare a rule that keeps every room an object has been seen in, language-model memories that store only written summaries, and language-model memories that can also read the raw history of sightings. The rule outperforms every summary-only memory, and giving language models the sighting history closes the gap. Surprisingly, writing summaries on top of the history adds nothing we can measure. When the illness returns, methods that keep the history search better than they did the first time, while summary-only methods show no consistent improvement.
