Sound.summary: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.
Sound.comment: 14 pages

Sound.title: Beyond File-Level Splits: Rethinking Symbolic Music Evaluation via Multi-View Alignment
Sound.summary: Symbolic music generation often continues MIDI passages by predicting subsequent notes or events. Held-out prediction loss can overestimate generalization to unseen compositions when training contains another performance or arrangement of a test work. We introduce Multi-View Alignment-Aware Same-Work Identification, combining complementary musical representations with temporal alignment of shared passages to remove test-work versions from training while preserving unrelated material and fixing evaluation files. In a controlled cohort of 100 manually verified pairs selected for high embedding similarity, replacing 3.29% of training windows with test-work versions reduces mean per-group NLL by up to 30.16% relative to matched unrelated content. Across two datasets and two generators, our method brings test losses closest to a reference built from independent work labels. Compared with removing the same number of files at random, it leaves fewer test works exposed and retains more eligible content, including about 99% of eligible tokens on the piano-performance dataset. A separate study on that dataset matches training tokens and updates: no test works remain exposed under the dataset labels, and mean relative test loss is 2.15% higher than an independently selected reference. These findings support keeping all versions of each composition in one split when evaluating generalization to unseen works. The project is available at https://kunbai05-nb.github.io/.
Sound.comment: 14 pages, including the appendix

Sound.title: Training speech deepfake detectors against worst-case filters: Gains, Costs and Limits
Sound.summary:
Speech deepfake detectors make few errors on standard benchmarks, yet a simple attack defeats them: the attacker passes fake speech through one short filter, tuned against the detector, and many fakes then pass as real. Training with random filters does not stop this attack, because the attacker uses the worst filter, not a random one.
  We therefore train the detector against the worst case: during training, a small set of filters is updated to fool the current detector, at about the cost of random filters. In a preregistered study, this made the detector more robust to filter attacks on real-world recordings than random filters did. It also lowered the in-domain attack error of the standard detector, and beat one-step adversarial training with additive noise on real-world recordings. The price is a higher error on unfiltered speech, and a validation study shows that choosing the checkpoint on held-out spoofing systems made the standard detector about as robust.

Sound.title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
Sound.summary: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible research in music generation. We present PopMelodyGen, a copyright-aware platform for controllable pop-melody generation that combines rule-based synthesis with neural generation. Our approach first uses an expert synthesizer to produce large-scale labeled synthetic melodies from explicit musical knowledge and templates, providing scalable pretraining data with auditable provenance. A neural model is then pretrained on this corpus and adapted with a small licensed real-pop corpus to improve melodic naturalness while preserving controllability. The platform supports interactive melody creation with accompaniment playback and export for creators, as well as batch construction of annotated symbolic datasets for researchers. PopMelodyGen demonstrates a practical training and deployment paradigm for creative AI when large-scale reusable real-world data are limited.
Sound.comment: AAAI 2027 Demonstration Program (accepted); extended version with appendix

Systems and Control.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
Systems and Control.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

Systems and Control.title: Construction of Universal Safe Stabilizing Formulas with Weighted Centroid Methodology
Systems and Control.summary: Control Lyapunov and control barrier functions ensure stability and safety, respectively, by imposing state-dependent affine constraints on the control input. Controller design can therefore be viewed as the problem of selecting an admissible input from the set defined by these constraints. This paper adopts this perspective and develops a weighted-centroid methodology for constructing explicit feedback formulas that are provably smooth. The selection method relies on the fact that weighted centroids of a convex set lie within the set. We establish conditions on the weight functions that guarantee smoothness and continuity for several classes of constraints, including single constraints, mirrored constraints, linearly independent multiple constraints, and two-constraint Gaussian constructions. The framework recovers Sontag's universal formula and generates other new explicit formulas. When specialized to control-theoretic settings, the resulting formulas yield smooth safety filters, stabilizing controllers, and safe-stabilizing controllers. Simulation and hardware experiments on a small quadrotor illustrate the practical benefits of the proposed construction.
Systems and Control.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control

Systems and Control.title: Deliverable Frequency Regulation Reserve for VPPs via Transmission-Distribution Co-Simulation
Systems and Control.summary: Aggregations of distributed energy resources can provide frequency regulation services. However, device-level power headroom may not accurately represent the power deliverable at the transmission-distribution interface. This paper proposes a bidirectional, storage-aware power-sharing framework for a virtual power plant (VPP). Delivery factors obtained from the perturbations used to construct the voltage-sensitivity matrix account for feeder losses and voltage-dependent loads, while battery energy limits and state-of-charge weights are included in the allocation. The framework is evaluated using the IEEE 8500-node feeder and IEEE 14-bus system. The proposed method tracks the feeder-head request within 2% compared with 23-26% over-delivery under the injection-headroom framework. It also sustains the requested power response 22% longer before reaching the storage energy limit. Moreover, communicating the updated VPP reserve to the transmission system operator reduces the post-transient integrated area control error by 80% relative to fixed reserve registration.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to the 2027 IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting (PESGM)

Systems and Control.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on learning-enabled components and distributed algorithms for perception, estimation, and control, introducing uncertainty that makes it challenging to satisfy mission requirements. Conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty with distribution-free guarantees, but existing methods do not address the challenging combination of dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and the distribution shift induced when calibrated uncertainty bounds modify the closed-loop system. We introduce Multi-Agent Interactive Conformal Prediction (MA-ICP), a distributed framework for computing robustness margins in heterogeneous systems to satisfy mission requirements with high probability. MA-ICP aggregates robot-level nonconformity scores, which measure errors in modeled or estimated quantities, into one mission-level score per robot class, allowing dependence among robots within each mission. Mission-level scores and quantiles are computed using neighbor-to-neighbor communication in a finite number of communication rounds. Updating the robustness margins changes robot trajectories and distributed algorithm outputs, so we use class-dependent score sensitivities to upper bound the shift in mission-level scores. We then establish calibration-conditional coverage guarantees per robot class for the updated margins. We demonstrate MA-ICP on cooperative payload control, formation control with obstacle avoidance, and distributed target tracking missions.

Systems and Control.title: Optical Motion Sensing for Piezoelectric-Resonator-Based Power Converters
Systems and Control.summary: Piezoelectric components present a promising alternative to conventional magnetics for miniaturized, high-frequency power converters. While high-Q piezoelectric resonators have demonstrated high efficiencies and large power densities in prototype high-frequency dc-dc converters, their optimal operating conditions are sensitive to temperature fluctuations and load variations. Therefore, robust closed-loop control is essential for practical deployment. Electrical approaches for sensing motional current may compromise the electrical isolation and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity inherently provided by the mechanical nature of these resonators. Here, we present an optical motion sensing approach for piezoelectric power converters. The optical sensing system comprises a laser, fiber optics, and a photodetector. The proposed approach uses optical interference to monitor the mechanical displacement in real time. The resulting optical signal carries both the amplitude and phase of the mechanical motion, which are necessary for closed-loop control. We experimentally characterize and validate this optical motion sensing approach using a 45-kHz piezoelectric resonator driven by a GaN half bridge with input voltages up to 45 V. We further experimentally demonstrate closed-loop control using the proposed optical motion sensing for a 99-kHz isolated piezoelectric converter. These initial results establish a viable pathway toward optically closed-loop control of piezoelectric power converters.

Systems and Control.title: Lithium Niobate Surface-Acoustic-Wave Resonator for Very-High-Frequency Isolated Power Conversion
Systems and Control.summary: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power conversion. Here, we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator that is optimized for isolated power transfer and show advantages in operating frequency, power density, power handling, and electrical isolation. Our application-optimized 40-MHz SAW resonator, with two electrically isolated interdigital transducers (IDTs) and acoustic Bragg mirrors, achieves a 25.7 W output power at a temperature rise of about 15 °C with only passive cooling through the back mounting side. With a chip size of 0.095 cm$^3$ and an acoustic mode volume of 0.00255 cm$^3$, our device features a peak chip power density of 270.5 W/cm$^3$ and a mode-volume power density of 10,078 W/cm$^3$. Our device shows an isolation voltage of 2.17 kV. Driven by a GaN full-bridge inverter, our device can drive different load resistors with a calculated peak power transfer efficiency of 87.5%. Our results show the potential of SAW devices as a core component for next-generation power systems.

Systems and Control.title: Suppressing Chaos Without Silencing Excitable Oscillators
Systems and Control.summary: A negative Lyapunov exponent is not a sufficient goal for controlling an excitable oscillator. A gain can remove chaos by removing the excitation that the model is meant to keep. This manuscript studies that failure mode in three models: the forced FitzHugh--Nagumo neuron, the forced Aliev--Panfilov cardiac cell, and the autonomous Hindmarsh--Rose neuron. Chaos is measured by the largest state Lyapunov exponent. Excitation is measured by threshold crossings, by the excursion of the fast variable, and by the firing rate. Recovery damping, tracking of an unstable periodic orbit, Pyragas delayed feedback, and a change of the fast time scale are compared on the same chaotic regimes. In the forced models, large damping and large rate changes reach regularity by silencing the cell, while tracking and delayed feedback keep firing. In the autonomous model, recovery damping raises the firing rate several-fold instead. A classical matrix-measure bound links these outcomes to the channel through which the gain acts. A constant-metric contraction certificate coexists with substantial firing only under tracking, which subtracts a gain from the fast direction.
Systems and Control.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos

Systems and Control.title: Which Model Belongs in the Loop? Evaluating Fitness Functions for Network Topology Optimization with a Quality-Diversity Algorithm
Systems and Control.summary: Network topology optimization (NTO) can reduce redispatch cost by rerouting power flows in transmission systems. To approach NTO, a complex combinatorial problem, gradient-free optimization algorithms that leverage diversity have shown promising results. These algorithms rely on frequent evaluations of candidate topologies by fitness functions. Recent work has shown that fast DC power flow-based fitness functions can serve this purpose. However, DC power flow fitness functions can misjudge the cost and feasibility of topologies, potentially leading to wrong operational decisions. Understanding the impact of fitness function accuracy on optimization performance is therefore crucial. This study compares the optimization performance of four fitness functions based on DC and AC power flow and on DC and AC optimal power flow. Furthermore, we propose a ranking-based metric to estimate the optimization performance of a fitness function on a curated dataset. Case studies cover the IEEE 118-bus case with 50 congested operating points and a 793-bus case for validation. Results show that optimal power flow-based fitness functions perform better in the optimization loop than power flow-based ones. Additionally, the results indicate that the metric can predict the optimization performance order of the fitness functions, but only if the distribution shift between the curated dataset and the search path of the optimization is small.
Systems and Control.comment: This preprint is currently under peer review

Systems and Control.title: Separating physics from discrepancy: Orthogonalized kernels for physics-encoded system identification
Systems and Control.summary: Physics-encoded identification combines a physical model with a data-driven correction, but the data alone do not determine how the input-output map is split between them: components representable by the physical model may be assigned to either part. In kernel-based model embedding, this allocation is governed by the kernel. As a consequence, the physical parameters lack a well-defined target. In this work, this ambiguity is resolved a priori by defining a canonical physical parameter as the parameter of the physical model that best approximates the noise-free map, in a weighted least-squares sense, over a user-defined operating domain, together with an orthogonal discrepancy. Specifically, an orthogonalized kernel is derived that restricts the correction to functions orthogonal to the physical model. The resulting estimator keeps the closed-form solution of model embedding, while the canonical parameter depends only on the prescribed geometry, not on the kernel or the data. As the inputs become dense and the noise vanishes, the set of parameters consistent with the data converges to the canonical parameter, a property that generally fails without orthogonalization. Under energy-bounded noise, suitable regularization attains optimal worst-case estimation accuracy. Numerical examples demonstrate consistent parameter estimates across different kernels and experiments.
Systems and Control.comment: Preprint submitted to Automatica

Systems and Control.title: Advanced Reactance Method - A Novel Approach for Distance Protection in Presence of Grid-Following Inverter-Based-Resources
Systems and Control.summary:
Renewable Energy Sources and consequently inverter-based resources (IBRs) are increasing worldwide.
  Grid-following (GFL) IBR control is the state-of-the-art.
  GFL IBRs exhibit different fault behavior compared to classical synchronous generators -- particularly in terms of Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) characteristics, which are critical for grid protection relaying.
  Grid protection must work securely, selectively and dependably, regardless of the feeding source.
  As common protection algorithms are designed for fault behavior determined by synchronous generators, their performance is expected to be compromised in the presence of GFL IBRs.
  Distance Protection is a widely used protection algorithm at all voltage levels.
  Literature shows that the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs impacts the Distance Protection relaying adversely.
  This paper proposes the Advanced Reactance Method, a further development of the Classical Reactance Method for Distance Protection in the presence of GFL IBRs.
  The key idea of the proposed method is to make the algorithm independent of the feeding source impedance.
  Therefore, the negative sequence voltage is taken into account along with the negative sequence current.
  This makes the algorithm independent of the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs, even in case of suppression of negative sequence current during unsymmetrical faults.
  Moreover, correct settings for the classical method in the presence of GFL IBRs are presented as a solution for relays without the advanced method.
  The novel algorithm is evaluated against the correctly parameterized Classical Reactance Method and the Distance Protection algorithm.

Systems and Control.title: Learning mechanical systems from real-world data using discrete forced Lagrangian dynamics
Systems and Control.summary: We introduce a data-driven method for learning the equations of motion of mechanical systems directly from position measurements. This is particularly relevant in system identification tasks where only positional information is available, such as motion capture, pixel data or low-resolution tracking. Our approach takes advantage of the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle and the forced discrete Euler-Lagrange equations to construct a physically grounded model of the system's dynamics. We decompose the dynamics into conservative and non-conservative components, which are learned separately using feed-forward neural networks. In the absence of external forces, our method reduces to a variational discretization of the action principle naturally preserving the symplectic structure of the underlying Hamiltonian system. We validate our approach on a variety of synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to baseline methods. In particular, we apply our model to (1) measured human motion data and (2) latent embeddings obtained via an autoencoder trained on image sequences. We demonstrate that we can faithfully reconstruct and separate both the conservative and forced dynamics, yielding interpretable and physically consistent predictions

Systems and Control.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
Systems and Control.summary: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable $\cosδ$, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66\% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

Systems and Control.title: PAC Infinite-Time Safety Guarantees for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Probabilistic Distributions
Systems and Control.summary: This paper studies infinite-time safety certification for discrete-time stochastic systems with continuous dynamics and unknown disturbance distributions that have full support on a known compact disturbance set. We develop a probably approximately correct (PAC) data-driven framework that uses only finitely many i.i.d. disturbance samples: with confidence at least $1-δ$, if the certification procedure accepts a candidate certificate defining a nonempty subset of a prescribed compact safe set, then the system, starting from any state in this subset, remains within the safe set for all future times with probability at least $1-ε$. Our approach builds on a fundamental characterization of infinite-time safety. We first prove that a robust invariant set exists within a compact safe set if and only if there exists an initial state from which the system remains in the safe set indefinitely with positive probability. This reduces infinite-time safety certification to two tractable subproblems: robust invariant-set computation and finite-horizon reach-avoid certification. We first compute a robust invariant set within the safe set, then use i.i.d. disturbance samples to certify, with PAC guarantees, a subset of initial states for which the probability of reaching this set within a finite horizon while remaining safe is at least a prescribed threshold. To our knowledge, this is the first PAC framework for infinite-time safety under unknown disturbance distributions. Finally, illustrative examples demonstrate the method using semi-definite programming.

Systems and Control.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part II: Underway Docking
Systems and Control.summary: In underway directional docking, a second-order nonholonomic problem, six pairs of states of two vehicles have to be made to match by two inputs. The key challenge is to design time-invariant feedback of the relative states and the leader's measured motion only, which makes the follower's convergence in range outpaced, with no sway actuation whatsoever, by the bearing and heading convergence of the follower relative to the leader's path. We begin with nonmodular backstepping, choosing speed and commanded heading jointly to control range and bearing. Curvature compensation and normalization of angular errors by different powers of range remove the range singularity from the model. Our construction passes from unicycle kinematics to the ships' zero-sideslip points and through the sway dynamics to the physical hulls. The design extends to a leader with a different hull and to a docking point astern or abeam of the leader, where we show that, while the leader turns, a follower without sway actuation holds the point only with a heading that differs from the leader's. With strict control Lyapunov construction, we achieve global $κ$-exponential convergence, with a rate independent of the initial error.

Systems and Control.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part I: Stabilization in Polar Coordinates
Systems and Control.summary: A surface vessel with surge force and yaw moment as inputs and no sway actuation cannot be stabilized at a fixed pose by continuous time-invariant feedback. We introduce a zero-sideslip point, a point whose position relative to the hull depends on the surge and sway speeds and whose velocity points along the vessel's heading at every instant, and show that it moves as a unicycle. This reduction allows the time-invariant, polar-coordinate steering laws of Todorovski et al. (2025) to be applied to the underactuated vessel without modification. With two steering laws, GloBa and BoLSA, we construct strict control Lyapunov functions and prove global asymptotic stability, first for a four-state model with surge speed and yaw rate as virtual inputs, and then, by one step of backstepping, for the full six-state model with surge force and yaw moment. The analysis extends to hulls with fore-aft asymmetric sway-yaw damping, excluded in prior work by the assumption of diagonal damping. Unlike prior time-varying designs, the time-invariant controller yields smooth, non-oscillatory trajectories, an important practical advantage for docking. The designs are validated in simulation on the Cybership I hull model.

Systems and Control.title: Range-Only Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Safe and Secure Target Circumnavigation
Systems and Control.summary: The safety and security of robotic systems are paramount when navigating hostile targets. This paper addresses the problem of circumnavigating an unknown target by a unicycle robot while ensuring it maintains a desired safe distance and remains within the sensing region around the target throughout its motion. The proposed controller design is based on a composite Lyapunov framework consisting of: (i) a quadratic Lyapunov function characterizing the target-circumnavigation objective, and (ii) a barrier Lyapunov function-based potential term enforcing the prescribed safety and sensing constraints. A notable feature of the proposed approach is that it relies exclusively on local range measurements between the robot and the target, achieved through a dynamic output-feedback controller that treats the range as the only measurable output. Using Lyapunov-based stability analysis together with an equivalent autonomous reformulation of the closed-loop dynamics, we establish asymptotic stability of the desired equilibrium while guaranteeing satisfaction of the prescribed safety and sensing constraints under the proposed controllers. Restrictive bounds on the post-design signals are also derived, and numerical simulations are presented to validate the proposed approach.

Systems and Control.title: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments
Systems and Control.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control. However, environmental perturbations, such as objects moving during execution, can undermine their reliability. Different policies exhibit complementary failures under mid-rollout perturbations, motivating selective switching between policies for recovery. Such switching can stall the robot during inference of the newly invoked policy or, if performed asynchronously, act on stale observations. We present AsyncMixVLA, an adaptive inference framework for proactive, asynchronous switching across heterogeneous VLA policies. A learned trigger balances recovery potential against intervention harm to selectively escalate to a higher-compute policy. AsyncMixVLA overlaps its inference with committed outgoing actions and aligns its context to the anticipated takeover state. On LIBERO-Long with mid-rollout perturbations, AsyncMixVLA improves perturbed task success from 69.5% to 77.1% over the lightweight policy. It achieves 84.9% overall success, comparable to 84.5% for synchronous switching, while reducing median exposed handoff latency from 226.5 ms to 0.1 ms. Without retraining or recalibration, it achieves 75.1% success across three unseen perturbation families, compared with 71.3% for the stronger constituent policy in aggregate.
Systems and Control.comment: Manuscript prepared for the DAC 2027 Research Track (IEEE conference format)

Systems and Control.title: Extended Deterministic Learning under Local Finite-Time Excitation
Systems and Control.summary: This paper develops an extension of classical deterministic learning (CDL) for the regulation of uncertain nonlinear systems, referred to as Extended Deterministic Learning (EDL). CDL relies on periodic or recurrent closed-loop trajectories to ensure that the locally active radial-basis-function (RBF) neurons satisfy a partial persistence-of-excitation (PE) condition. During regulation, however, the state approaches a constant operating point and continued excitation disappears. EDL preserves the local-learning mechanism of CDL while enabling locally accurate learning under a local finite-time excitation (local FTE) condition, which requires neither persistent excitation nor recurrent system trajectories. Specifically, an adaptive RBF controller is combined with filtered finite-time data storage. Under local FTE, the resulting scheme guarantees that all closed-loop signals are uniformly ultimately bounded, the regulation state converges exponentially to a small neighborhood of the desired operating point, and the neural weights associated with the locally active RBFs converge exponentially to small neighborhoods of their ideal values. Consequently, the unknown nonlinear dynamics are learned locally and accurately over the experienced region without requiring persistent excitation after the finite learning interval. A numerical example illustrates the improvement in local learning achieved by EDL over CDL.
Systems and Control.comment: submitted to 2027 American Control Conference

Systems and Control.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
Systems and Control.summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.
Systems and Control.comment: submitted to SICON

Systems and Control.title: Environment-Aware Probabilistic State Estimation of Continuum Robots from Planar Imaging
Systems and Control.summary: Continuum robots are compliant along their entire length, making them well suited to navigating confined environments where contact with surrounding structures is often unavoidable. However, this compliance makes their modeling more complex compared to rigid robots, especially under contact, so their state must often be estimated from information available during operation. In many applications, the environment is known in advance, for example from preoperative imaging in medicine or from design models in industrial inspection. We present a probabilistic state estimator that represents the known environment as a signed distance field, informing the estimated shape. Continuous in arclength and time, it estimates the full state from asynchronous measurements anywhere along the robot. It also fuses planar images of body-fixed markers from a moving camera with commanded actuation, so the robot needs no embedded sensors. In a simulated aortic arch and a hardware phantom, the estimator tracked the robot into the target branch, and with a single view, using the known environment lowered the tip error from 2.5% to 1.6% and from 20.0% to 11.3% of the robot length, respectively. The continuous estimate of the full state and its uncertainty can support navigation and control of sensorless continuum robots.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures

Systems and Control.title: Real-time Priority-aware UAS Arrival Planning Framework for Multi-layer UTM
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes a real-time, priority-aware UAS arrival-planning framework for multi-layer UTM terminal airspace represented as a funnel of concentric rings, discrete holding slots, connecting edges, and a landing pad. Managing dense arrivals is challenging because terminal resources are limited and UAS must remain spatially and temporally separated throughout their approaches. New arrivals, wind disturbances, and emergency landing requests further require rapid replanning beyond conventional landing-pad sequencing. To achieve computational tractability, the framework employs a greedy planning method that first establishes a priority-aware landing order and then plans the UAS sequentially. For each UAS, the method determines its slot assignments, traversal path, landing time, and slot entry and exit times while treating previously planned trajectories as fixed. Spatial and temporal constraints prevent conflicts on holding slots, connecting edges, and the landing pad. Within a rolling-horizon implementation, the framework incorporates new arrivals, reactively adjusts plans affected by wind disturbances, and prioritizes emergency UAS without altering completed operations. Computational results show that the method generates and updates feasible, conflict-free arrival plans within operational time limits while providing expedited landing access to emergency UAS. The results demonstrate the suitability of the proposed framework for responsive and safety-critical arrival management in dynamic multi-layer UTM environments. Video link: https://youtu.be/F9IP1dz-9PE
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to AIAA Journal of Aerospace and Information Systems

Systems and Control.title: A Shared-Autonomy Construction Robotic System for Overhead Works
Systems and Control.summary: We present the ongoing development of a robotic system for overhead work such as ceiling drilling. The hardware platform comprises a mobile base with a two-stage lift, on which a bimanual torso is mounted with a custom-designed drilling end effector and RGB-D cameras. To support teleoperation in dynamic environments with limited visibility, we use Gaussian splatting for online 3D reconstruction and introduce motion parameters to model moving objects. For safe operation around dynamic obstacles, we developed a neural configuration-space barrier approach for planning and control. Initial feasibility studies demonstrate the capability of the hardware in drilling, bolting, and anchoring, and the software in safe teleoperation in a dynamic environment. Experiment videos and results are available at https://kmk9846.github.io/Construction-Robot/
Systems and Control.comment: 5 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Presented at the ICRA 2025 Workshop on Future of Construction. v2: corrected an author name and added the project page link

Multiagent Systems.title: graspit-py: A Python Interface to GraspIt! for Grasp Planning Under Pose and Friction Uncertainty
Multiagent Systems.summary: In simulated multifingered grasps, pose error can change contacts formed during hand closure, while friction uncertainty changes the loads supported by those contacts. Existing C++ APIs and ROS 1 services provide programmatic GraspIt! access but require native bindings or a service transport layer for Python use and application-specific integration of contact geometry with uncertainty sampling. A Python workflow for these studies must connect native closure and contacts to caller-defined wrench scores, uncertainty samples, and command reconstruction. We present graspit-py, a Python interface to native GraspIt! operations that supplies this workflow. The interface provides native scene access, contact-wrench analysis, and configurable approach planning under pose and friction uncertainty. A grasp record associates the object-relative palm pose and closed independent coordinates with nominal contacts and quality scores evaluated under sampled pose and friction conditions. Our MuJoCo exporter derives serial hinge chains and affine joint couplings, including nonzero reference angles, and preserves individual collision components. Across 75 configurations of five hand models, maximum discrepancy between source and exported palm-frame vertex sets was approximately 1.3 micrometers against a 100-micrometer geometry tolerance. We isolated reference-angle and collision-component effects through controlled ablations and validated 1,920 directional task-wrench capacity calculations against independent Cartesian-force linear programs. In a common GraspIt! workload, median reset-close-score-state cycle latency through direct Python was 10.7% lower than through persistent ROS 1 services. An executable export-plan-reconstruct workflow and grasp examples on six hand models demonstrate how the contact, score, and joint representations support numerical analysis and command reconstruction.
Multiagent Systems.comment: Technical report. 31 pages, 8 figures, 9 tables. Code: https://github.com/coenwerem/graspit-py

Multiagent Systems.title: Portable Extended-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic for Scientific Computing Kernels
Multiagent Systems.summary:
Many scientific computations need more accuracy than IEEE double precision, but arbitrary precision is often too costly on CPUs and GPUs. Multi-float arithmetic fills this gap by representing each value as an unevaluated sum of IEEE numbers. Existing implementations are generally confined to a CPU, CUDA, or language-specific programming model.
  We present MultiFloats.cpp, a header-only C++17 library that uses Kokkos to compile the same extended-precision kernels for Serial, OpenMP, CUDA, and HIP. The library supports Float64x2 through Float64x4 (106--212 bits) and the corresponding Float32-based types. We evaluate it using seven SHOC-style kernels and compare against QD, CAMPARY, MPFR, and Julia MultiFloats.jl on A100, GH200, and AMD RX 780M systems. On A100, Float64x4 addition sustains 15,700 MOps/s, or 1.5 times CAMPARY; on CPU, vectorized Float64x4 operations are 4.2--6.6 times faster than QD's qd_real. Addition and multiplication produce 0 ULP error over 10,000 inputs, while Float64x4 division and square root remain within 1.71 and 17.9 ULP, respectively. Thus, extended precision can remain practical and portable without separate backend implementations.
Multiagent Systems.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables and as accepted in IEEE HPEC 2026

Databases.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
Databases.summary: Text-to-SQL systems built on large language models (LLMs) often aggregate over one-to-many and many-to-many joins, a classic trap: when the joined rows repeat an entity, a SUM or COUNT counts it more than once, yet the query runs and returns a plausible number. We characterize these fan-out errors by one condition on the relation an aggregate reads, which depends on two facts a schema does not show: each measure's grain, and how many rows a join on each key repeats. An audit that tests the condition on the data finds distorted gold answers for 4.2% of the dev questions of BIRD, a widely used benchmark, and BIRD's later, independent revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags as definite fan-out, against 16% of unflagged ones. We release BIRD-FanOut, 486 BIRD questions with reviewed gold, and GrainTraps, synthetic questions that set this trap and related ones. Across eight LLM agents, functional dependencies (FDs) computed from the data help no more than per-column statistics on GrainTraps, but grain-aware FDs, which also state each measure's grain and the repetition per key, cut fan-out errors on BIRD from 18.4% of runs to about 13%, also on held-out questions and without LLM judges. Accuracy rises less, because most remaining errors are not fan-out and BIRD's hints often prescribe the over-count. Text-to-SQL models should be given the grain of the data, and benchmark gold should be audited on the data. Code, data and benchmarks are available at https://github.com/ahmed-mahran/misqal
Databases.comment: 17 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables. Code, data and benchmarks: https://github.com/ahmed-mahran/misqal

Databases.title: A Design Space for Data Agents: Insights from KDD Cup 2026
Databases.summary: Data agents interpret analytical requests, gather evidence from heterogeneous sources, and compute results within finite resource budgets. We analyze the final code submissions of the ten highest-ranked teams in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents for Complex Data Analysis competition. We organize the observed design choices into three interacting layers, covering workflow orchestration, analytical functions, and working state. The comparison reveals recurring patterns for allocating computation in response to task progress, structuring evidence for computation and assessment, and preserving reusable artifacts with their provenance. Candidates that rely on the same evidence can inherit the same error, so interpreting their agreement requires tracing those dependencies. The design space motivates controlled evaluations of how resource allocation, evidence sharing, and targeted recovery affect task completion and correctness.
Databases.comment: 3 pages, 1 figure, 1 table

Databases.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
Databases.summary: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. Our experimental results show that AltoPIR outperforms existing CPU-based solutions by up to 50.1x.
Databases.comment: Code: https://github.com/GyuyeongKim/AltoPIR-public

Databases.title: Bound to be Complete: Efficient Verification for SQL Equivalence via U-Expressions
Databases.summary:
Automated verification of SQL query equivalence is a fundamental problem in database area. Recent works developed verifiers with guaranteed completeness, which can generate counterexamples to disprove non-equivalent queries and are useful in various scenarios. However, they have to solve complex formulas and can fail to produce counterexamples within a reasonable time budget.
  This paper presents a new complete verifier called SQLution, which not only greatly reduces the verification time, but also supports more SQL features. The key insight is to represent SQL semantics using U-expression, a functional algebra that can model SQL with significantly simpler formulas than prior works, thereby leading to more efficient SMT solving. To turn this insight into a practical verifier, SQLution further tackles two technical challenges associated with modeling SQL using U-expression, namely, the lack of tuple ordering and the presence of unbounded summations. In particular, to support tuple ordering, SQLution proposes order semantics encoding which combines U-expressions with first-order logic. To handle unbounded summation, SQLution introduces unbounded summation expansion to transform them into bounded summations, which can be directly encoded into FOL formulas. Evaluation shows that compared with state-of-the-art verifiers, SQLution can support all 271 non-equivalent query pairs derived from the Spider dataset and reduces verification time by up to 98.6%.

Databases.title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation
Databases.summary: Coupling a property-graph database to an external language-model server imposes a three-part socket tax: serialization overhead dwarfing microsecond graph reads, repeated prefill of verbose schemas, and blind decoding divorced from the live catalog and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) engine. We present Shoonya, from-scratch commercially clean (0.0% non-commercial or share-alike data) tri-modal (Python, Rust, OpenCypher) small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) co-designed with shoonya-infer, a zero-dependency pure-Rust runtime embedded inside the samyama-graph-enterprise address space. Direct GraphStore references unlock three database-native primitives: (1) an epoch-invalidated SchemaPrefixCache over a copy-on-write PagedKvArena accelerating warm CPU time-to-first-token by 4.91x--13.68x with O(1) DDL invalidation; (2) a 36 us columnar catalog and source-span logit mask enforcing valid ontology identifiers and verbatim spans; and (3) a sub-65 us read-only MVCC gate serving Tier-0 queries inside 389.8 MiB INT8 RSS (59.8--67.9 tok/s) with 0.0% hallucination leak. Rank-factorized tied embeddings (-74.5% vocabulary weights), atomic indentation tokens (0/421 indentation errors), 4:1 grouped-query attention with 2:1 cross-layer KV sharing (-93.75% INT8 KV memory), Warmup-Stable-Decay training, KnOTS SVD merging, Step-GRPO, and Rust Jacobi SVD governance keep 100% of layers heavy-tailed ($α\in [1.88, 2.20]$). Finally, we synthesize nine lessons across v0.1--v1.0, resolving a Reverse-Token-Density Distillation Trap via teacher scaling and zero-VRAM Verifier-Advantage-Gated Knowledge Distillation (AdvKD), recovering +13.61 MBPP points (33.07%) while reaching 100% validity on enrichment, grounded extraction, and tool planning.
Databases.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Open weights (Apache-2.0), shard provenance manifests, and Rust Jacobi SVD spectral certificates: https://huggingface.co/VaidhyaMegha/Shoonya

Emerging Technologies.title: Examining QRMI as a Unified Interface for Quantum-HPC Integration
Emerging Technologies.summary: The efficient and scalable integration of quantum resources into high-performance computing (HPC) environments requires standardized mechanisms for resource management, scheduling, and workflow orchestration across diverse and heterogeneous infrastructures. The Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) addresses this challenge through a thin, vendor-agnostic middleware layer that provides standardized APIs for scheduling, executing, and monitoring quantum workloads while exposing quantum resources as first-class schedulable resources alongside CPUs and GPUs. Although previous work demonstrated QRMI integration with the Slurm workload manager, its applicability across other workload managers remained unexamined. This paper extends the validation of QRMI to a broad range of workload managers, including PBS, LSF, Grid Engine, Kubernetes, and the Flux Framework, encompassing traditional batch schedulers, a cloud-native orchestration platform, and a graph-based scheduler. We examine the integration patterns, implementation requirements, and scheduler-specific considerations associated with each environment and compare QRMI with alternative approaches to quantum resource integration. We demonstrate that QRMI provides a portable and flexible abstraction layer that minimizes scheduler-specific modifications while enabling consistent access to heterogeneous quantum resources across both on-premises and cloud environments.
Emerging Technologies.comment: 12 pages, 3 tables, 1 figure, 3 listings, Published in the SC26 2nd International Workshop for Software Frameworks and Workload Management on Quantum-HPC Ecosystems (SFWM)

Emerging Technologies.title: Who Gets to Do Computing Research? Rethinking Access, Funding, and the Cost of Research -- How do we ensure that everyone with the ideas, ability, and desire to contribute to computing research can do so?
Emerging Technologies.summary:
The future of computing research will be shaped not just by the questions we ask, but also by who has the opportunity to pursue them. Major investments in advanced computing, including artificial/super intelligence (AI) and quantum computing (QC), are expanding opportunities for discovery and innovation. Pursuing these opportunities requires more than a promising idea: researchers also need time, infrastructure, technical expertise, and support to compete for and administer funding.
  Access to these resources varies across institutions and may shape who can participate and which research directions they can pursue. A healthy computing research ecosystem depends on research taking place at institutions with different missions and resources, not only at the best-resourced ones.
  Computing research spans a broad spectrum of resource requirements, from theoretical work and software developed by small teams to experiments requiring specialized hardware, large datasets, and substantial technical support. Preserving opportunities across this range requires understanding not only the resources needed to conduct research, but also the costs of securing them.
  What does it cost an institution -- and an individual researcher -- to participate in computing research? This article invites computing researchers, university leaders, funding agencies, and industry partners to examine how funding structures, access to infrastructure, administrative responsibilities, and institutional expectations affect research opportunities, and how meaningful pathways can be preserved across institutions with different missions and resources.
Emerging Technologies.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, Computing Community Conference article initially posted on Medium https://medium.com/@computing-community-consortium/who-gets-to-do-computing-research-rethinking-access-funding-and-the-cost-of-research-43caacd7b71b

Emerging Technologies.title: MM-Open5x: Practical Conformal Electronics via Multi-Material Multi-Axis Additive Manufacturing
Emerging Technologies.summary: Multi-axis, multi-material additive manufacturing enables the production of conformal electronic systems that are difficult to realise using planar processes and can offer enhanced performance; however, accessibility and reproducibility remain challenging. This paper presents MM-Open5x, an open and low-cost multi-material, multi-axis additive manufacturing workflow for practical conformal electronics. The workflow spans design, simulation, toolpath generation, fabrication, testing, and assembly, and is released alongside complete design files, toolpaths, and representative G-code. Representative case studies demonstrate both the benefits and limitations of multi-axis deposition in practice, explicitly documenting common failure modes, calibration sensitivities, assembly bottlenecks, and material variability. Rather than prescribing an optimal solution, MM-Open5x is presented as a transparent, reproducible foundation upon which a broader community can iterate, extend, and apply conformal electronics workflows across diverse application domains.
Emerging Technologies.comment: 4 pages, 5 figures, To appear in the Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Additively Manufactured Electronic Systems (AMES) 2026

Emerging Technologies.title: Analytical Modeling and Optimal GPU Provisioning for Disaggregated LLM Inference
Emerging Technologies.summary: We present OSplit, an exact analytical method that enables efficient partitioning of a GPU L1 domain into prefill and decode workers, including sharding for classical and advanced GPUs. OSplit takes into consideration model parameters, enabling any inference model to be partitioned into prefill and decode workers with a goal of producing the maximum throughput possible. OSplit is based on a capacity model that takes as inputs the model, the loading scheme (batch size, max sequence length), and models an inference serving framework (vLLM) and computes the efficiency of each GPU. For this, we model H100 and GB300 GPUs, and model a scale-up domain, along with FlashAttention-based kernels. OSplit first computes an optimal collective generation policy, which gives inputs to the capacity model that enables optimal split of prefill and decode GPUs. We evaluate our scheme over H100 (NVL8) and GB300 (NVL72) using vLLM inference serving and show throughput, predicted and measured latency, showing near-perfect theoretical-to-measured values over leading LLMs (Llama and Qwen)

Emerging Technologies.title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage
Emerging Technologies.summary: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost. Group-wise integer quantization stores every weight of a group at the same precision, although the input channels of a group differ in sensitivity. We present BITSHARE, a codebook-free weight format that keeps the integer grid and the dequantizer of group-wise quantization but varies precision within each group. Sensitivity-aware binning places the channels of each group into three bins at fixed positions, and static bit sharing with optimal bit-value allocation lets the less sensitive weights share their lower bits, each stored once per group or once per pair of weights. A sharing-aware version of GPTQ chooses every stored value, with no fine-tuning and no codebook. BITSHARE has two modes. BITSHARE-U gives every group the same layout, so its decoder routes bits by fixed wiring, while BITSHARE-N chooses a layout per group within the same bit budget. With calibration on the Pile and at the same storage, both modes have lower perplexity than GPTQ at 3 and 2 bits on WikiText-2 and C4. At 2 bits across Llama-2 and Llama-3 models, BITSHARE-N lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by up to 70% against SliM-LLM and up to 35% against GPTAQ. At the 2-bit perplexity of SliM-LLM, BITSHARE-U stores 13.6-19.4% fewer bits per weight, cutting DRAM weight traffic by the same fraction. A verified hardware decoder implementation synthesized in SkyWater 130 nm reconstructs BITSHARE weights at the throughput of INT-n and SliM-LLM decoders.

Emerging Technologies.title: APUF-SNG: A Low-Cost Arbiter-PUF Stochastic Number Generator with Tunable Output Probability
Emerging Technologies.summary: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes numerical values as probabilistic bit-streams and enables arithmetic operations using simple logic gates, offering a promising paradigm for low- cost, fault-tolerant, and highly parallel computation. However, the accuracy and efficiency of SC systems depend on the quality of the stochastic number generator (SNG). Conventional SNGs rely on pseudo-random or quasi-random generators, whose deterministic nature introduces periodicity, correlation, and bias, limiting achievable accuracy and robustness. This paper proposes a low- cost arbiter physical unclonable function (APUF)-based SNG that operates in near-metastable delay conditions to generate true- random stochastic bit-streams with controllable output probabilities. By selecting input challenges that drive the path delay difference toward a target value, the resulting output probability is governed by intrinsic device noise, eliminating the need for conventional random-number generators and comparator-based SNGs. The proposed design inherits the low hardware overhead and statistical independence properties of the APUF structure. A probabilistic model and a challenge selection method are developed to characterize and control the stochastic behavior. An 8-stage APUF-SNG matches the 1% mean absolute error of state- of-the-art true-random SNGs at 1024-bit streams and occupies 116μm^2 in 45nm, 2.5x and 7x smaller than the TRNG-based and Sobol-based generator designs, respectively.

Emerging Technologies.title: Coupled Dynamical System for Sparsemax Attention
Emerging Technologies.summary: We present a family of coupled dynamical systems that compute sparsemax attention. Each system fuses query-key similarity and normalization into a single physical relaxation. Specifically, we cast sparsemax attention as a constrained energy minimization problem and derive a pair of coupled differential equations: one drives the energy minimization and the other enforces the constraint. At equilibrium, the system state gives exactly the sparsemax attention probabilities. We realize this formulation with continuous Ising spins and with Kuramoto oscillators. These relaxations run natively on emerging non-von Neumann platforms such as Ising machines, which have demonstrated orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency than digital processors, yet have so far been used mostly for unconstrained quadratic combinatorial optimization. Because analog hardware has limited precision and is noisy, we simulate both systems under these non-idealities, and inference quality degrades gracefully. Our formulation extends these emerging computing substrates from combinatorial optimization to attention, opening a path toward a new class of physical accelerators for transformer inference.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: MidasTUI: Instant Tangible User Interfaces for Wearable Displays using Everyday Objects
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: While wearable displays can bring digital workspaces anywhere, interaction remains limited by mid-air gestures that lack tactile feedback and induce fatigue, or controllers that are cumbersome to carry. We present MidasTUI, a system that instantly transforms arbitrary everyday objects into opportunistic tangible user interfaces through brief interaction demonstrations. For example, a user can slide an earbud case across a table as a mouse, enabling opportunistic interaction without carrying a dedicated input device. MidasTUI detects when a user is holding and moving an object using the wearable display camera and a Transformer-based temporal classifier. It then infers the intended input modality (e.g., slider, mouse, keypad) from hand movement and maps the tracked hand-object interaction to an application function. Our evaluations demonstrate reliable cross-object and cross-user generalization. A comparative user study further shows that grounding interaction in everyday objects reduces physical burden and improves perceived usability and control relative to mid-air interaction.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Project page link: https://midastui.github.io/

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Supporting Without Taking Over: AI Support in Gratitude Writing
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Gratitude writing can support well-being, but independent practice may lack guidance. Generative AI could help while shaping reflection, agency, and ownership. We investigated how gratitude-writing format and AI-assistance mode influence well-being and writing experiences. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (N=401), participants completed a gratitude reflection or a gratitude letter using two AI-assistance modes: scaffolding, which provided reflective questions after inactivity, or co-writing, which offered inline text suggestions. Participants' well-being improved after using our AI-assisted gratitude-writing system, consistent with the activity's intended benefits. However, participants' experiences revealed a trade-off between the AI-support types: co-writing received higher usability ratings, yet its immediacy could disrupt writing, and greater suggestion acceptance was associated with weaker perceived agency. Scaffolding supported stronger perceived human ownership but was sometimes overlooked. These findings extend human-AI writing research beyond productivity and text quality by showing how AI involvement shapes psychological outcomes and the experience of self-guided, emotionally meaningful writing.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Tap-to-Adapt: Learning User-Aligned Response Timing for Speech Agents
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Aligning speech agents' response initiation with users' expectations remains challenging. We introduce Tap-to-Adapt, a framework for interactive speech systems in which manual activation and interruption provide both immediate response control and online supervision for personalized initiation timing. To learn from sparse corrections and recent feedback, we introduce \emph{Balanced Proximal Replay for History-conditioned Timing} (BPRHT) as its response initiation timing control mechanism, combining frozen speech representations, class-balanced replay with proximal regularization, and recent correction history. We evaluate acoustic backbones for BPRHT on recorded speech and compare update rules and recent-history configurations in simulation. The selected replay and history mechanisms lower simulated correction rates relative to their respective baselines. To reduce new users' cold-start correction burden, we evaluate shared initialization in a two-stage user study. Stage~1 established shared initialization with 20 participants, locking the average of earlier participants' final heads upon parameter and opening-correction plateaus. Stage~2 assigned 48 new participants equally to online adaptation with or without shared initialization, or frozen shared initialization. Online adaptation without shared initialization had more opening corrections per minute than with it (rate ratio 1.69, 95\% confidence interval 1.15--2.49). Final-block correction rates were similar across conditions. Online updates accompanied reported speaking and waiting adjustments. Declining corrections under frozen parameters also suggest user accommodation. Code and 1,000 labeled pilot recordings are available at: https://github.com/ZihongHe/tap_to_adapt

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
Human-Computer Interaction.summary:
Multi-session hiring assistants must infer evolving recruiter preferences and decision patterns across projects and time. We introduce Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. We also introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes through prompted reflection or reinforcement learning. We compare these approaches with no memory, full-history context, and conversation search, and evaluate Jev-class models for index navigation and GPT-5.6 Luna as a lower-cost alternative to GPT-5.4.
  In our evaluation, OKF-indexed retrieval achieves low-priority preference F1 scores of 0.93-0.95 at medium and high preference overlap between hiring projects. It significantly outperforms full-history context and conversation search in both settings, and no memory at high overlap, while using 69% fewer context tokens than full history. Procedure Memory reduces conversational turns by up to 39% relative to no memory. Qualitative and long-horizon evaluations provide evidence of temporal reasoning, with RL-learned procedures achieving 60% on both correct abstention and exact-field identification. Jev-class models improve conversational efficiency but more frequently miss temporally relevant evidence, highlighting the importance of evidence selection.
  On PersonaMem-v2, Procedure Memory with OKF retrieval achieves 50.2% accuracy versus 48.6% for full-history context and 29.0% for no memory, using 90.5% fewer reader input tokens than full history. GPT-5.6 Luna performs comparably to GPT-5.4 at lower cost. These findings highlight the value of structured episodic memory and learned decision procedures for efficient personalization and temporal reasoning.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Includes supplementary appendices with experimental configurations, prompts, evaluation protocols, and learned procedure examples

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures neural activity associated with human perception and decision-making. It provides human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems with measurable evidence for event recognition, situation assessment, and action preparation. External sensing cannot easily provide such evidence. However, the quality and complementarity of this evidence vary across samples, and existing EEG fusion methods do not explicitly determine when EEG improves a prediction. We therefore framed selective EEG use as a sample-wise incremental-value estimation problem and proposed Value Estimation and Constraint-Aware Triage for Adoption (VECTA). VECTA separates the generation of an EEG-informed Fusion prediction from the decision about whether it should replace the existing Base prediction. The framework uses system gain to quantify the loss reduction from Base to Fusion and matching gain to assess whether benefits arise from sample-matched EEG. A signed-value learner estimates system gain from decision-time evidence and prioritizes high-value Fusion outputs under budget constraints. Cross-subject evaluations on three HRC datasets showed that matched Fusion outperformed shuffled controls. Estimated gains tracked realized gains, with Spearman correlations of 0.347-0.612 and positive-gain areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.708-0.842. Under budget constraints, VECTA reduced Brier loss and harmful Fusion adoption and achieved the highest mean normalized AUBC across three datasets among the selective-decision methods evaluated. Validation on three external multi-modal datasets showed that VECTA could be applied directly as a post-hoc decision layer to task-specific predictors without retraining. These results show that selective Fusion adoption can translate the uneven utility of EEG into system-level gains.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Research on serendipity-oriented recommender systems has focused on algorithms that recommend unexpected yet useful items. However, serendipity is increasingly viewed as a user experience shaped by both algorithmic outputs and system features. This study positions recommendations not as the primary goal users pursue but as an environmental affordance that creates opportunities for discovery during other activities. We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely arrange movies into collection zones. For each collection, RecField provides attribute-based recommendation lists labeled according to their recommendation perspectives. A between-subjects experiment ($N$ = 57) examined the effects of recommendations on discoveries made during a foreground task of creating and organizing personal movie profiles. Although recommendations did not significantly affect environment-level perceived serendipity, ratings of encounter-related aspects tended to be higher, with small effect sizes. At the individual-movie level, favorites in the recommendation condition received significantly higher ratings for stimulating the desire to watch and broadening preferences, but not for novelty or unexpectedness. Notably, only 14\% of evaluated favorites in the recommendation condition were added directly from recommendation lists. Differences in ratings showed similar effect sizes even when the analysis was restricted to favorites added through other routes. These findings suggest that embedded recommendations can contribute to serendipitous experiences both directly through item acceptance and indirectly by prompting users' own exploration and re-evaluation. They also highlight the value of evaluating serendipity at both the environment and item levels and the limitations of relying solely on direct recommendation acceptance rates.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 17 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables

Human-Computer Interaction.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification. In human-AI research partnerships, confidence can therefore outgrow evidence through three mechanisms: recursive reinforcement, loss of provenance and miscalibrated reliance on AI-generated contributions. Verification debt accumulates when such contributions are carried into later claims or decisions without adequate scrutiny. Accordingly, we propose the Socratic Pause as a deliberate checkpoint at consequential decision gates, where an AI contribution remains provisional while a researcher examines its basis. The PAUSE protocol structures this examination through five steps: Pin down the claim, Ask and challenge, Uncover assumptions and alternatives, Scrutinise the evidence and Exercise judgement. It concludes with a recorded decision to accept, revise, reject or defer the contribution. We show how AI research tools can support this practice without displacing human judgement, and outline a framework for evaluating whether it improves verification, decision-making and independent understanding. The aim is to preserve the freedom to explore with AI while ensuring that those responsible for the work can say what was examined, what remains uncertain and why the next step is justified.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Prompt Engineer: Analyzing Hard and Soft Skill Requirements in the AI Job Market
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has prompted speculation about a new job role: the prompt engineer. However, empirical evidence on how common such positions are and what skills employers expect of them remains scarce. In this paper, we present a data-driven analysis of a snapshot of LinkedIn job postings for data and AI roles taken in April 2025, after LLMs had entered everyday work but before LLM-based agents became widely adopted. We analyzed 20,662 job postings on LinkedIn for prompt engineers (72 postings) and four established data and AI roles: data scientist, data engineer, data analyst, and machine learning engineer. We find that prompt engineer roles were rare even at this point in time, making up less than 0.5% of the postings across the five roles we sampled. Because our snapshot predates the widespread adoption of LLM-based agents, we argue that the data captures the role of prompt engineer under favorable conditions. Whether its share has since declined is an open question that later snapshots can test. Despite its rarity, prompt engineering has a distinct skill profile. Prompt engineer postings emphasize AI knowledge (22.8%), communication (21.9%), prompt design (18.7%), and creative problem-solving (15.8%). These soft and hard skill requirements differ significantly from those of the four established roles. Taken together, the distinct skill profile and the scarcity of dedicated postings suggest that prompt engineering is best understood not as a profession of its own, but as a distinct skill that is useful across many professions. Our findings inform job seekers, employers, and educators about how to position prompt engineering in the evolving AI workforce.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 23 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables

Human-Computer Interaction.title: On Semiotic-Grounded Interpretive Evaluation of Generative Art
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Interpretation is essential to deciphering the language of art: audiences communicate with artists by recovering meaning from visual artifacts. However, current Generative Art (GenArt) evaluators primarily emphasize surface-level image quality or literal prompt adherence, failing to assess the deeper symbolic or contextual meaning intended by the creator. We formalize this observation using Peircean computational semiotic theory that models Human-GenArt Interaction (HGI) as cascaded semiosis. This framework reveals that artistic meaning is conveyed through iconic, symbolic, and indexical modes, whereas appearance-centered evaluators tend to emphasize the iconic mode. Building on this account, we propose SemJudge, an interpretation-centric evaluation framework that uses a Hierarchical Semiosis Graph (HSG) to reconstruct meaning conveyance from prompt to generated artifact. Experiments on an interpretation-intensive benchmark, SemiosisArt, show that SemJudge aligns more closely with human judgments than existing baselines. User studies further demonstrate that SemJudge produces deeper, more insightful artistic interpretations. We hope these findings pave the way for GenArt to move beyond the generation of "pretty" images toward a medium capable of understanding and expressing complex human experience. Project page: https://github.com/songrise/SemJudge
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: ACM MM 2026

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Interacting with Alexa: A Longitudinal Case Study of Voice Assistant Use in Down Syndrome
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: As life expectancy for individuals with Down syndrome (DS) continues to increase, supporting cog- nitive engagement, everyday autonomy, and participation throughout adulthood has become an important research priority. Conversational voice assistants have emerged as promising assistive tech- nologies for these purposes, yet evidence regarding their long-term use in naturalistic settings remains limited. This paper presents a longitudinal case study of the everyday use of Amazon Alexa by an adult with Down syndrome over nine months in a real domestic environment. The study combines analyses of interaction logs, audio recordings, and qualitative observations to investigate usage pat- terns, interaction performance, communicative adaptation, and the integration of the voice assistant into everyday life. Results show that Alexa became progressively embedded in daily routines, sup- porting entertainment, information access, and autonomy-related activities. Longitudinal analyses reveal stable interaction patterns, reduced retry behavior, and the emergence of effective communi- cation strategies, while qualitative observations highlight increasing communicative engagement and the value of proactive reminders.
