PyTorch can therefore compute gradients of quantities such as cell areas, volumes, and interface areas with respect to the generator positions, so that these quantities can be optimized using standard gradient-based methods. The package also includes tools for extracting interfaces between groups of cells and for exporting meshes. For one million points using 28 threads, VoroPlex is 46 times faster than SciPy in 2D and 39 times faster in 3D. We demonstrate the package with three applications: centroidal Voronoi tessellations with a variable density, meshing of 2D shapes defined by signed distance functions, and the design of foams with a preferred cell orientation.

Mathematical Software.title: CAMPS: Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers
Mathematical Software.summary: Mixed-precision solvers usually assign a fixed precision to each algorithmic component. This makes it hard to reuse a lower-precision solver at different depths inside a higher-precision solver. We introduce CAMPS (Composable Adapters for Mixed-Precision Solvers), a framework that uses iterative refinement to connect solvers across precisions. An adapter computes residuals and updates in the precision of its parent and passes each correction solve to a child solver in a lower precision. The child can be a direct solver, an iterative solver, or another adapter. The adapter checks every correction and keeps it if the residual does not increase. We prove three results. Adapters can be placed at any compatible set of precision boundaries in a solver tree without breaking the solver interface. Every output that the root solver reports as successful satisfies a backward-error bound set by the stopping tolerance and the root precision. Convergence follows from one sufficient condition per boundary, computed from the leaves of the tree to its root. We test five configurations on dense and sparse systems in 64-bit, 32-bit, and 16-bit floating-point arithmetic (FP64, FP32, and FP16). On dense well-conditioned systems, CAMPS is up to 9.6x faster than an FP64 direct solver for a single solve that includes the factorization. On sparse nonsymmetric systems, a three-precision hierarchy is the fastest method we tested. Compared with our implementation of the nested solver F3R, CAMPS is as fast and uses about 3.4x less peak memory. CAMPS does not always win. Plain conjugate gradient is faster on sparse symmetric positive definite systems. On very ill-conditioned systems, FP32 corrections fail, and the adapter detects the failure and switches to an FP64 fallback.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Linear Single-Source Shortest Path, Almost
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We give a comparison-addition algorithm for single-source shortest paths in undirected graphs with nonnegative real edge lengths. For each input with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, its expected running time is $O(m+n\log\log\log n)$. It terminates almost surely. Every terminating run returns exact distances and a shortest-path tree on the reachable vertices. The bound is independent of the ratio of edge lengths and is linear whenever $m=Ω(n\log\log\log n)$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Robust large-scale approximate solutions of the constrained Kemeny aggregation ranking problem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The Kemeny aggregation ranking problem consists of computing the consensus rankings of an election with respect to the well-known Kemeny-Young voting method. These consensus rankings satisfy many fundamental properties and are the geometric medians of the votes in the election under the Kendall-tau distance which counts the number of pairwise disagreements. While having various applications in computational social choice, machine learning, operations research, and biology, the problem of computing the consensus rankings is NP-hard and encounters a severe bottleneck in practice. In this paper, we consider the more general Kemeny aggregation ranking problem under immutable input pairwise constraints and propose robust and scalable approximate methods with provable guarantees. We thus provide an algorithmic solution to the more general constrained problem of incorporating a posteriori immutable pairwise constraints into past rankings (e.g., historical voter ballots or legacy laboratory assays) without incurring the cost of generating new data. Our base algorithm $Γ$-XCC provides a source of rankings with a bounded constant approximation factor. $Γ$-XCC generalizes the Copeland ranking method and satisfies the constrained Condorcet consistency property, an extension of the Condorcet winner criterion for elections with immutable pairwise constraints. Thereby, our methods provide large-scale solutions that address the reliability and explainability issues. Our algorithms are also applicable to weighted tournaments with input pairwise constraints and satisfy similar properties in this larger context.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Pinwheel Scheduling is PSPACE-Complete
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Pinwheel Scheduling is a classical periodic scheduling problem, receiving as input the deadlines $d_i$ of $n$ tasks and asking for an infinite schedule with one task per time unit, such that every task $i$ is scheduled at least once in every $d_i$ time units. Holte, Mok, Rosier, Tulchinsky, and Varvel introduced the problem in 1989 and showed that it lies in \(\PSPACE\). Its exact complexity has been open since then. \(\NP\)-hardness for explicitly listed deadlines was established only recently, and membership in \(\NP\) is open.
  In this work we prove that Pinwheel Scheduling is \(\PSPACE\)-complete when the deadlines are written in binary. This finally settles the long-standing open question about the complexity of Pinwheel Scheduling. We present a chain of reductions, starting from Periodic 3-SAT, a classical \(\PSPACE\)-complete problem, and using two newly-defined intermediate periodic scheduling problems. These intermediate problems can be seen as periodically assigning tasks to days, with each day containing a fixed number of slots (\emph{hours}) in which tasks are scheduled. In the first of these problems, each day is additionally allowed to contain \emph{breaks}, that is, hours in which no task can be scheduled.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realize maximum-weight independent set encoding on unit-disk graphs under the ideal blockade model, but embedding nonlocal interactions requires auxiliary atoms and limits the size of tractable instances. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, uniform cell weights guarantee that every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution of the original problem, even when local copies disagree. For binary quadratic objectives subject to pairwise Boolean constraints, every feasible optimum yields consistent active copies and a target weight given by an explicit constant offset minus the source objective. A rectangular variant of the architecture further encodes minimum set cover problem. Prior to constraint-induced site deletions, the full layout requires $2n^2 - n$ sites, halving the leading-order site count of a fixed complete-grid reference, while activity pruning yields an exact site count set by the propagation span. Across 18 paired benchmarks with independent ordering from a shared candidate pool, the layout reduces site counts by 12.1%-54.0%.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 17 pages,6 figures

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Min-Plus Products and Dynamic Programming with Few Violations of the Adjacent Monge Inequalities
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Local rewards can introduce negative adjacent mixed differences into a convex transition cost. If a cost array $B$ has $s(B)$ such differences, we express it as a Monge array minus $s(B)$ weighted rectangles and sweep its columns, maintaining the lower envelope of the active rows. For explicit finite $n\times n$ matrices $A,B$ and $L=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$, we compute $A\otimes B$ and the smallest minimizing index for every entry in $\mathcal{O}(n^2L+ns(B)L^3)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ space, giving near-quadratic time for arbitrary $A$ when $s(B)=\mathcal{O}(n)$, including right factors with $Θ(n^2)$ positive differences.
  For block costs given by a constant-time Monge oracle and $r$ signed rectangle corrections, the sweep activates each row when its prefix optimum becomes available and computes an optimal contiguous partition in $\mathcal{O}((n+r)L^3)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(n+r)$ working space. The sweep handles convex transitions with interval rules and assigns one rectangle to each internal edge or hyperedge reward in a convex block cost, giving near-linear exact algorithms on sparse inputs for ordered graph modularity, weighted contiguous cluster editing, all-or-nothing HyperLam, and bounded-rank strict hypergraph modularity.
  Let $c_{\mathrm{APSP}}$ denote the deterministic exponent of all-pairs shortest paths with polynomially bounded integer weights. For fixed $3-c_{\mathrm{APSP}}<α\le1$, any deterministic $\mathcal{O}(n^β)$-time min-plus product algorithm for polynomially bounded integer matrices with $s(B)\le n^{1+α}$ satisfies $β\ge c_{\mathrm{APSP}}-1+α$. The reduction from general integer min-plus multiplication uses right factors obtained from $(j-k)^2$ by at most $n^{1+α}$ interval discounts, with $Θ(n^2)$ positive differences and all remaining differences negative.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Low-degree hardness rules out eigenvalue tests but not eigenvector tests
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study what low-degree hardness implies for spectral tests, with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) as the null distribution. We show that, once a fixed amount of Gaussian noise is added, it rules out every test based on eigenvalues, but not tests based on eigenvectors. For eigenvalues, if the low-degree advantage vanishes at logarithmic degree, then the joint law of the noisy eigenvalues converges to that of the GOE in total variation. For eigenvectors, we construct planted distributions with vanishing low-degree advantage whose eigenvalues follow the GOE law exactly at every noise level, yet whose noisy eigenvectors still distinguish them from the GOE. A single eigenvector can suffice. After a small amount of noise, a polynomial-time test that uses only the span of a fixed fraction of the top eigenvectors also succeeds, even when the low-degree advantage vanishes at a prescribed polylogarithmic degree.
  To prove the eigenvalue result, we split the noise into three increments. The first uses the low-degree assumption to establish eigenvalue rigidity. The second couples the two spectra through Dyson Brownian motion and applies homogenization to obtain a transport estimate. The third uses Gaussian smoothing to convert this estimate into closeness in total variation.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 65 pages, 4 figures

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Toward a human-friendly proof of a polynomial bound for the Directed Grid Theorem
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015] states that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph of directed treewidth at least $f(k)$ contains a cylindrical grid of order $k$ as a butterfly minor. Their function is not elementary, and Hatzel, Kreutzer, Garlet Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] improved it to a tower of exponentials of height $22$, by a proof in three stages through paths and cycles of well-linked sets. In this paper we prove each stage with a polynomial bound, so that $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial of degree $20\,031\,568$. As a consequence, Younger's conjecture, proved by Reed, Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas [Combinatorica, 1996], holds with a polynomial bound: for the polynomial $f$ that we construct, every digraph without $k$ pairwise disjoint cycles has a feedback vertex set of size at most $(k-1)f(k)$. In fact, beyond cycles, we obtain polynomial packing-covering bounds for every strongly connected digraph that is a butterfly minor of a cylindrical grid.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Uniform Guarded Bootstrapping for Topology-Sensitive Directed Shortest Paths
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
On a source star, every leaf distance is an input weight. Thus computing labeled distances need not reveal their order. For a rooted directed topology, let $K$ be the least worst-case sum of comparisons and additions among finite deterministic programs specialized to that topology and correct for every nonnegative weighting.
  We give one deterministic program that takes the graph as input. This graph-input-uniform algorithm has total comparison-addition RAM time $O(m+n+KΦ(K)\exp(O(\log_2^*(K+2))))$, where $n$ and $m$ count vertices and arcs, and $Φ$ is a regularized product of successive logarithms. An active core is the small graph remaining after directly recoverable distances are separated. The algorithm chooses its parameters from the core size.
  Frozen entry ceilings let each interrupted local call be replayed on a small completion, whose complete-run bound controls the stopped work. The cost coefficient satisfies a linear one-step recurrence, yielding at most exponential growth in the number of generations. This permits a depth chosen from the measured core size.
  For $m=O(n)$, the solver gives $O(n\sqrt{\log n}(\log\log n)^{1/4+o(1)})$ time, improving the sparse directed bound of Duan, Mao, Shu, and Yin. A complementary result uses reusable dominator calibration for changing seed vectors on a fixed weighted graph.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 48 pages. An earlier version was publicly posted as STOC 2027 submission #1592 on 2 November 2026 at 11:59 pm AoE (3 November 2026, 7:59 pm Asia/Shanghai): https://sigact-stoc.github.io/stoc2027/. This arXiv version updates the related-work discussion to cite arXiv:2611.26453v2. It builds on the resource framework and active-core reduction in arXiv:2609.04825v1

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Parameterized Complexity of Finding a Maximum Common Vertex Subgraph Without Isolated Vertices
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In this paper, we study the Maximum Common Vertex Subgraph problem: Given two input graphs $G_1,G_2$ and a non-negative integer $h$, is there a common subgraph $H$ on at least $h$ vertices such that there is no isolated vertex in $H$. In other words, each connected component of $H$ has at least $2$ vertices. This problem naturally arises in graph theory along with other variants of the well-studied Maximum Common Subgraph problem and also has applications in computational social choice. We show that this problem is NP-hard and provide an FPT algorithm when parameterized by $h$. Next, we conduct a study of the problem on common structural parameters like vertex cover number, maximum degree, treedepth, pathwidth and treewidth of one or both input graphs. We derive a complete dichotomy of parameterized results for our problem with respect to individual parameterizations as well as combinations of parameterizations from the above structural parameters. This provides us with a deep insight into the complexity theoretic and parameterized landscape of this problem.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (SOFSEM 2027)

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Square-root comparison, Turnpike, and exact semidefinite feasibility
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Given positive integers $a_i,K$, put $S=\sum_{i=1}^k\sqrt{a_i}$. We construct a realizable Turnpike instance in which the minimum spacing of distinct distances and the smallest nonzero addition residual are both at most $|S-K|$ when $S\ne K$. With approximation oracles, one three-distance realizability query decides $S\le K$. For unordered lists of radical sums with nonnegative rational coefficients, a polynomial-time substitution by integers preserves every normalized ruler. We give the classical reduction of square-root comparison to exact semidefinite feasibility in both threshold directions. The comparison enters through numerical separation and marked sorting; the integer recoding needs no such comparison for unordered reconstruction.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, 1 table

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: On the Assadi Liu Tarjan Auction Algorithm for Bipartite Matching: Simplification, Alternative Analysis, and Hard Instance
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Assadi, Liu, and Tarjan [SOSA'21] gave an auction algorithm that outputs a $(1-ε)$-approximation to Maximum Matching in bipartite graphs. Their algorithm computes a sequence of $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ maximal matchings in subgraphs of the input graph and can be implemented in the multi-pass streaming setting with $O(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ passes in a straightforward manner, which constitutes the state-of-the-art pass/approximation trade-off result in the multi-pass streaming setting. Their analysis uses tools from combinatorial auctions and, at its heart, relies on a clever potential function argument. Their proof, however, provides only limited insight into the inner workings of the algorithm. In this paper, we revisit the ALT-algorithm and present the following contributions. Simplification: The ALT-algorithm is built upon a freezing mechanism where vertices on one side of the bipartition that have already been rematched $Θ(\frac{1}ε)$ times over the course of the algorithm remain matched to their current partner forever. We show that this mechanism is in fact unnecessary, i.e., no special treatment of such vertices is needed. Alternative Analysis: We give an alternative analysis of the algorithm that is based on augmenting paths. Our analysis allows for a reinterpretation as one that follows the traditional approach of searching for and eliminating augmenting paths. Our analysis also copes with the removal of the freezing mechanism in a natural way, whereas the analysis of Assadi et al. strictly depends on its use. Hard Instance: We provide the first hard instance on which the algorithm requires $Ω(\frac{1}{ε^2})$ iterations/maximal matching computations. The instance is a simple path graph, where we exhibit a cyclic behaviour that prevents fast progress.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: ESA 2026 (track S). Update to author details

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Testing Expansion without Connectivity via Return Probabilities
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study whether every connected component of a bounded-degree graph is an edge expander, given access to its neighbor lists. Dinur and Goldreich give a tester using $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)n^α$ queries for every fixed $α>2/3$. We obtain \[
  \widetilde O_{d,c,β}\!\left(\frac{n^{1/2+β}}{\varepsilon}
  +\frac{\sqrt n}{\varepsilon^4}\right) \] queries for every fixed $0<β\le1$. The tester accepts graphs whose components have edge expansion at least $c$ and rejects graphs $\varepsilon$-far from having edge expansion at least $κβc^2/d$ in every component (for an absolute constant $κ>0$), each with probability at least $2/3$. No structural promise is imposed on the input.
  The tester compares pairwise collision probabilities at two walk lengths and starts further walks at vertices where sampled endpoints coincide. These additional samples control the contribution of vertices with larger return probabilities. We show that the resulting conditions force the longer walk to be nearly uniform on an induced expander with few edges leaving it. For fixed degree $d\ge3$ and completeness threshold $0<c<(d-2\sqrt{d-1})/2$, we show that a sufficiently small rejection expansion threshold of $γd$ requires $n^{1/2+Ω_d(γ)}$ queries when $\varepsilon$ is a sufficiently small multiple of $γ$. Thus the dependence of the excess query exponent on the rejection threshold is optimal up to constant factors in this regime. We also prove an $Ω(\sqrt{n/\log n})$ lower bound for Cayley graphs at infinitely many input sizes.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Parameterized Algorithms for Minimum Sum Vertex Cover on Dense Graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The \textsc{Minimum Sum Vertex Cover} (MSVC) problem asks for a linear ordering of the vertices of a graph that minimizes the sum, over all edges, of the position of the earlier endpoint. We study its parameterized complexity on graphs that become a clique, cluster graph, or a split graph after deleting a small set of vertices, called the Modulator. We prove that MSVC is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized jointly by the cluster modulator size and the maximum clique size in the remaining cluster graph, while allowing arbitrarily many cliques. For the clique modulator parameterization, we present a combinatorial algorithm that avoids the integer quadratic programming used in prior work [Aute, Panolan, Theoretical Computer Science, 2025]. We also introduce a vertex-weighted formulation of MSVC and obtain an XP algorithm parameterized by the clique modulator size. Using this algorithm as a subroutine, we develop an XP algorithm parameterized by the split modulator size. These results extend the known structural parameterizations of MSVC and highlight weighted MSVC as a promising direction for further research.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Appears in the Proceedings of the 52nd International Conference on Current Trends in Theory and Practice of Computer Science (Sofsem 2027)

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A latent index $J\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ is drawn from a prior $π$. Conditional on $J=j$, a gambler observes random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ drawn independently from a non-negative component distribution $F_j$. The gambler knows $n$, the prior $π$, and the component distributions $F_1,\ldots,F_k$, but not $J$, observes the values sequentially, and selects at most one value at the time it is revealed. We show that the largest $α$ such that the gambler can guarantee to select a value of $α\cdot\mathbb{E}[\max_iX_i]$ in expectation, for all distributions where this expectation is finite, is \[
  α=\frac1e+\frac{1}{k^{2/3+o(1)}}. \] The lower bound is achieved by the better of two variants of the standard secretary rule. The upper bound uses a finely tuned instance of the common-scale model, which scales a sequence of independent random variables by a single latent variable.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Policy Iteration Is Not Polynomial for Deterministic Markov Decision Processes: The Price of Algorithmic Anarchy
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We establish exponential iteration lower bounds in the number of states for Howard's policy iteration on deterministic discounted and average-reward Markov decision processes (MDPs), with a constant number of actions per state. This rules out polynomial-time complexity of Howard's policy iteration in both settings. We further prove that a Dantzig counterpart of Howard's policy iteration runs in strongly polynomial time on deterministic average-reward MDPs. Together with the known strongly polynomial bound for Dantzig's rule on deterministic discounted MDPs, these results establish an exponential separation between the two algorithms in both settings. This separation between Howard's decentralized and simultaneous selfish improvements and Dantzig's coordinated selection of a single action with the largest improvement across all states reveals a "price" of algorithmic anarchy.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Local-Counting Approach for Distributed Induced Path Detection
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
A well-known application of the celebrated color-coding technique is fast detection of paths in a distributed setting with limited bandwidth, by propagating a signal along colorful paths [Even et al., DISC 2017]. However, since vertices of the same color are indistinguishable by this procedure, it cannot detect induced paths, as they appear the same as cycles.
  We make the following observation. If, for a given edge, we \emph{count} the number of such signals over all permutations of the random coloring that terminate at that edge, then we can separate an induced path from a cycle: an induced path contributes one to that count, while a cycle contributes two. Refining and generalizing this observation gives our \emph{local-counting approach}, which allows us to separate induced paths from any other subgraph.
  We establish the following end results, all improving upon the state of the art in their round complexities and refined detection variants.
  * An $O(1)$-round algorithm for induced $P_4$ detection.
  * $O(Δ)$-round algorithms for detection of induced $P_5$ and $P_6$.
  * An $\tilde{O}(n^{1/3})$-round algorithm for detection of induced $P_5$ in induced-$C_4$ free graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Tropical and maximum colorful matchings in vertex-colored graphs
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: A subgraph of a vertex-colored graph istropical if it contains every color. We study matchings by the number of colors they cover. A matching is maximum colorful if no matching covers more colors. When a tropical matching exists, the maximum colorful matchings are exactly the tropical matchings. We give polynomial-time algorithms for two problems: a maximum matching that covers the most colors, and a tropical matching with the fewest edges. Both algorithms rest on a counterpart of Berge's theorem: a matching is optimal if and only if it admits no tropical augmentation, or no tropical reduction. These are chains of alternating paths linked by relays, and each one is found by a single augmenting-path search in an auxiliary graph. The same tools give a maximum colorful matching with the fewest edges, and show that all maximum matchings that are maximum colorful are connected by flips. Finally, the sets of colors that a matching can cover form a matroid. The greedy algorithm then computes a matching of maximum color weight. This paper extends the conference version and the PhD thesis of one of the authors.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Concavity of cardinality-constrained interval stabbing and interval cover problems
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: We consider the cardinality-constrained interval stabbing problem, in which the goal is to maximize the total weight of intervals hit by at least one of at most $k$ selected points. Although this problem does not admit a simple greedy solution, we show that its optimal value is a concave function of $k$. We establish this result using a linear programming formulation whose relaxation always admits an optimal solution with integer values. This allows us to prove concavity for the original problem. We further extend the result to the related interval cover problem. These concavity properties provide a basis for applying Lagrangian optimization using algorithms for the corresponding unconstrained problems.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source-destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---long a central open problem in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $Θ(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $$O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right),$$ where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $Θ\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean 4. Our reduction is independent of the address-field interchange construction. Using the one from recent work on multitape integer multiplication gives the bound for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, with an $\varepsilon$-dependent constant.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 45 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. New in v4: Appendix E extends the sorting bound to every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Lean 4 code: https://github.com/rtyu-1/coded-sorting-lean

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Near-Tight Robust Coresets for Clustering in Euclidean Spaces
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
This paper considers coresets for the robust $(k,z)$-clustering problem with $m$ outliers in Euclidean spaces. A robust coreset is a weighted subset of the data that, for every set of $k$ centers and every outlier budget $0\leq b\leq m$, approximates the clustering cost with $b$ outliers removed to within relative error $ε$. For every constant $z\geq 1$, we prove that the optimal worst-case size of such coresets over all ambient dimensions is \[
  Θ(m) + \widetildeΘ_z(\min\{kε^{-(z+2)}, k^{2(z+1)/(z+2)}ε^{-2} + km^{z/(z+2)}ε^{-4/(z+2)}\}), \qquad 1\leq z \leq 2, \] \[
  Θ(m) + \widetildeΘ_z(\min\{kε^{-(z+2)}, k^{2(z+1)/(z+2)}ε^{-2} + k \min\{m, \sqrt{m}ε^{-z/2}\} \}), \qquad z > 2. \]

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Directed $k$-Disjoint Shortest Paths in Polynomial Time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: The $k$-Disjoint Shortest Paths problem asks for pairwise vertex-disjoint shortest paths connecting $k$ prescribed terminal pairs in a graph with positive edge weights. Eilam-Tzoreff [DAM 1998] asked whether it is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed $k$. Lochet [SODA 2021] answered this for undirected graphs, while for directed graphs it has remained open for every $k\ge3$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for directed graphs and every fixed $k$, resolving this open problem for all graphs.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Almost Tight Hardness of Approximation for $0$-Extension
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
In the $0$-Extension problem, we are given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with non-negative edge weights $w: E\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, a collection $T \subseteq V$ of $k$ terminals, and a metric $D$ over terminals $T$. The goal is to find a retraction $f:V\rightarrow T$ that maps every terminal to itself, while minimizing the sum over all edges of the product of the edge's weight and the distance in $D$ between the terminals to which its endpoints are assigned, i.e.,
  \[
  \sum_{\{u,v\}\in E} w_{\{u,v\}} \cdot D(f(u), f(v)).
  \]
  Fakcharoenphol, Harrelson, Rao, and Talwar achieve the best known approximation ratio of $O(\log k / \log \log k)$, while the known approximation hardness is $Ω(\sqrt{\log k})$ assuming the unique games conjecture.
  In this work, we establish an $Ω(\log^{1-\varepsilon}k)$ hardness of approximation for every constant $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and arbitrarily large fixed $k$, almost matching the upper bound in the exponent of $\log k$. The main technical contribution is an $Ω(\log^{1-\varepsilon}k)$ integrality gap for the earthmover relaxation. Our construction is inspired by randomized extensions of expanders introduced by Schwartz and Tur for the metric relaxation. The result then follows from an existing theorem by Manokaran, Naor, Raghavendra, and Schwartz that translates the integrality gap for the earthmover relaxation to the approximation hardness for every fixed $k$.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Computing EF1 Allocations under Budget Constraints in Polynomial Time
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the allocation of indivisible goods to agents with budgets and additive valuations. Each agent compares its bundle with every budget-feasible subset of another agent's bundle or of the unallocated goods. We give a strongly polynomial algorithm for computing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good (EF1), even when agents have different valuations and budgets. Deciding whether a given allocation satisfies EF1 is coNP-complete. Equivalently, deciding whether it violates EF1 is NP-complete. When all agents have the same valuation, we can compute an EF1 allocation with welfare at least $(1/2-\varepsilon)$ times the maximum feasible welfare in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$, for any $0<\varepsilon<1/2$.
  Finding an allocation that is envy-free up to any good (EFX) is NP-hard even for one agent. We give polynomial-time EFX algorithms when each agent values goods in proportion to their sizes or when the number of distinct positive item values per agent is bounded by a constant.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: Added a proof that finding an EFX allocation is NP-hard

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Space Complexity Dichotomies for Subgraph Finding Problems in the Streaming Model
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We study the space complexity of four variants of the standard subgraph finding problem in the streaming model. Specifically, given an $n$-vertex input graph and a fixed pattern graph on at least three vertices, we consider two settings: undirected simple graphs, denoted by $G$ and $H$, and oriented graphs, denoted by $\vec{G}$ and $\vec{H}$. Depending on the setting, the task is to decide whether $G$ contains $H$ as a subgraph or as an induced subgraph, or whether $\vec{G}$ contains $\vec{H}$ as a subgraph or as an induced subgraph. Let $\textsc{Sub}(H)$, $\textsc{IndSub}(H)$, $\textsc{Sub}(\vec{H})$, and $\textsc{IndSub}(\vec{H})$ denote these four variants, respectively.
  An oriented graph is well-oriented if it admits a bipartition in which every arc is oriented from the same part to the other, and a vertex is internal if both its in-degree and out-degree are non-zero. For each variant, we obtain a complete dichotomy theorem, briefly summarized as follows. \begin{itemize} \item $\textsc{Sub}(H)$ can be solved by an $\tilde{O}(1)$-pass $n^{2-Ω(1)}$-space algorithm if and only if $H$ is bipartite. \item $\textsc{IndSub}(H)$ can be solved by an $\tilde{O}(1)$-pass $n^{2-Ω(1)}$-space algorithm if and only if $H$ is $P_3$, $P_4$, or $\mbox{co-}P_3$. \item $\textsc{Sub}(\vec{H})$ can be solved by a deterministic single-pass $n^{2-Ω(1)}$-space algorithm if and only if every connected component of $\vec H$ is either a well-oriented bipartite graph or a tree containing at most one internal vertex. \item $\textsc{IndSub}(\vec{H})$ can be solved by an $\tilde{O}(1)$-pass $n^{2-Ω(1)}$-space algorithm if and only if the underlying undirected simple graph $H$ is a $\mbox{co-}P_3$. \end{itemize} All our upper bounds are attained by deterministic algorithms that find a copy, whereas all our lower bounds hold even for randomized algorithms that only detect one.S
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 55 pages, 8 figures. v2: substantially revised, with corrections and a reorganized presentation

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for ARRIVAL
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In ARRIVAL, a token moves through a directed graph from a specified starting vertex, alternating between the two outgoing arcs of each vertex on successive departures. The problem asks whether the token ever reaches a given destination. Although the walk can be exponentially long, we give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, resolving an open problem. We first average the local routing rules and then restore the original rules on selected periods. The number of refinement rounds is at most the number of nonterminal vertices. The algorithm extends to explicitly given cyclic successor lists. It also computes exact departure counts when every nonterminal vertex has a path to an absorbing terminal and recovers the configuration of the walk at any binary-encoded time.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Toggle Tree: A New Data Structure for Efficient Parallel Graph Processing
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
We present the Toggle Tree, a parallel data structure for frontier-based graph algorithms. A Toggle Tree is used to represent a subset of vertices using hierarchical bit vectors, enabling efficient parallel updates, traversal, and set-wise reductions without global packing. It provides an IndexSet interface that unifies a wide range of parallel graph algorithms under a common abstraction of frontiers and active sets, and an IndexMap interface that also incorporates priority-queue semantics. Specifically, the Toggle Tree aims to combine the advantages of traditional sparse and dense frontier representations, offering both provable theoretical guarantees and high efficiency in practice.
  Using Toggle Trees, we implement five fundamental graph algorithms, including breadth-first search (BFS), k-core, degree-based graph coloring, single-source shortest paths using Bellman-Ford, and weighted-BFS (wBFS). Across a diverse set of large real-world graphs and the five graph problems, our implementations outperform state-of-the-art baselines, including GBBS and PASGAL, achieving substantial speedups. Our code is publicly available.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. To appear in PPoPP 2027. Code: https://github.com/ucrparlay/toggle-tree

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for TSP and More
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a canonical NP-hard optimization problem. For general edge weights, the classical dynamic programs of Bellman and of Held and Karp solve TSP on $n$ cities in $O^*(2^n)$ time. To date, no $\Oh(c^n)$-time classical algorithm is known for any $c<2$. Combining Grover search with the dynamic programming technique, Ambainis et al. (SODA 2019) introduced a quantum algorithm with running time $O^*(1.7274^n)$, which is still the best known quantum time bound.
  In this work, we improve the running time to $O^*(1.70961^n)$. The core idea of our algorithm is to combine the framework of Ambainis et al. with the extremal set-system framework, which was recently used for classical space-time tradeoffs of TSP by Jabal Ameli, Nederlof and Wang (FOCS 2026) and Dallant and Kozma (FOCS 2026). To obtain our upper bound, we decompose the optimal tour into four consecutive subpaths of different sizes, for which, based on the idea of set-systems, the optimal values are computed using dynamic programming with small success probability and use amplitude amplification. Using the same idea, we also give a new quantum space-time tradeoff for TSP, improving the previous results of Caroppo et al. (ESA 2026) and Dallant (arXiv:2607.12374). Finally, we obtain the same quantum upper bounds for several other related problems.

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Dynamic Tensor Product Regression
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: In this work, we initiate the study of Dynamic Tensor Product Regression. One has matrices $A_1\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times d_1},\ldots,A_q\in \mathbb{R}^{n_q\times d_q}$ and a label vector $b\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\ldots n_q}$, and the goal is to solve the regression problem with the design matrix $A$ being the tensor product of the matrices $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_q$ i.e. $\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\ldots d_q}} \|(A_1\otimes \ldots\otimes A_q)x-b\|_2$. At each time step, one matrix $A_i$ receives a sparse change, and the goal is to maintain a sketch of the tensor product $A_1\otimes\ldots \otimes A_q$ so that the regression solution can be updated quickly. Recomputing the solution from scratch for each round is very slow and so it is important to develop algorithms which can quickly update the solution with the new design matrix. Our main result is a dynamic tree data structure where any update to a single matrix can be propagated quickly throughout the tree. We show that our data structure can be used to solve dynamic versions of not only Tensor Product Regression, but also Tensor Product Spline regression (which is a generalization of ridge regression) and for maintaining Low Rank Approximations for the tensor product.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: NeurIPS 2022. Corrections: input-sparsity updates need CountSketch leaves (OSNAP multiplies nnz by sparsity). Main bounds assume oblivious updates. Adaptively, path refresh keeps the tree and low rank approximation valid with a larger sketch, regression gets $\sqrt{1+ε}{\rm OPT}+ξ$ via private medians, and query refresh covers splines. Fixed: [DJSSW19] comparison, spline sketch size

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: SAT-Driven Exact Treewidth via Safe Separators and Structure-Aware Encodings
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary: Treewidth is a standard measure of graph structure, but computing it exactly is NP-hard. SAT- and MaxSAT-based approaches provide a uniform way to solve treewidth by encoding it in conjunctive normal form and delegating the search to modern Boolean solvers, thus directly benefiting from continued progress in SAT technology. This report studies how to strengthen such SAT-driven solvers with structural reasoning and low-overhead guidance, both at the meta-algorithmic level and within the encoding itself. Starting from a baseline SAT/MaxSAT formulation, we investigate structure-based simplifications that reduce solver effort while preserving exactness, and we evaluate practical heuristic enhancements (fast upper/lower bounds and solver guidance) within iterative SAT and MaxSAT workflows. Experiments show consistent speedups on instances with exploitable structure, and clarify where SAT-based approaches remain limited.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 22 pages, 16 figures

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Online Network Design with Batch Processing
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
An online service chooses which waiting jobs to start together. Each finishes after its own processing time, and the longest determines the next possible launch. We charge network cost plus either total flow or the sum of per-batch maximum flows. For TCP acknowledgment with a fixed fee per launch, the optimal deterministic total-flow ratio is \(1+ρ\), where \(ρ\) is the processing-time spread. For batch maxima, a union of intervals on the release-time axis gives the exact offline cost when batches may overlap. It yields an offline \(2\)-approximation and pays for an online timer of ratio five. The optimal deterministic ratio is two at equal lengths and lies in \([2+2\sqrt2,5]\) at unrestricted spread.
  How often can later batches incur the same blocking delay? Rooted purchases can be combined, giving a polynomial-time \(3+2\sqrt2\) guarantee for batch maxima on undirected Steiner networks. A mobile server can concatenate walks in order, transferring an instantaneous maximum-wait ratio \(α\) to a batch-maximum flow ratio \(3α+6\). With \(k\) ephemeral facilities sharing one processor and one site per launch, separate openings can each incur the wait. The optimal deterministic batch-maximum ratio is then \(Θ(k)\) at unrestricted spread. The upper bound uses exact assignments, computable in polynomial time for fixed \(k\).

Data Structures and Algorithms.title: Node Differential Privacy via Node-Stable Graph Projections
Data Structures and Algorithms.summary:
Node-differentially private algorithms enable learning on network-structured datasets in which records reflect interactions among individuals. They protect the privacy of each individual's information, including all their associated records. A key challenge in the design of such algorithms is to exploit the structure of realistic graphs---where most nodes have low degree---to achieve high accuracy, without compromising on the worst-case privacy guarantee.
  In this work we give two new tools for designing accurate, computationally efficient node-differentially private algorithms. First, we give a nearly linear time, randomized, node-stable graph projection: the projection leaves graphs of maximum degree $D$ unchanged, maps arbitrary graphs to subgraphs of maximum degree $\hat D \approx D$, and ensures that changing one node of the input graph has only a small effect on the distribution of the edges selected among the remaining vertices. Unlike prior approaches, which abstain when the input violates the degree bound, our projection acts as degree clipping: even when $D$ is set well below the true maximum degree (trading truncation bias at high-degree outliers for lower privacy noise), it retains at least as many edges as a maximal $D$-bounded subgraph.
  Second, for graphs with bounded edge weights, we give a deterministic nearly linear time Lipschitz extension for the total edge weight that agrees with the original sum on graphs of maximum degree $D$ yet is $D$-Lipschitz on all graphs.
  Finally, we show how to apply these methods to design node-private algorithms for high-dimensional vector summation and gradient descent on datasets where records are associated with graph edges, such as email threads.
Data Structures and Algorithms.comment: 41 pages

Signal Processing.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
Signal Processing.summary: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

Signal Processing.title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
Signal Processing.summary: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last $m$ observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly $1/2$. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most $\bar P(m)+\bar s(m-1)/2$, where $\bar P(m)$ is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and $\bar s$ the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly $1/2$, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor $p_{\min}^{m-1}$. For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of $σ^2/Δ^2$, depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is $\bar s\log(1/\bar s)/(2I)(1+o(1))$, with $I$ the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most $2\log2\approx1.39$, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with $\pm1$ steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.
Signal Processing.comment: 29 pages, 8 figures. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24532266

Signal Processing.title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
Signal Processing.summary: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.

Signal Processing.title: On the Distance Properties of Huffman Sequences
Signal Processing.summary: In this letter, we study pairwise distances between sequences with a common aperiodic autocorrelation function. First, we show that pairwise distances are determined by a ternary signed pattern encoding the relative zero flips between spectral factors. Then, for Huffman sequences, we prove that Dihedral symmetries of the zeros preserve pairwise distances, and we further derive lower bounds on the minimum distance. The results in this letter offer a starting point for designing codes with a fixed autocorrelation. These codes are relevant in integrated sensing and communication.
Signal Processing.comment: This work has been accepted to IEEE Signal Processing Letters

Signal Processing.title: Unsupervised Detection of Underground Tunnels in Ground-Penetrating Radar Using Depth-Restricted Reconstruction Scoring
Signal Processing.summary: Hand-dug tunnels that reach buried pipelines from below are hard to find before they are used, and too rare to train a supervised detector. The engineering application of this work is detecting such tunnels in ground-penetrating radar surveys of a monitored site. The contribution in artificial intelligence is a detection scheme that needs no tunnel examples: a convolutional autoencoder learns the site's normal ground from surveys recorded before any tunnel exists, later survey windows are scored by their largest reconstruction errors within the travel-time band where a tunnel can lie, and evaluation holds out whole survey lines. On field data from a tunnel hand-dug for this study (0.6 m wide, 1 m high, roof 0.9-1.4 m deep) and surveyed repeatedly with a 250-megahertz radar in dry and wet conditions, the detector reaches an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.994 and an F1 score of 0.972 on 1,600 test windows and flags all 29 tunnel crossings. Restricting the score to the depth band improves all six detectors tested and, with a quarter of the training data, outperforms whole-window scoring trained on all of it; the best rule for the same band without learning misses 9 of the 29 crossings. On two unseen plots, false alarms stay at 1.6% on comparable ground but reach 9.3% on irrigated soil; recalibrating the threshold on a fifth of that plot's lines lowers them to 4.2%, retraining brings no significant further reduction, and models trained there alone still detect the original tunnel.
Signal Processing.comment: 32 pages, 8 figures, 12 tables. Substantially revised version, prepared for submission to Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence. Data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/muhammadjunaid007/gpr-normal-and-tunnel-anomaly-dataset ; code: https://github.com/Codingcahesession/gpr-tunnel-detection

Signal Processing.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
Signal Processing.summary: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.

Signal Processing.title: Device-Referred Channel Sounding With Commodity Wi-Fi Receivers: Error Budget and Body-Worn Measurements at 5 and 6 GHz
Signal Processing.summary: A wireless product experiences the channel through its own antennas and, when worn, its user's body. Commodity Wi-Fi receivers report channel state information (CSI) per frame and can serve as device-referred sounders if their impairments are corrected. Synthetic ground truth reproducing a commercial receiver's impairments shows that five corrections are needed: subcarrier mapping, receive-chain order, per-packet alignment, received-signal-strength referencing, and window-response removal. Without them, the RMS delay spread reads up to 191% high, the coherence bandwidth falls to about half, or the Rician $K$-factor and Doppler estimates lose their meaning; with all five, the median delay-spread bias is between $-6\%$ and $+14\%$. Applied to beacons from seven access points, including a body-worn receiver at six indoor sites at 5 and 6 GHz, the chain gives delay spreads of 24-96 ns; walking lowers the median correlation over one beacon interval from 0.85 to 0.15, near the estimator's floor. Unprecoded data frames gave 0.2-1.2 times the beacons' delay spread on the same channel, so the two should not be pooled.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation (Communication). Companion letter submitted to IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters

Signal Processing.title: AutoRSP: An AI Agent for Radar Sensing Pipeline Design
Signal Processing.summary: Radar sensing demands a pipeline that is well-thought-out across hardware and software. We ask whether an AI agent can automatically design radar sensing pipelines at a fraction of the time, cost, and expertise that current practice needs. We present AutoRSP, an agent that embeds radar-system-level structure through sub-agents mapped to five stack layers, a code-based representation of every layer with explicitly modeled cross-layer dependencies. Feedback for the agentic search process comes from a pipeline of realistic RF simulation, on-sensor emulation, and execution on real edge devices, rather than from an LLM judge. Because such feedback can be slower than an LLM call, we present methods to efficiently optimize agentic loops. We evaluate AutoRSP on robotic imaging, automotive perception, and vital sign sensing. It produces executable pipelines with performance comparable to or better than human-expert pipelines and closed-source agents. AutoRSP's harness, tools, and benchmarks will be released to bridge the rising gap in agentic research abilities outside of frontier labs.

Signal Processing.title: On the Relation of Characteristic Modes of Different Conducting Structures
Signal Processing.summary: A formalism is derived to analyze the scattering of a conducting structure based on the characteristic modes of another structure whose surface is a superset of the first structure. This enables the analysis and comparison of different structures using a common basis of characteristic modes. Additionally, it is shown that the scattering matrices and perturbation matrices are no longer diagonal in these cases. Based on this, a modal transformation matrix is defined to describe the mapping between the characteristic fields and the weighting coefficients of the two structures. This matrix enables the conversion of the perturbation matrices in different bases. Finally, three examples are provided along with a discussion of some aspects of the theory. The first two examples aim to validate and illustrate the formalism. The third example shows how the formalism can be applied in the design process of an antenna element that is gradually modified, starting from a base structure.

Signal Processing.title: First Order Real Resonant Digital Filters and A Novel Orthogonal State Generator
Signal Processing.summary: We describe FOREST, a real, first order digital resonant filter and orthogonal state generator. We show that in spite of the imaginary nature of the roots of the transfer function of a resonator, appropriate interpretation of this transfer function nonetheless leads to a practical first order filter with real coefficients. We use a discrete state space model of FOREST to predict the resonator properties, and implement the filter in digital signal processing slices on a digital signal processing platform. Applications are in real time digital signal processing, engineering fields such as mains electricity monitoring and motor control, any application requiring a phase locked loop, and physics applications utilising high-quality-factor resonators.
Signal Processing.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures

Signal Processing.title: Doppler RaDAR Single-Frame Anomaly Detection and Consistency Assessment by Velocity-Conditioned Gaussian Spectral Modeling
Signal Processing.summary: Reliable speed-over-ground estimation is essential for automated railway vehicles. However, the accuracy of a velocity estimate alone does not indicate whether the underlying RaDAR measurement is physically plausible. This paper introduces a velocity-conditioned Gaussian spectral modeling framework for anomaly detection and velocity consistency assessment. A neural encoder estimates the vehicle velocity from complex Doppler spectra, while a Gaussian decoder models the expected spectral distribution conditioned on a velocity estimate. Three complementary inference-time online indicators are derived: the spectral anomaly score (SAS), conditional anomaly score (CAS), and absolute velocity disagreement (AVD). Experiments demonstrate the sensitivity of the scores to velocity deviations. Under controlled spectral anomalies, SAS and CAS outperform conventional spectral indicators in most conditions. Furthermore, AVD exhibits strong correlations with actual velocity estimation errors (Pearson $r>0.99$) for the investigated extra-peak and local anomalies. These results demonstrate the potential of online conditional spectral modeling to assess measurement plausibility and velocity estimation reliability without requiring ground-truth velocities during inference.

Signal Processing.title: Conditional Independence Graph Learning from Dependent Data Via Time-Delay Embedding
Signal Processing.summary: We consider the problem of inferring the conditional independence graph (CIG) of a high-dimensional stationary multivariate Gaussian time series which could be short-range dependent (SRD) or long-range dependent (LRD). In a time series graph, each component of the vector series is represented by a distinct node, and associations between components are represented by edges between the corresponding nodes. We consider a time-domain approach based on time-delay embedding, casting the problem as one of multi-attribute graph estimation for random vectors where a vector is associated with each node of the graph. For an embedding dimension $d$, at each node the associated $(d+1)$-dimensional random vector consists of a time series component and its $d$ delayed copies, with integer delays up to $d \ge 1$. Graph estimation from dependent data has been investigated in the past using frequency-domain methods whose analysis is restricted to SRD data. We consider a penalized negative pseudo log-likelihood function with convex lasso or non-convex regularizations to estimate the CIG. Non-convex regularization functions are log-sum, smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) and minimax concave penalty (MCP). We exploit an existing alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) approach to optimize the objective function. We establish sufficient conditions in a high-dimensional setting for consistency, local convexity when using non-convex penalties, and graph recovery, for both SRD and LRD series. We illustrate our approach with both synthetic and real-data examples. For a $p$-dimensional time series, the computational complexity of the ADMM algorithm is ${\cal O}((d+1)^3 p^3)$. Based on the numerical examples, a heuristic is suggested and illustrated for selection of $d$ which, in theory, should tend to infinity to infer the time series graph.
Signal Processing.comment: 26 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables

Signal Processing.title: From Very Fine Vertical Resolution to Range Super-Resolution on BIOMASS P-BAND SAR Data
Signal Processing.summary: This paper demonstrates range super-resolution over arid regions using SAR tomography data with very fine vertical resolution from the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission. As the first civilian spaceborne P-band SAR mission, BIOMASS is operating with a bandwidth limited to 6~MHz by International Telecommunication Union regulations, yielding a native slant-range resolution of approximately 25 m. The large spatial baseline data acquired during the commissioning phase in July and August 2025 provide a valuable opportunity to enhance range resolution based on the InSAR wavenumber shift principle. According to this principle, a wider effective bandwidth can be synthesized by combining complementary sub-bands of the ground reflectivity spectrum sampled across acquisitions at different look angles. Unlike existing literature, this paper offers a novel interpretation of this problem from the perspective of SAR tomography. Furthermore, the proposed method also accounts for residual topography errors. The range resolution enhancement performance is validated using all 20 available acquisitions from the July-August 2025 commissioning phase over Lop Nur, China, and Wadi al-Hayat, Libya, achieving spatial detail comparable to optical satellite imagery in a grid finer than 2 m. Furthermore, the reconstructed range spectrum of the central Libyan oasis exhibits an effective bandwidth exceeding 70 MHz. The point spread function (PSF) of a point like target in the scene demonstrates a slant-range resolution finer than 2.1 m, representing more than a twelvefold improvement over the native resolution.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 7 figures. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Signal Processing.title: A Real-Time Low-Cost Platform for Non-Contact Respiratory Rate Monitoring: A Comparative Evaluation of RGB Optical Flow and Time-of-Flight Depth Sensing
Signal Processing.summary: Respiratory rate (RR) is one of the earliest indicators of clinical deterioration, which makes its continuous measurement clinically valuable. In routine practice, however, RR is monitored almost exclusively with contact-based sensors, which require skin attachment, may alter natural breathing, and are poorly tolerated by vulnerable groups such as newborns and elderly patients. Non-contact sensing removes these constraints, with RGB video and depth imaging among its most accessible modalities. In this work, we present a low-cost, real-time platform based on a single multimodal sensor that provides both RGB and time-of-flight (ToF) data streams, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device. The system integrates three RGB optical-flow pipelines, namely Farnebäck, Horn--Schunck, and Lucas--Kanade, together with a depth-based pipeline incorporating region-of-interest stabilization and distance-derived signal extraction, enabling the two modalities to be evaluated independently under the same experimental protocol. The proposed approach was evaluated on twelve healthy volunteers following a controlled protocol, including normal breathing, hyperventilation, and breath-holding, using a piezoresistive respiratory belt as a reference. RGB-based methods achieved lower RR estimation errors, with Lucas--Kanade attaining the lowest median MAE (3.83 BPM), whereas the ToF-based pipeline, although less accurate for RR estimation (median MAE 6.24 BPM), reached a higher apnea detection sensitivity (0.66 vs 0.51-0.55). These findings highlight the complementary strengths of both modalities and support their integration into unified low-cost platforms.

Signal Processing.title: Fast Fluid Antenna Multiple Access: Exact Analysis and Fixed-Aperture Asymptotics
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we investigate the interference-limited outage performance of fast fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA), in which the receive port is selected according to the instantaneous symbol-based signal-to-interference energy ratio. For any positive-definite spatial covariance matrix and an arbitrary finite number of candidate ports, we show that constant-modulus multiuser interference admits an exact reduction to the comparison of two independent correlated exponential random vectors. This representation leads to a nonnegative double multi-index series for the outage probability, a recursive coefficient evaluation, and a certified truncation-error bound. We then study the distinct asymptotic regime where the number of candidate ports goes to infinity while the physical aperture remains unchanged, assuming exponential spatial correlation. For this model, we derive an explicit finite-port series requiring no numerical integration, and characterize continuous port selection through a convergent one-dimensional series for arbitrary thresholds. The analysis further yields an exact expression relating the maximum supportable number of users to the antenna aperture size and target outage probability. Numerical results validate the finite-port and asymptotic analyses, and illustrate that given sufficient aperture size, a user utilizing fast FAMA can overcome a massive number of interferers for decent communication performance.

Signal Processing.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures

Signal Processing.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing Time
Signal Processing.summary: Multi-threshold sampling encodes signals through crossing times at prescribed thresholds, offering an alternative to uniform time-domain sampling. Its potential to reduce hardware requirements and power consumption motivates its use in high-speed pulse acquisition, including scintillation detector readout. We model the relation between signal statistics and recorded-crossing statistics by composing measurable stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators. The threshold noise processes are independent across thresholds. The sampler applies independent timing jitter at each analog crossing before quantization and enforces dead time separately at each threshold in the recording window. We express the joint cumulative distribution function of first recorded crossing times using path infima and suprema when crossings at each threshold share the same timing jitter. Specializing this formula to a single threshold gives the marginal distribution, from which we obtain the conditional standard deviation. We use these formulas to approximate the corresponding exact quantities under independent timing jitter at each crossing and bound each approximation error. In a scintillation example, the shared-jitter formulas and independent-jitter waveform simulations agreed within Monte Carlo sampling uncertainty for the joint and marginal distributions and for the conditional standard deviation. Engineers can use these results to choose thresholds and assess how sampler changes affect timing precision.

Signal Processing.title: Distortion-Corrected Diffusion MRI Using Rotated-View EPI and Joint Field-Map/Image Estimation with Gaussian Primitives
Signal Processing.summary: Echo planar imaging (EPI) is the standard acquisition technique for diffusion and functional neuroimaging, enabling rapid imaging but suffering from geometric distortions caused by B0 field inhomogeneities. Existing correction methods first reconstruct distorted images using parallel imaging, then estimate the B0 field and correct the distortion in the image domain. In this sequential process, reconstruction artifacts at high acceleration factors and low SNR at high diffusion b-values degrade B0 estimation and limit the overall correction quality. We propose a physics-informed framework that jointly estimates the B0 field, the distortion-free image, and the shot-to-shot phase directly from k-space data, without depending on an intermediate parallel-imaging reconstruction. All three are represented as superpositions of Gaussian primitives embedded within an EPI forward model; the explicit, continuous parameterization captures both smooth regions and tissue boundaries and is evaluated on rotated sampling grids without resampling. The diffusion-weighted image is modeled as real and non-negative, with the image phase absorbed into a per-shot phase factor. Acquiring the blip-up/blip-down data at several phase-encoding orientations, the rotated-view principle of PROPELLER applied to full-FOV single-shot EPI, distributes distortions across orientations, improving point spread function isotropy and providing stronger constraints for B0 estimation. On in vivo brain diffusion EPI at R=4 and 5, the proposed method attains the closest brain-boundary agreement with a distortion-free structural reference, with the largest improvement over sequential methods at high b-value.

Signal Processing.title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
Signal Processing.summary: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.
Signal Processing.comment: Papers submitted for journal consideration in September 2026

Signal Processing.title: Exact Error Analysis of Noise-Domain OTFS with Paired Covariance Signaling
Signal Processing.summary: Noise-domain orthogonal time frequency space (ND-OTFS) encodes bits through opposite correlations in Gaussian delay--Doppler pairs of equal average energy. This letter derives the exact conditional bit error probability (BEP) of maximum-likelihood detection using generalized covariance eigenvalues and characteristic-function inversion. For scalar channels, we obtain an incomplete-beta expression and its finite-sum Rayleigh average. Partial correlation yields an error floor for a fixed observation count. At unit correlation, the conditional BEP decays with an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exponent equal to the number of pair observations, and common Rayleigh fading yields diversity order one. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify pair-placement effects.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages

Signal Processing.title: Cross-Layer Design for Near-Field mmWave Beam Management and Scheduling under Delay-Sensitive Traffic
Signal Processing.summary: Next-generation wireless networks will rely on mmWave/sub-THz spectrum and extremely large antenna arrays (ELAAs). This will push their operation into the near field where far-field beam management degrades and beam training becomes more costly and must be done more frequently. Because ELAA training and data transmission consume energy and training trades off with service time, we pose a cross-layer control problem that couples PHY-layer beam management with MAC-layer service under delay-sensitive traffic. The controller decides when to retrain and how aggressively to train (pilot count and sparsity) while allocating transmit power, explicitly balancing pilot overhead, data-phase rate, and energy to reduce the queueing delay of MAC-layer frames/packets to be transmitted. We model the problem as a partially observable Markov decision process and solve it with deep reinforcement learning. In simulations with a realistic near-field channel and varying mobility and traffic load, the learned policy outperforms strong 5G-NR--style baselines at a comparable energy: it achieves 85.5% higher throughput than DFT sweeping and reduces the overflow rate by 78%. These results indicate a practical path to overhead-aware, traffic-adaptive near-field beam management with implications for emerging low-latency, high-rate next-generation applications such as digital twin, spatial computing, and immersive communication.
Signal Processing.comment: NeurIPS 2025 AI4NextG Workshop paper (non-archival). OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=ySE32cqT5D. Code: https://github.com/Zijun-Wang0823/cross-layer-near-field-beam-management. Metadata update only; manuscript unchanged

Signal Processing.title: Sparsity-Aware Near-Field Beam Training via Multi-Beam Combination
Signal Processing.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive near-field beam training method to enhance performance in multi-user and multipath environments. The approach identifies multiple strongest beams through beam sweeping and linearly combines their received signals - capturing both amplitude and phase - for improved channel estimation. Two codebooks are considered: the conventional DFT codebook and a near-field codebook that samples both angular and distance domains. As the near-field basis functions are generally non-orthogonal and often over-complete, we exploit sparsity in the solution using LASSO-based linear regression, which can also suppress noise. Simulation results show that the near-field codebook reduces feedback overhead by up to 95% compared to the DFT codebook. The proposed LASSO regression method also maintains robustness under varying noise levels, particularly in low SNR regions. Furthermore, an off-grid refinement scheme is introduced to enhance accuracy especially when the codebook sampling is coarse, improving reconstruction accuracy by 69.4%.
